Split_Squats: From a standing position, jump into a split stance with one foot forward and the other back, bending your knees and slightly lowering your hips.
Once lowered, immediately jump up and switch legs in midair. Perform 5–10 reps per leg.
Cat_Stretch: Get down on all fours, supporting yourself on your hands and knees.
Pull in your belly and round your back, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop down.
3_4_Sit-Up: Lie on the floor and secure your feet with your knees bent.
Place your hands behind your head or by your temples, keeping your back on the floor. This is your starting position.
Bending at your hips and spine, raise your torso toward your knees until it is perpendicular to the floor.
Lower yourself back down, but only three-quarters of the way.
Air_Bike: Lie on your back with your lower back pressed to the floor and your hands by your head. Lift your shoulders off the floor, just like in a crunch.
Raise your knees so your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and your shins are parallel to it. This is your starting position.
Slowly pedal your legs: extend your right leg forward while pulling your left knee in, and exhale as you twist your torso to bring your right elbow toward your left knee.
Inhale as you return, then exhale and twist to the other side, bringing your left elbow toward your right knee. Continue alternating sides.
Caution: Do not strain your neck.
Alternating_Cable_Shoulder_Press: Set the pulleys to the lowest position and select an appropriate weight.
Grasp the handles and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend your arm and press one handle straight overhead.
Pause at the top, return to the starting position, and repeat with the other arm.
Alternating_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.
Place one kettlebell on your chest, then the other, holding them by the handles with your palms facing forward.
Extend both arms, holding the kettlebells above your chest. Lower one kettlebell toward your chest, rotating your wrist toward the kettlebell on the extended arm.
Press the kettlebell back up and repeat with the other arm.
Alternating_Hang_Clean: Place two kettlebells between your feet. Hinge your hips back and look straight ahead. This is your starting position.
Clean one kettlebell to your chest while keeping the other in your lowered hand: extend your legs and hips to pull the kettlebell to your shoulder, rotating your wrist.
Lower the kettlebell back to a hang position and clean the other one to your chest. Continue alternating arms.
Alternating_Kettlebell_Press: Clean two kettlebells to your chest: extend your legs and hips to pull the kettlebells to your shoulders, rotating your wrists.
Press one kettlebell straight overhead by extending your elbow and turning your palm forward, keeping the other kettlebell stationary.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and immediately press with the other arm.
Anti-Gravity_Press: Place a barbell on the floor behind the head of an incline bench.
Lie face down on the bench and grasp the barbell from the floor with an overhand grip. Bend your elbows to pull the bar toward your chest. This is your starting position.
Press the barbell forward in front of your head by extending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the floor the entire time.
Return to the starting position and continue until the end of the set.
Arnold_Dumbbell_Press: Sit on a bench with back support and hold the dumbbells at upper chest level, palms facing you, with your elbows bent and tucked in—just like at the top of a bicep curl. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, press the dumbbells upward while rotating your palms forward until your arms are extended overhead.
After pausing for a second at the top, inhale and lower the dumbbells to the starting position, rotating your palms back toward you.
Tip: As you lower the weights, your left hand rotates counterclockwise and your right hand rotates clockwise.
Around_The_Worlds: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells in your hands with your palms facing the ceiling. Keep your arms parallel to the floor by your hips. This is your starting position.
Inhale and move the dumbbells in a semi-circle from your hips to behind your head. Keep your arms parallel to the floor throughout the movement.
Exhale and reverse the motion to return the dumbbells to the starting position.
Caution: Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid injury.
Back_Flyes_-_With_Bands: Loop the resistance band around a stationary anchor, such as a squat rack.
Grasp the handles and step back until there is tension in the band.
Extend your arms straight in front of you, parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso. Keep your feet planted shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull your straight arms out to the sides and back, keeping them parallel to the floor until they are aligned with your sides.
Pause, then inhale and return to the starting position.
Bent_Over_Dumbbell_Rear_Delt_Raise_With_: Stand upright holding dumbbells in your hands, with an incline bench placed in front of you.

Keeping a natural arch in your back, bend forward until your forehead touches the bench. Keep your torso parallel to the floor and let your arms hang straight down with palms facing each other. This is your starting position.
Without moving your torso, exhale and raise the dumbbells straight out to the sides with slightly bent arms until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Hold for a second at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Caution: Do not swing your torso or draw your arms backward—move them only out to the sides.
Bodyweight_Squat: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. You can place your hands behind your head. This is your starting position.
Begin the movement by bending your knees and hips, pushing your hips back.
Squat down to full depth if you can, then quickly return to the starting position. Keep your head and chest up, pushing your knees outward.
Incline_Push-Up: Face a bench or a sturdy elevated platform. Place your hands on the edge slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step your feet back, balancing on the balls of your feet; keep your arms and body straight, with your arms perpendicular to your body.
Keeping your body in a straight line, bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the edge of the platform.
Push your body back up until your arms are fully extended.
Bench_Dips: Place a bench behind you, perpendicular to your body. Facing away from it, place your hands shoulder-width apart on the edge with your arms straight.
Extend your legs forward, hinging at the hips so your legs are perpendicular to your torso. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself by bending your elbows until the angle in your elbows is slightly less than 90 degrees.
Use your triceps to press yourself back up to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your elbows as close together as possible, with your forearms pointing down at all times.
Dumbbell_Shoulder_Press: Sit on a bench with back support holding dumbbells, resting them vertically on your thighs.
Use your thighs to help hoist the dumbbells one by one to shoulder height, and turn your palms forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and press the dumbbells upward until they touch at the top.
After a brief pause at the top, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Single_Leg_Glute_Bridge: Lie on the floor with your feet flat and knees bent.
Lift one leg and pull the knee toward your chest. This is your starting position.
Driving through your planted heel, extend your hips upward to lift your glutes off the floor.
Raise your hips as high as you can, pause, and return to the starting position.
Butt_Lift_Bridge: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, knees bent, and feet about shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Driving mainly through your heels, exhale and lift your hips off the floor, keeping your back straight. Hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Seated_Leg_Curl: Adjust the machine lever to your height and sit with your back firmly against the backrest.

Place the backs of your lower legs on the padded lever just below your calves, and secure the thigh pad just above your knees. Grasp the side handles, keep your toes pointed straight, and extend your legs. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl your legs backward as far as possible toward the backs of your thighs. Keep your torso still. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Hanging_Leg_Raise: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms using a wide or medium grip. Keep your legs straight with your pelvis slightly tucked back. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your legs until your torso and legs form a 90-degree angle. Hold for about a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Bodyweight_Walking_Lunge: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips.
Step forward with one leg and bend your knees to lower your hips until your back knee almost touches the floor. Keep your torso upright and your front knee aligned over your foot.
Drive through the heel of your front foot, extend your knees, and stand up.
Step forward with your back leg and repeat the lunge on the opposite side.
Barbell_Hip_Thrust: Sit on the floor with your back against a bench and a barbell across your legs. A thick bar or a barbell pad will significantly reduce discomfort.
Roll the barbell over your hips and lean back against the bench so your shoulder blades rest against its edge.
Drive through your feet and thrust your hips up with the barbell. The weight should be supported by your shoulder blades and feet.
Lift as high as you can, then return to the starting position.
Superman: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your arms extended straight forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and simultaneously lift your arms, legs, and chest off the floor, holding for 2 seconds while engaging your lower back.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms, legs, and chest back to the starting position.
Glute_Kickback_Machine: Position yourself in the machine: rest your torso against the pad, hold the handles, and place your working leg on the platform or under the roller. Keep your supporting knee slightly bent and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your working leg back and up as high as comfortable, without arching your lower back.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position, resisting the weight. Once you finish the set, switch legs.
Tip: Squeeze your glute for a second at full extension.
Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a medium grip (elbows bent at about 90 degrees at the midpoint), unrack the barbell and hold it straight over your chest with locked arms. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar until it gently touches the middle of your chest.
After a brief pause, exhale and press the bar back up, driving with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, squeeze your chest for a second, and slowly lower again.
Once you finish, safely rack the barbell.
Tip: Ideally, lowering the bar should take about twice as long as pressing it up.
Standing_Dumbbell_Press: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Raise the dumbbells to head height, with your elbows out and bent at about 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Strictly, without using your legs or leaning back, press the dumbbells overhead together until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Leg_Press: Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform in front of you (you can also use a different foot stance).
Release the safety bars and press the platform until your legs are fully extended, without locking your knees. Your torso and legs should form a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the platform until your thighs and lower legs form a 90-degree angle.
Exhale and push back to the starting position, driving primarily through your heels and engaging your quads.
Caution: When you finish your set, securely lock the platform with the safety bars so it does not drop under the weight.
Barbell_Squat: For safety, perform this exercise in a power rack. Set the bar just below shoulder height, step underneath it, and rest the barbell across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck.

Hold the bar with both hands, push up with your legs, and straighten your torso to unrack it. Step back from the rack with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower down by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and head up, until the angle between your thighs and calves is slightly less than 90 degrees.
Exhale and rise back up to the starting position by driving through your heels and extending your legs.
Stiff-Legged_Dumbbell_Deadlift: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms straight. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart or narrower, knees slightly bent. This is your starting position.

Keeping your knees at that same slight bend, exhale and hinge forward at your hips with a flat back, lowering the dumbbells toward your feet as if picking something up off the floor, until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Inhale and extend your hips to return your torso to the starting position.
Pullups: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip at your preferred width: wide (wider than shoulders), medium (shoulder-width), or narrow (closer than shoulders).
Hanging with straight arms, lean your torso back about 30 degrees, create a slight arch in your lower back, and bring your chest forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up until the bar touches your upper chest, drawing your shoulders and elbows down and back.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly lower yourself until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
Tip: Squeeze your back muscles at the top. Keep your torso still—only your arms move, while your forearms simply grip the bar.
Seated_Cable_Rows: Attach a close-grip handle to a low pulley cable machine. Sit down and place your feet on the platform with your knees slightly bent.
Lean forward while maintaining the natural curve in your back and grab the handle.
With straight arms, lean back until your torso is perpendicular to your legs. Keep a slight arch in your lower back, chest lifted, and lats stretched. This is your starting position.

Keeping your torso still, exhale and pull the handle toward your abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your body. Squeeze your back muscles hard, hold for a second, and inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Lunges: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. This is your starting position.
Step forward with your right leg about 60 cm and lower your hips on an inhale, keeping your torso upright and maintaining your balance.
Exhale and push through your front heel to return to the starting position. Complete all reps on this side, then switch legs.
Tip: Keep your front shin nearly vertical.
Plank: Lie face down and prop yourself up on your toes and forearms. Keep your elbows bent directly beneath your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line and hold this position for as long as you can.
Variation: To make it more challenging, lift one arm or one leg off the floor.
Side_Lateral_Raise: Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand upright with your arms at your sides, palms facing in. This is your starting position.

Without swinging your torso, exhale and raise the dumbbells out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows, tilting your hands slightly forward as if pouring water. Lift until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause at the top for a second, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Pallof_Press: Attach a handle to a cable machine, ideally at shoulder height; if that is not available, a low pulley works too.
Stand sideways to the machine, grab the handle with both hands, and step away about an arm's length so the cable is under tension.
Set your feet hip-width apart, soften your knees, and hold the handle at the center of your chest. This is your starting position.
Press the handle straight out from your chest until your arms are fully extended, bracing your core. Hold for a few seconds, then return to the starting position.
Once you finish the set, turn around and repeat on the other side.
Face_Pull: Face a high cable pulley with a rope attachment or two handles.
Pull the weight directly toward your face, flaring your arms out to the sides. Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Bent_Over_Barbell_Row: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly bend your knees, and hinge forward at your hips with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Let the bar hang directly in front of you with your arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.

Keeping your torso still, exhale and row the bar toward your torso, keeping your elbows close to your body; use your forearms only to hold the weight. Squeeze your back muscles at the top and pause briefly.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Barbell_Ab_Rollout: Get into a push-up position, but instead of the floor, grip an Olympic barbell loaded with 2.5–5 kg plates on each side. This is your starting position.
Keeping a slight arch in your back, exhale, lift your hips, and roll the barbell toward your feet.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly roll the barbell forward back to the starting position.
Tip: lift your hips high, brace your core, and keep your arms perpendicular to the floor at all times—otherwise your shoulders and back will do the work instead of your abs.
Dumbbell_Bicep_Curl: Stand tall holding dumbbells at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate your palms forward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows stationary, exhale and curl the weights up while contracting your biceps until the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold at the top and squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Triceps_Pushdown: Attach a straight or angled bar to a high cable pulley and grab it with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Stand upright with a slight forward lean, tuck your elbows into your sides, and point your forearms up toward the pulley. This is your starting position.
Exhale and push the bar down using your triceps until it touches your thighs and your arms are fully extended. Keep your elbows tucked into your sides; only move your forearms.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly raise the bar back to the starting position.
Wide-Grip_Lat_Pulldown: Sit down at a lat pulldown machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pads to your height—they keep your body from lifting up with the weight.

Grip the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width. With your arms fully extended, lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back, and push your chest out. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the bar down until it touches your upper chest, drawing your shoulders and elbows down and back.
Hold for a second, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then inhale and slowly return the bar back up until your arms are fully extended and your lats feel stretched.
Tip: squeeze your back muscles at the bottom. Keep your torso still and move only your arms; avoid pulling with your forearms—they are only holding the bar.
Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Lie back on a flat bench with the dumbbells resting on your thighs, palms facing each other. Use your thighs to help hoist the dumbbells up one at a time and hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

Rotate your wrists so your palms face away from you. Position the dumbbells at the sides of your chest with your elbows at a 90-degree angle. Maintain full control of the weights at all times. This is your starting position.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up using your chest muscles. Extend your arms at the top, squeeze your chest, pause for a second, and slowly lower the weights down.
Tip: ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as lifting it.
Goblet_Squat: Stand holding a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest. This is your starting position.
Squat down between your legs until your hamstrings touch your calves. Keep your chest and head up, and your back straight.
Pause at the bottom and use your elbows to gently push your knees outward. Return to the starting position; complete 10–20 reps.
Close-Grip_Front_Lat_Pulldown: Sit down at a lat pulldown machine with a handle attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pads to your height—they keep your body from lifting up with the weight.

Grip the handle with an overhand grip narrower than shoulder-width. With your arms fully extended, lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back, and push your chest out. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the handle down until it touches your upper chest, drawing your shoulders and elbows down and back.
Hold for a second, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then inhale and slowly return the handle back up until your arms are fully extended and your lats feel stretched.
Tip: squeeze your back muscles at the bottom. Keep your torso still and move only your arms; avoid pulling with your forearms—they are only holding the handle.
Standing_Calf_Raises: Adjust the padded lever of the calf raise machine to fit your height. Place your shoulders under the pads and position the balls of your feet on the platform with your heels hanging off, toes pointing forward (or slightly inward or outward).
Push the lever up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is upright. Keep a slight bend in your knees without locking them. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves. Keep your knees stationary and do not bend them. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower your heels until you feel a stretch in your calves, returning to the starting position.
Barbell_Curl: Stand tall holding a barbell with a shoulder-width grip, palms facing forward and elbows tucked close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows stationary, exhale and curl the bar up while contracting your biceps until the barbell is at shoulder level. Move only your forearms.
Hold at the top for a second, squeezing your biceps hard.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Barbell_Full_Squat: For safety, perform this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar just above shoulder height, step underneath it, and rest the barbell across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck.

Grip the bar, unrack it by pushing through your legs and straightening your torso. Step back from the rack with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Keep your back straight and your head up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower down by bending your knees and sending your hips back, keeping your back straight and head up, until your hamstrings touch your calves.
Exhale and stand back up by driving through your heels or mid-foot, extending your knees and hips to return to the starting position.
Close-Grip_Barbell_Bench_Press: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a close grip (about shoulder-width apart), unrack the barbell and hold it straight above you with arms extended. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar until it touches the middle of your chest. Unlike a regular bench press, keep your elbows tucked close to your torso to emphasize your triceps.
Pause for a second, then exhale and press the bar back up using your triceps. Lock out your arms, hold for a second, and slowly lower again.
When you finish, re-rack the barbell.
Tip: Lowering the bar should take at least twice as long as pressing it up.
Incline_Dumbbell_Curl: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate your palms forward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows stationary, exhale and curl the weights up while contracting your biceps until the dumbbells reach shoulder level. Only your forearms should move. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
EZ-Bar_Skullcrusher: Grip an EZ-bar with a close grip and lie back on the bench, keeping your elbows tucked in. Hold the bar with your arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows stationary, inhale and lower the bar by bending your elbows. Pause once the bar is just above your forehead.
Exhale, extend your elbows, and return the bar to the starting position.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench angled at no more than 30 degrees. Extend your arms above you with a slight bend in your elbows.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face you, with your pinkies close together. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, rotating your wrists as you go. At the bottom, your arms are out at your sides with palms facing the ceiling.
Exhale and bring the dumbbells back to the starting position in reverse, rotating your wrists until your pinkies are close together again.
Tip: The movement should only occur at your shoulder and wrist joints, keeping your elbows fixed.
Lying_Leg_Curls: Adjust the machine lever to your height and lie face down so the padded lever rests on the back of your legs, just below your calves.
Keep your torso flat against the bench, fully extend your legs, and grab the side handles. Point your toes straight. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl your legs up as far as possible without lifting your thighs off the pad. Hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and lower your legs back to the starting position.
Tip: It is best to use an angled bench rather than a flat one, as it activates your hamstrings more effectively.
Incline_Dumbbell_Press: Lie back on an incline bench with the dumbbells resting on your thighs, palms facing each other. Use your thighs to help hoist the dumbbells up one at a time, holding them at shoulder width.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face away from you. This is your starting position.
Maintain full control of the dumbbells at all times. Exhale and press them up using your chest muscles. Lock out your arms at the top, hold for a second, and slowly lower them.
When finished, bring the dumbbells down to your thighs and then to the floor—this is the safest way to exit.
Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as pressing it up.
Seated_Palm-Up_Barbell_Wrist_Curl: Grab a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up) at shoulder width. Place your feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean forward and rest your forearms on your thighs with palms facing up, letting your wrists hang just over your knees. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the barbell as far as possible while maintaining a firm grip.
Exhale and curl the bar up as high as you can by bending your wrists, holding for a second at the top. Only your wrists should move.
Cable_Crunch: Kneel beneath a high pulley with a rope attachment. Grab the rope and pull it down until your hands are next to your face.
Hinge slightly at your hips and let the weight gently arch your lower back. This is your starting position.
Keeping your hips still, exhale and crunch down by contracting your abs, bringing your elbows toward the middle of your thighs. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your abs engaged throughout the entire movement, and avoid using too much weight so your lower back does not take over.
Dead_Bug: Lie on your back with your arms extended toward the ceiling. Raise your legs with your hips and knees bent at a 90-degree angle.

Exhale forcefully, drawing your ribs down and pressing your lower back into the floor, tuck your pelvis slightly, and squeeze your glutes. Maintain this brace throughout the exercise. This is your starting position.
Extend one leg straight out at the hip and knee, lowering it just above the floor. Keep your lower back and pelvis locked in place—your back will want to arch.
Keeping your core tight, return the leg to the starting position. Repeat with the other leg, alternating until the end of the set.
Triceps_Overhead_Extension_with_Rope: Attach a rope to a low pulley, select an appropriate weight, grab the rope with both hands, and turn to face away from the machine.
Bring your hands behind your head with elbows bent and pointing up. For stability, use a staggered stance and lean slightly forward away from the machine. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows stationary, extend your arms to press your hands overhead.
Squeeze your triceps at the top, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Push_Up_to_Side_Plank: Get into a plank position on your toes with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Perform a push-up by bending your elbows while keeping your body in a straight line.
As you push back up, shift your weight to your left side, rotate your body, and raise your right arm toward the ceiling into a side plank.
Return your hand to the floor, do another push-up, and rotate to the opposite side. Alternate sides for 10 or more reps.
Straight-Arm_Pulldown: Grasp a wide bar on a high pulley with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width apart, and step back about 60 cm.

Hinge your torso forward about 30 degrees with arms extended in front of you and elbows slightly bent (if your arms are not fully extended, step back a bit more). Engage your lats. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, exhale and pull the bar down using your lats until your hands reach your thighs.
Keeping your arms straight, inhale and return to the starting position.
Barbell_Deadlift: Stand in front of a loaded barbell.
Keeping your back as straight as possible, bend your knees, hinge forward, and grip the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip. This is your starting position.
Exhale and lift the barbell by driving through your legs while straightening your torso. At the top, bring your chest forward and pull your shoulder blades back like a soldier at attention.
Return to the starting position by bending your knees and hinging forward with a flat back until the plates touch the floor.
Tip: If you have trouble holding onto the bar, use a mixed grip or lifting straps.
Barbell_Guillotine_Bench_Press: Using a medium grip (creating a 90-degree angle at your elbows midway through the movement), unrack the barbell and hold it with straight arms over your neck. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell until it is about 2.5 cm (1 inch) from your neck.
After a one-second pause, exhale and press the barbell back up using your chest muscles. Extend your arms, squeeze your chest, pause for a second, and slowly lower it again.
Tip: Lowering the bar should take at least twice as long as pressing it up.
Barbell_Hack_Squat: Stand tall, holding a barbell behind you with straight arms and a shoulder-width grip, palms facing backward. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up and your back straight, inhale and slowly squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push back up, driving primarily through your heels and engaging your thighs.
Tip: You can use wrist straps for a more secure grip.
Barbell_Incline_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Gri: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium grip (creating a 90-degree angle at your elbows midway through the movement), unrack the barbell and hold it above you with straight arms. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell until it touches your upper chest.
After a one-second pause, exhale and press the barbell back up using your chest muscles. Extend your arms, squeeze your chest, pause for a second, and slowly lower it again.
Tip: Lowering the bar should take at least twice as long as pressing it up.
Barbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium grip (slightly wider than shoulder-width), unrack the barbell and hold it above you with straight arms. This is your starting position.
Without bending your arms, exhale and raise the barbell by bringing your shoulder blades forward and lifting your shoulders off the bench.
Inhale and return the barbell to the starting position.
Barbell_Lunge: For safety, perform this exercise inside a power rack. Set the bar just below shoulder height, step underneath it, and rest the barbell across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck.
Grip the bar with both hands, unrack it by pushing with your legs, and straighten your torso.
Step back from the rack, take a step forward with your right leg, and inhale as you lower into a lunge, keeping your torso upright and maintaining your balance.
Exhale, drive primarily through your front heel, and return to the starting position. Complete all reps, then switch to the left leg.
Barbell_Rear_Delt_Row: Stand upright, holding a barbell with a wide overhand grip (wider than shoulder-width).

Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward while maintaining a natural arch in your back, letting the barbell hang straight down. Once your torso is parallel to the floor, flare your elbows out to form a "T" shape.
Keeping your elbows flared out perpendicular to your torso, exhale and row the bar toward your upper chest, squeezing your rear delts.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: This movement is similar to an inverted bench press. Avoid pulling with your biceps—let your rear delts do the work, using your hands and arms merely as hooks.
Barbell_Rollout_from_Bench: Place a loaded barbell on the floor next to the edge of a bench. Kneel on the bench and grip the bar with a medium or narrow grip. This is your starting position.
Slowly roll the barbell forward by extending your hips, raising your arms so the bar moves out past your head. Keep your arms straight the entire time.
Once you have rolled the barbell out as far as possible, pull yourself back to the starting position.
Barbell_Shoulder_Press: Sit on a bench with back support inside a power rack. Set the barbell just above head level and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing forward).
Unrack the barbell and press it overhead with straight arms, positioning it slightly in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell down toward your shoulders.
Exhale and press the barbell back up to the starting position.
Barbell_Side_Split_Squat: Stand upright with a barbell resting across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck. Take a wide stance, turning the foot of your lead leg outward to the side. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower your body toward the turned-out foot by bending the knee and hip of your lead leg, keeping your other leg only slightly bent.
Exhale and return to the starting position by extending the hip and knee of your lead leg.
Complete all reps, then repeat on the other side.
Barbell_Step_Ups: Stand upright with a barbell across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck, behind an elevated platform (such as a spotter stand on a bench). This is your starting position.
Place your right foot firmly on the platform. Exhale and step up by extending the hip and knee of your right leg, driving primarily through your heel, and place your left foot next to it.
Inhale and step down with your left foot by bending the hip and knee of your right leg, then return your right foot to the floor next to your left.
Complete all reps leading with the right leg, then switch to the left leg.
Barbell_Walking_Lunge: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell resting across your upper back.
Take a step forward with one leg and bend both knees to lower your hips until your back knee is just above the floor. Keep your torso upright and your front knee aligned over your foot.
Drive through the heel of your front foot, extend your knees, and rise back up.
Step forward with your rear leg and repeat the lunge on the opposite side.
Bench_Press_-_With_Bands: Secure a resistance band under the leg at the head of a flat bench. Grab both handles and lie down on the bench.
Extend your arms, holding the handles in front of you shoulder-width apart with your palms facing away. This is your starting position.
Slowly lower the handles until your elbows reach a 90-degree angle. Keep the movement under control at all times.
Exhale and press the handles up using your chest muscles. Straighten your arms, squeeze your chest, pause for a second, and slowly lower back down.
Tip: Lowering should take at least twice as long as pressing.
Bent-Arm_Barbell_Pullover: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell with a shoulder-width grip.
Hold the barbell over your chest with your elbows slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Keeping the bend in your elbows, inhale and slowly lower the barbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring the barbell back along the same arc to the starting position, then hold for a second.
Bent-Arm_Dumbbell_Pullover: Stand a dumbbell upright on a flat bench.

Making sure the dumbbell is secure, lie perpendicular across the bench with only your shoulders resting on it. Keep your hips below the bench, knees bent, feet firmly on the floor, and head hanging off.
Grasp the dumbbell with both hands, resting your palms against the underside of the top plate, and hold it over your chest with elbows slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Keeping the bend in your elbows, inhale and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest. Exhale to bring it back along the same arc, and hold for a second.
Caution: Make sure the dumbbell is completely secure—if the plates are loose, it could come apart and fall on your face.
Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides.
Bend your knees to about 75 degrees and lift your feet about 2 inches (5 cm) off the floor.
Exhale and use your lower abs to draw your knees toward you, maintaining the 75-degree bend, until your hips lift off the floor. Your knees should end up over your chest.
Squeeze your abs at the top for a second, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Keep the movement under control at all times.
Bent_Over_One-Arm_Long_Bar_Row: Load weight plates onto one end of an Olympic barbell. Wedge the other end into a corner or secure it with a heavy object to keep it from sliding.

Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Grab the bar right behind the plates with one hand, resting the other on your knee. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the bar up, keeping your elbow close to your body, until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze your back muscles and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the bar until you feel a stretch in your lats, without letting the plates touch the floor. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
Tip: Do not swing your torso—only your arm should move. Use smaller plates instead of large ones for a greater range of motion.
Bent_Over_Two-Arm_Long_Bar_Row: Load weight plates onto one end of an Olympic barbell. Wedge the other end into a corner or secure it with a heavy object to keep it from sliding.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Grip the bar with both hands right behind the plates. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the bar up, keeping your elbows close to your body, until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze your back muscles and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the bar until you feel a stretch in your lats, without letting the plates touch the floor.
Tip: You can hook a single-handle stirrup or a close-grip V-handle under the bar. Use smaller plates instead of large ones for a greater range of motion.
Bent_Over_Two-Dumbbell_Row: Hold a pair of dumbbells with an overhand grip (palms facing you), soften your knees, and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Let the dumbbells hang directly in front of you with your arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.

Keeping your torso still, exhale and row the dumbbells up to your sides, keeping your elbows close to your body; your forearms should only hold the weight. Squeeze your back muscles at the top and pause for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Bent_Over_Two-Dumbbell_Row_With_Palms_In: Hold a pair of dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), soften your knees, and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Let the dumbbells hang directly in front of you with your arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso still, exhale and row the dumbbells up to your sides, pulling your shoulder blades together. Squeeze your back muscles at the top and pause for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Bottoms-Up_Clean_From_The_Hang_Position: Stand up straight holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Swing the kettlebell forcefully back between your legs, then drive it forward. Grip the handle as hard as you can and bring the kettlebell up to shoulder height, inverted.
Bottoms_Up: Lie on your back with your legs straight and arms by your sides. This is your starting position.
Draw your knees toward your chest by bending your hips and knees, then extend your legs straight up perpendicular to the floor. Roll your pelvis up and lift your glutes off the floor.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
Bradford_Rocky_Presses: Sit on a shoulder press bench with a barbell at shoulder level, using an overhand grip (palms facing forward) wider than shoulder width so your elbows form a 90-degree angle at the bottom. This is your starting position.
Unrack the barbell and press it overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell behind your head, then exhale and press it back up overhead.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell to the front starting position—this is one rep. Continue alternating in this manner for the rest of the set.
Butt-Ups: Get into a plank position on your forearms with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Round your back slightly upward rather than keeping it completely flat.
Exhale and lift your hips toward the ceiling, bracing your abs hard and drawing your ribs toward your pelvis to form a high arch.
Inhale and slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Tip: Do not let your back sag.
Dumbbell_Raise: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and stand straight with your back flat, arms at your sides, and elbows slightly bent. Keep the dumbbells next to your thighs with your palms facing backward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise the dumbbells out to your sides using your side delts until they are nearly level with your chin. Lead with your elbows, keeping them higher than your forearms at all times.
Pause at the top for a second while keeping your torso still. Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Rear_Lunge: Stand straight holding dumbbells at your sides with your arms extended. This is your starting position.
Inhale and step backward with your right leg about 2 feet (60 cm), lowering your hips while keeping your torso upright and maintaining balance.
Exhale, push through your feet, and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side.
Tip: A longer lunge places more emphasis on the glutes, while a shorter lunge targets the quads.
Tip: Pushing off the balls of your feet emphasizes the quads, while pushing through your heels targets the glutes.
Dumbbell_Squat: Stand straight holding dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing your thighs. Place your feet shoulder-width apart with your toes turned slightly out.
Keep your head up—looking down can throw off your balance—and maintain a straight back. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and slowly lower down, keeping an upright posture, until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Exhale and rise back up, pushing through the floor mainly with your heels, straightening your legs back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Squat_To_A_Bench: Stand straight with your back facing a flat bench, holding dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing your thighs. Place your feet shoulder-width apart with your toes turned slightly out.
Keep your head up—looking down can throw off your balance—and maintain a straight back. This is your starting position.
Inhale, bend your knees, and slowly lower down with an upright posture until you lightly touch the bench.
Exhale and stand back up, pushing through the floor mainly with your heels, straightening your legs back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Step_Ups: Stand straight holding dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing your thighs.
Place your right foot on an elevated platform. Exhale and step up by extending your right hip and knee, driving mostly through your heel, then place your left foot next to your right.
Inhale and step down with your left leg, bending your right hip and knee. Then return your right foot to the floor next to your left into the starting position.
Complete all reps on your right leg, then switch to your left.
Elbow_to_Knee: Lie on the floor, bend your left leg, and rest your right ankle on your left knee. Clasp your hands behind your head with your shoulder blades on the floor. This is your starting position.
Curl your spine and rotate your torso, bringing your left elbow toward your right knee.
Return to the starting position. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
Elevated_Back_Lunge: Set a barbell with an appropriate weight on a rack at shoulder height. Place a low platform behind you.
Rest the barbell across your upper back, keeping your back arched and tight. Step onto the platform with both feet. This is your starting position.
Step backward with one foot and lower down by bending your hips and knees until your back knee lightly touches the floor.
After a brief pause, extend your hips and knees to rise fully back to the starting position, then switch legs.
Elevated_Cable_Rows: Place a 4–6 inch (10–15 cm) platform (such as an aerobic step) on the seat of a seated cable row machine.
Sit down and place your feet on the front footrests with your knees slightly bent. Hinge forward while keeping the natural curve of your back and grip the V-bar handle.
With your arms extended, lean back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle with your legs. Keep a slight arch in your back, chest up, and lats stretched. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso stationary, exhale and pull the handle into your abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your body. Squeeze your back muscles hard.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Extended_Range_One-Arm_Kettlebell_Floor_: Lie on the floor and grab a kettlebell by the handle with one hand in a press position. Bend the leg on the pressing side and bring that knee across your body past the midline.
Press the kettlebell straight up by extending your elbow and bringing your arm toward the center. Return to the starting position.
External_Rotation_with_Band: Secure a resistance band to a rack at elbow height. Stand with your left side facing the anchor point, about 2 feet (60 cm) away.
Grasp the other end of the band with your right hand and tuck your elbow firmly against your side—it can help to place a rolled towel or pad between your elbow and torso.
Keep your upper arm still, elbow bent at 90 degrees, and hand in front of your stomach. This is your starting position.
Without moving your elbow, rotate your forearm outward as far as comfortable, as if hitting a backhand in tennis.
Pause briefly, then return to the starting position.
Flat_Bench_Leg_Pull-In: Lie on an exercise mat or a flat bench with your legs extending off the edge.
Place your palms down under your glutes or hold onto the sides of the bench (if on a mat, keep your hands palms down by your sides). Extend your legs. This is your starting position.
Exhale, bend your knees, and pull your thighs toward your abdomen until your knees reach your chest. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Flutter_Kicks: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at the edge, legs straight, and feet hovering off the floor. Grip the front edge of the bench with your hands.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings and raise your legs until they are level with your hips. This is your starting position.
Lift your left leg higher than your right, then lower your left leg while simultaneously raising your right.
Continue alternating legs in a controlled, flutter-kick swimming motion until you complete the target number of reps on each leg.
Tip: Breathe naturally and steadily throughout the movement.
Cable_Chest_Press: Select a weight, sit down, and grab the handles. Keep your arms flared about 45 degrees from your torso with elbows bent at about 90 degrees, head and chest up. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows to press the handles out in front of you, bringing them together. Keep your shoulder blades retracted.
Pause with your arms extended, then return to the starting position while keeping tension on the cables.
Variation: you can perform this without back support, at an incline or decline, or alternating arms.
Cable_Deadlifts: Set the pulleys to the lowest position, select an appropriate weight, and stand centered between the posts.
Squat down by bending at your hips and knees until you can reach the handles, then grip them.
Drive through your heels, extend your hips and knees, and stand up tall with your arms hanging at your sides, keeping your head and chest up throughout.
Once fully upright, return to the starting position and repeat.
Cable_Internal_Rotation: Sit sideways to a low pulley with your legs extended or crossed, and grab the single handle with the hand closest to the pulley.
Keep your elbow tucked against your side bent at 90 degrees, with your forearm pointing toward the pulley. This is your starting position.
Internally rotate your shoulder to pull the handle toward you in a semicircle until your forearm is across your stomach. Keep your forearm perpendicular to your torso throughout.
Slowly return to the starting position. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
Tip: if the pulley height is adjustable, sit on a flat bench.
Cable_Judo_Flip: Attach a rope to the low pulley. Stand sideways to the pulley with your feet wide, and grip the rope with both hands.
Pivot away from the pulley, bringing the rope over your shoulder as if performing a judo throw.
Twist and bend forward, shifting your weight from one foot to the other and pulling the cable downward.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the rest of the set, then switch sides and repeat.
Cable_Rope_Rear-Delt_Rows: Sit at a low pulley as you would for a seated row. Attach a rope and grab it with an overhand grip, arms extended parallel to the floor and elbows out.
Keep your lower back upright and slide your hips back so your knees are slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the rope toward your upper chest, just below your neck, keeping your elbows high and wide until they are slightly behind your back.
Inhale and return to the starting position, straightening your arms and letting your shoulders move forward.
Tip: keep your upper arms horizontal throughout the movement—perpendicular to your torso and parallel to the floor.
Cable_Russian_Twists: Attach a standard handle to the cable at medium height.
Lie back on an exercise ball perpendicular to the cable, about an arm's length away from the pulley so the cable is taut.
Grip the handle with both hands and extend your arms over your chest, keeping your wrists aligned with the pulley (adjust the pulley height if needed).
Keeping your hips lifted and core braced, rotate your torso a quarter turn away from the pulley. Keep your body straight from your head to your knees. Pause, then slowly return.
Maintain tension on the cable in the starting position. Repeat for the rest of the set, then switch sides.
Cable_Shoulder_Press: Set the pulleys to the lowest position and select an appropriate weight.
Stand centered between the posts, grab the handles, and hold them at shoulder height with your palms facing forward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend your arms and press the handles straight overhead.
Pause at the top, then return to the starting position.
Chair_Squat: Set the bar to your height. Step under the loaded barbell and rest it across the back of your shoulders.
Grip the bar with palms facing forward, unlock the safety catches, and lift the bar by straightening your legs.

Step your feet forward about 18 inches (45 cm) in front of the bar, shoulder-width apart, with toes pointed slightly outward. Look straight ahead with a neutral or slightly arched spine. This is your starting position.
Slowly lower yourself by bending your knees, keeping your back straight and head up, until your knees are bent past 90 degrees.
Exhale and push through your heels, extending your knees to return to the starting position.
Chin-Up: Grip the pull-up bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) narrower than shoulder-width.
Hanging with straight arms, keep your torso as straight as possible, slightly arch your lower back, and push your chest forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up until your head is roughly level with the bar, engaging your biceps and keeping your elbows close to your torso.
Squeeze your biceps for a second, then inhale and slowly lower yourself until your arms are fully extended.
Tip: keeping your torso upright places more emphasis on your biceps and less on your back. Only your arms should move; your forearms should just hold the bar.
Clean_and_Press: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. With a straight back, squat down and grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, knees inside your arms, and shoulders over the bar. This is your starting position.
Extend your knees to pull the bar up close to your body, raising your hips and shoulders at the same rate while maintaining your back angle.
As the bar clears your knees, explosively extend your ankles, knees, and hips as if jumping. Shrug your shoulders and pull the bar as high as possible with your elbows out.
At the top, drop under the bar, rotate your elbows forward beneath it, and catch the bar on your shoulders, absorbing the weight by bending your hips and knees. Stand up fully.
Without moving your feet, exhale and press the bar overhead, then lower it with control.
Clock_Push-Up: Get into a plank position on your hands and toes, arms extended shoulder-width apart. Keep your body straight throughout. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
At the bottom, explode upward by extending your arms to push off the floor, hopping 12–18 inches (30–45 cm) to the side.
As you push off, move your trailing leg away from the direction of travel and rotate your body about 30 degrees in the air.
Land in the starting position and continue until you complete a full circle back to where you started.
Close-Grip_Dumbbell_Press: Place a dumbbell vertically on a flat bench.
Making sure the dumbbell is stable, lie across the bench with only your shoulders supported. Keep your hips below the bench, knees bent, and feet firmly on the floor.
Grip the dumbbell with both hands, pressing your palms against the underside of the top plates, and hold it over your chest with arms extended. This is your starting position.
Lower the dumbbell toward your chest.
Extend your elbows to return to the starting position.
Decline_Smith_Press: Place a decline bench inside the Smith machine. Set the bar at a height you can reach with almost straight arms while lying down.
Unrack the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and hold it above you with straight arms. This is the starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar in a controlled motion by bending your elbows until it lightly touches your torso.
After a brief pause, exhale and press the bar back to the starting position by extending your elbows.
Once you finish the set, re-rack the bar securely.
Dip_Machine: Sit in the dip machine, select your weight, and firmly grip the handles.
Keep your elbows close to your sides to emphasize the triceps, bent at a 90-degree angle.
Exhale and straighten your arms downward, engaging your triceps.
Inhale and slowly let your arms return to the starting position.
Tip: keep a slight bend in your elbows at the bottom to maintain tension in the triceps.
Dips_-_Triceps_Version: Grip the parallel bars and support your body on nearly straight arms. This is the starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself down. Keep your torso upright and elbows close to your body to target the triceps. Lower until your elbows reach a 90-degree angle.
Exhale and push your body back up to the starting position using your triceps.
Double_Kettlebell_Alternating_Hang_Clean: Place two kettlebells between your feet. For the starting position, hinge your hips back and look straight ahead.
Clean one kettlebell up to your shoulder in the rack position, keeping the other one down.
Smoothly lower the upper kettlebell while simultaneously cleaning the lower one.
Double_Kettlebell_Jerk: Grasp a kettlebell by the handle in each hand.
Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending your hips and legs, rotating your wrists so your palms face forward. This is the starting position.
Dip down slightly by bending your knees while keeping your torso upright, then immediately drive through your heels as if jumping to create momentum.
Using this momentum, drive the kettlebells overhead to locked-out arms and drop into a split stance, with one foot forward and the other back.
Holding the kettlebells overhead, step your feet together and stand up straight. Lower the kettlebells to reset for the next rep.
Double_Kettlebell_Push_Press: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders into the rack position.
Dip slightly at the knees and quickly reverse the motion, using the drive from your legs to push the kettlebells overhead.
Lock out your arms at the top, lower the kettlebells back to your shoulders, and repeat.
Drag_Curl: Grip a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing forward), keep your elbows close to your torso, and pull them back slightly. This is the starting position.
Exhale and curl the bar upward by drawing your elbows back, dragging the bar straight up against your torso.
Slowly lower back to the starting position, keeping the bar in contact with your body the entire time.
Tip: do not pin your elbows to your sides; let them move backward. Avoid shrugging your shoulders.
Dumbbell_Bench_Press_with_Neutral_Grip: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie on a flat bench. Keep your feet flat on the floor and pull your shoulder blades together.
With a neutral grip (palms facing each other), extend your arms straight above you, perpendicular to the floor. This is the starting position.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells out to the sides until they are level with your chest.
Pause briefly, then press the dumbbells back up by extending your elbows to return to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Clean: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees, pushing your hips back to lower the dumbbells toward the floor. This is the starting position.
Explosively jump upward by extending your hips, knees, and ankles to accelerate the dumbbells. Keep a neutral grip and straight arms until full extension.
Immediately after full extension, bend your hips and knees to catch the weight in a squat, bending your arms and directing the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Once you catch the weight in the squat, extend your hips and knees to stand upright with the dumbbells on your shoulders.
Dumbbell_Incline_Row: Lie chest-down on an incline bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip and fully extended arms. This is the starting position.
Retract your shoulder blades and bend your elbows to pull the dumbbells toward your sides.
Hold for a moment at the top, then lower back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_One-Arm_Shoulder_Press: Pick up a dumbbell and sit on a bench with back support—resting the dumbbell upright on your thigh—or stand upright.
Bring the dumbbell up to shoulder height. Place your free hand on your hip, out to the side, or hold onto a support.
Rotate your wrist so your palm faces forward. This is the starting position.
Exhale and press the dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a second, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat on the other side.
Dumbbell_One-Arm_Upright_Row: Hold a dumbbell and stand tall with a flat back, arm extended in front of you and a slight bend in the elbow. Rest the dumbbell against your thigh with your palm facing in.
Place your free hand on your hip, hold it out to the side, or hold onto a support. This is the starting position.
Exhale and pull the dumbbell straight up close to your body toward chin level using your lateral deltoid. Lead with your elbow, keeping it higher than your forearm at all times.
Pause at the top for a second while keeping your torso steady. Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat on the other side.
Close-Grip_EZ-Bar_Press: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar with an appropriate weight.
Hold the bar with a close grip above your torso, elbows tucked in, and arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Exhale and press the bar back up using your triceps, extending your elbows.
Close-Grip_Push-Up_off_of_a_Dumbbell: Place your hands on a vertically positioned dumbbell on the floor. Balance on your toes and hands, keeping your body rigid, elbows close to your sides, and arms straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower yourself down by bending your elbows. Keep your body straight without letting your hips sag or rise.
Exhale, press yourself back up by extending your elbows, and pause at the top.
Cocoons: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead. This is your starting position.
Bring your knees toward your chest, tucking your pelvis and lifting your glutes off the floor. At the same time, crunch your torso forward, swinging your arms over your head toward your knees.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
Cross-Body_Crunch: Lie on your back with your knees bent at about a 60-degree angle. Keep your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting loosely behind your head. This is your starting position.
Exhale and crunch up, bringing your right elbow and shoulder across your torso while pulling your left knee inward. Aim to touch your elbow to your knee.
Inhale, return to the starting position, and repeat with your left elbow toward your right knee. Continue alternating sides.
Tip: Reach toward your knee with your shoulder, not just your elbow—the focus is on engaging your abs, not just moving your arm.
Cross_Over_-_With_Bands: Anchor a resistance band securely around a sturdy post.
Face away from the post, grab the handles, and take a step forward until the band is tense.
Extend your arms out to the sides parallel to the floor with palms facing forward and elbows slightly bent, forming a "T" shape with your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms fixed, exhale and bring them together in front of your chest in a wide arc, squeezing your pecs. Hold for one second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Cuban_Press: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells with an overhand grip. Raise your elbows out to shoulder height with your forearms hanging down, forming a scarecrow position. This is your starting position.
Without shifting your elbows, rotate your shoulders upward until your wrists are directly above your elbows and your forearms are perpendicular to the floor.
Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells straight overhead.
Inhale and reverse the motion step-by-step to return to the starting position.
Decline_Barbell_Bench_Press: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and slowly lie back.

Using a medium grip (where your elbows form a 90-degree angle at the midpoint), unrack the barbell and hold it directly above you with your arms straight and perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell until it touches your lower chest. After a one-second pause, exhale and press it back up using your pecs, squeeze your chest for a second, and then lower it again.
Once you finish, re-rack the barbell safely.
Tip: To protect your rotator cuff, have a spotter help you unrack the bar. Take at least twice as long to lower the barbell as you do to press it up.
Decline_Close-Grip_Bench_To_Skull_Crushe: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and slowly lie back. Unrack the barbell using a close grip (slightly narrower than shoulder-width) and hold it with arms extended and elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the barbell toward your lower chest while keeping your elbows close, then exhale and press it back up using your triceps.
Keeping your elbows fixed in place, inhale and slowly lower the barbell in an arc toward you by bending your elbows until the bar lightly touches your forehead.
Exhale and engage your triceps to press the barbell back to the starting position. Alternate between the press and the extension for the entire set.
Tip: To protect your rotator cuff, have a spotter help you unrack the bar.
Decline_Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and lie back with the dumbbells resting on your thighs, palms facing each other.
Once lying down, bring the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width and rotate your wrists so your palms face away from you. This is your starting position.
Slowly lower the dumbbells down to your sides with full control. Keep your forearms perpendicular to the floor throughout the movement.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up using your chest muscles. Straighten your arms, squeeze your pecs, hold for a second, and then slowly lower the weights.
Tip: Take at least twice as long to lower the weights as you do to press them up.
Decline_Dumbbell_Flyes: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and lie back with the dumbbells resting on your thighs, palms facing each other.
Once in position, raise the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width: palms facing each other, arms straight and perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce stress on your biceps tendons, and inhale as you open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a gentle stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms back along the same arc to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles. Hold for one second.
Tip: Keep the angle in your elbows unchanged throughout the movement; only your shoulder joints should be moving.
Decline_Oblique_Crunch: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and slowly lie back.
Raise your torso off the bench so it sits at about a 35–45 degree angle from the floor. Place one hand behind your head and the other on your thigh. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly curl your torso up while twisting to the left until your right elbow touches your left knee. Hold for one second.
Inhale and slowly lower back to the starting position. Complete the set, then switch sides.
Tip: Keep your abs tight, move with steady control, rotate your torso fully, and focus on the contraction at the top.
Decline_Reverse_Crunch: Lie on your back on a decline bench and grip the top of the bench with both hands to keep yourself from sliding down.
Use your abs to hold your legs parallel to the floor with your knees and feet together, legs extended with a slight bend in the knees. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull your legs toward your torso, curling your pelvis and lifting your hips off the bench until your knees touch your chest.
Hold for a second, then inhale as you return your legs to the starting position.
Freehand_Jump_Squat: Cross your arms over your chest. Keep your head up, back straight, and feet shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your back straight and chest up, inhale and squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower.
Exhale and jump as high as you can, pushing primarily off the balls of your feet and using your thighs like springs.
As you land, immediately drop back into a squat and jump again.
Front_Raise_And_Pullover: Lie flat on a bench, holding a barbell with an overhand grip about 15 inches (38 cm) wide.
Rest the barbell on your upper thighs and extend your arms, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. This is your starting position.

Inhale and lift the barbell with your arms extended in a semi-circular motion until it is behind your head (about 180 degrees). Your arms should be parallel to the floor with palms facing the ceiling.
Exhale and return the barbell along the same path back to the starting position.
Front_Squat_Clean_Grip: Set the barbell on a rack just below shoulder height. Rest the bar across your front deltoids near your collarbones, lightly touching your throat.
Hold the bar with a clean grip, touching it with your fingertips only. Unrack the bar by extending your legs and straightening your torso.
Step back from the rack and place your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Keep your head and elbows lifted at all times. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and squat down between your legs until your hamstrings touch your calves. Push your knees out in line with your toes.
Exhale and drive up through your heels or mid-foot, straightening your legs back to the starting position.
Front_Squats_With_Two_Kettlebells: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders by extending your hips and legs, pulling the weights up and rotating your wrists as you go.
Looking straight ahead, squat down as deep as you can and pause at the bottom. Push your knees out, sit between your legs, and keep your torso upright with your head and chest up.
Drive up through your heels to return to the top, and repeat.
Full_Range-Of-Motion_Lat_Pulldown: Standing or sitting on a high bench, grasp the handles of two high cable pulleys with crossed arms—each hand taking the opposite handle, palms facing forward.
Keeping your chest up and a slight arch in your lower back, pull the handles down in an arc, as you would in a regular lat pulldown.
Rotate your wrists as you pull down so that your palms face each other at the bottom. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
Glute_Kickback: Kneel on the floor or a mat and bend forward, placing your hands shoulder-width apart with arms straight. Look forward with your knees bent at 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Exhale and lift your right leg, keeping the 90-degree bend, until your thigh aligns with your back. Squeeze your glutes and hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and return to the starting position, then repeat with your left leg. Alternate legs for the rest of the set.
Tip: At the top of the movement, your thigh should be parallel to the floor and your shin perpendicular to it.
Gorilla_Chin_Crunch: Hang from a pull-up bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Bend your knees to 90 degrees so your shins are parallel to the floor and your thighs are perpendicular. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up while simultaneously driving your knees toward your chest. Stop when your nose is level with the bar—at this point, your crunch should also be complete.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Hack_Squat: Rest your back against the back pad and position your shoulders under the shoulder pads. Place your feet on the platform shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold the side handles and release the safety catches (usually by turning the handles outward). Straighten your legs without locking your knees. This is your starting position.
Inhale, bend your knees, and slowly lower yourself until the angle at your knees is just under 90 degrees. Keep your head up and your back pressed against the pad throughout.
Exhale and push through your heels to extend your legs back to the starting position.
Hammer_Grip_Incline_DB_Bench_Press: Lie back on an incline bench holding dumbbells on your thighs, palms facing each other. Use your thighs to help kick the dumbbells up to shoulder level one at a time.
Maintain a neutral grip. Bring your elbows out so your upper arms are perpendicular to your torso, with elbows bent at 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells to your sides with full control.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up using your chest muscles, extend your arms, hold for a second, and then lower them slowly—taking at least twice as long to lower as you did to press.
When finished, bring the dumbbells down to your thighs and then place them on the floor—this is the safest way to exit.
High_Cable_Curls: Stand between two high cable pulleys and take a handle in each hand. Extend your arms out to the sides with your upper arms parallel to the floor and palms facing you. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl your arms, pulling the handles toward your ears. Keep your upper arms stationary, moving only your forearms. Squeeze your biceps and pause for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Hip_Extension_with_Bands: Attach one end of the resistance band to the base of a post and the other end around your ankle.
Face the anchor point and hold onto the post for balance.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend your banded leg straight back as far as you can without bending your knee.
Return your leg to the starting position.
Hip_Flexion_with_Band: Attach one end of the resistance band to the base of a post and the other end around your ankle.
Stand with your back to the anchor point.
Keeping your head and chest up, raise your knee to a 90-degree angle and hold briefly.
Return your leg to the starting position.
Kettlebell_Arnold_Press: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending your hips and legs, keeping your palm facing inward.
Looking straight ahead, press the kettlebell overhead, rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward at the top.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with your palm facing inward.
Kettlebell_Dead_Clean: Place the kettlebell between your feet. Push your hips back and look straight ahead to set up.
Clean the kettlebell to shoulder height by extending your hips and legs, rotating your wrist along the way.
Lower the kettlebell back down, keeping your back straight and hips pushed back to maintain tension in your hamstrings.
Kettlebell_Hang_Clean: Place the kettlebell between your feet. Push your hips back and look straight ahead to set up.
Clean the kettlebell to shoulder height by extending your hips and legs, rotating your wrist along the way.
Lower the kettlebell to a hang between your legs, keeping tension in your hamstrings and your head held high throughout.
Kettlebell_One-Legged_Deadlift: Hold the kettlebell by the handle with one hand and stand on the leg on that same side.
Keeping a slight bend in your standing knee, hinge at the hips as in a stiff-legged deadlift, extending your free leg back for balance.
Lower the kettlebell until your torso is parallel to the floor, then return to an upright position.
Kettlebell_Pass_Between_The_Legs: Place the kettlebell between your feet and take a comfortable stance. Hinge forward by pushing your hips back and keeping your back flat.
Pick up the kettlebell and pass it between your legs to the other hand. Continue passing it back and forth.
Kettlebell_Pirate_Ships: Take a wide stance and hold the kettlebell with both hands. Keep your arms straight with the kettlebell hanging at waist level. This is your starting position.
Rotate to one side, swinging the kettlebell up to head level. Pause for a moment at the top.
Let the kettlebell swing back down as you rotate to the opposite side, lifting it up to head level once again.
Kettlebell_Seated_Press: Sit on the floor with your legs comfortably spread.
Bring the kettlebell up to your shoulder.
Press the kettlebell overhead until your arm is fully extended. Return to the starting position.
Kettlebell_Seesaw_Press: Clean two kettlebells up to your shoulders.
Lower it while immediately pressing the other kettlebell up. Complete an equal number of reps on each side.
Kettlebell_Sumo_High_Pull: Place the kettlebell between your feet, take a wide stance, and grab the handle with both hands. Push your hips back as far as possible with knees bent, keeping your chest and head up. This is your starting position.
Extend your hips and knees while simultaneously pulling the kettlebell toward your shoulders, leading with your elbows.
Reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
Kettlebell_Thruster: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders by extending your hips and legs, rotating your wrists along the way. This is your starting position.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to squat as deep as possible between your legs, keeping your back straight and upright.
At the bottom, reverse direction and stand up by driving through your heels and extending your knees and hips. Simultaneously press both kettlebells overhead, using the momentum of your drive.
Lower the kettlebells back to your shoulders as you begin the next rep.
Kettlebell_Turkish_Get-Up_Lunge_style: Lie flat on your back and press the kettlebell overhead, locking your elbow out. Bend the knee on the same side as the kettlebell.
Keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead, roll onto your opposite side and use your free hand to prop yourself up, transitioning toward a lunge position.
Push off your free hand into a seated position, then sweep your leg underneath into a half-kneeling position.
Keep your eyes on the kettlebell and slowly stand up. Reverse the steps to return to the starting position and repeat.
Kettlebell_Turkish_Get-Up_Squat_style: Lie flat on your back and press the kettlebell overhead, locking your elbow out. Bend the knee on the same side as the kettlebell.
