Keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead, roll onto your opposite side and use your free hand to prop yourself up, transitioning toward a lunge position.
Push off your free hand into a seated position, then shift your weight onto both feet into a squat.
Keep your eyes on the kettlebell and slowly stand up. Reverse the steps to return to the starting position and repeat.
Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextension_B: Have a partner hold your legs down and slide toward the edge of a flat bench so your hips are off the edge and your upper body hangs toward the floor.

Keeping your body straight, cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head. This is your starting position. For extra resistance, you can hold a weight plate under your crossed arms.
Inhale and slowly bend down with a flat back as far as you can—until you almost touch the floor or feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Exhale and slowly raise your torso back to the starting position.
Caution: never round your back, hyperextend past a straight line, or swing your torso to avoid back injury.
Incline_Cable_Chest_Press: Select the weight, sit down, and grasp the handles. Keep your upper arms at about a 45-degree angle to your torso, head and chest up, and elbows bent at roughly 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows to press the handles straight out in front of you, bringing them together. Keep your shoulder blades retracted.
After a brief pause at full extension, return to the starting position while keeping tension on the cables.
Incline_Dumbbell_Bench_With_Palms_Facing: Lie back on an incline bench holding dumbbells on your thighs with your palms facing each other. Use your thighs to help hoist the dumbbells up to shoulder level one at a time.
Maintain a neutral grip. Flare your elbows out with your upper arms perpendicular to your torso and elbows bent at 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells to your sides with complete control.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up using your chest, fully extend your arms, hold for a second, and slowly lower them again—taking at least twice as long to lower as to press.
When finished, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and then to the floor—this is the safest way.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes_-_With_A_Twist: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench set to no more than 30 degrees. Extend your arms above you with a slight bend in your elbows.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face you, with your pinkies close together. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides, rotating your wrists. At the bottom, your arms are out to your sides with palms facing the ceiling.
Exhale and reverse the movement to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your wrists so your pinkies are close together again.
Tip: move only at the shoulder and wrist joints, keeping the elbow angle fixed.
Incline_Push-Up_Close-Grip: Face a Smith machine bar or a sturdy elevated surface of suitable height and place your hands on the bar close together.
Step your feet back so your arms and body are straight. This is your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, bend your arms and lower your chest toward the bar.
Extend your elbows to press yourself back up to the starting position.
Incline_Push-Up_Medium: Face a Smith machine bar or a sturdy elevated surface of suitable height and place your hands on the bar about shoulder-width apart.
Step your feet back so your arms and body are straight. This is your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, bend your arms and lower your chest toward the bar.
Extend your elbows to press yourself back up to the starting position.
Incline_Push-Up_Reverse_Grip: Face a Smith machine bar or a sturdy elevated surface of suitable height and grasp the bar with a reverse grip (palms facing up) about shoulder-width apart.
Step your feet back so your arms and body are straight. This is your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, bend your arms and lower your chest toward the bar.
Extend your elbows to press yourself back up to the starting position.
Incline_Push-Up_Wide: Face a Smith machine bar or a sturdy elevated surface of suitable height and place your hands on the bar wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step your feet back so your arms and body are straight, with your arms perpendicular to your body. This is your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, bend your arms and lower your chest toward the bar.
Extend your elbows to press yourself back up to the starting position.
Isometric_Wipers: Get into a push-up position on your hands and toes with your body straight and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Shift your body weight as far as possible to one side, bending that elbow and lowering your body.
Extend your bent arm to push yourself back up and shift your weight to the other side.
JM_Press: Start as you would for a close-grip bench press: lie on a flat bench holding the barbell with straight arms and elbows tucked in. The bar should be directly over your upper chest. This is your starting position.

Inhale and lower the barbell as you would in a lying triceps extension. Halfway down, let the bar roll back about an inch (2.5 cm), shifting your upper arms toward your feet until they are perpendicular to your torso.
Exhale and press the bar up using your triceps, as in a close-grip press, returning to the starting position.
Tip: when shifting your upper arms forward, keep your elbow angle unchanged.
Jackknife_Sit-Up: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your arms extended overhead and legs straight. This is your starting position.

Exhale and fold at the waist, raising your arms and legs toward each other. Keep your legs straight at a 35–45 degree angle to the floor, arms parallel to them, and your upper body lifted off the floor.
Inhale and lower your arms and legs back to the starting position.
Jefferson_Squats: Place a barbell on the floor and stand over the center of the bar so it runs lengthwise between your feet.
Squat down with a straight back and take a neutral grip, with your right hand on the bar in front and your left hand in back. Keep both hands equidistant from your torso.
Stand up with the barbell: position your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned slightly out.
Inhale and squat down with a flat back until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your torso as upright as possible and your head up.
Push through your feet to return to the starting position. Keep your arms straight, acting only as hooks—lift the weight with your legs and hips, not your arms.
Kettlebell_Windmill: Place a kettlebell in front of your lead foot. Clean it to your chest with the opposite hand by extending your hips and legs and rotating your wrist palm forward.
Extend your elbow and press the kettlebell overhead.
Keeping the kettlebell locked out on a straight arm, turn your feet 45 degrees away from the loaded arm and shift your hips toward the kettlebell.
Hinge laterally at your hip, pushing your hips to the side, and slowly bend down until your free hand touches the floor. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell overhead the entire time.
Pause for a second at the floor, then reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
Kneeling_High_Pulley_Row: Set the weight on a high cable pulley and attach a rope. Kneel about 60 cm away from the pulley, holding the rope in front of you with straight arms. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull the rope toward your upper chest, flaring your elbows out and fully squeezing your shoulder blades together.
After a brief pause, slowly return to the starting position.
Kneeling_Single-Arm_High_Pulley_Row: Attach a single handle to a high cable pulley and select the weight.
Kneel in front of the pulley and grab the handle with one hand, arm fully extended. This is your starting position.
Starting with your palm facing forward, pull the handle toward your torso by bending your elbow and retracting your shoulder blade. Rotate your wrist as you pull so your palm faces you at the end.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
Landmine_180s: Insert one end of the barbell into a landmine base or securely anchor it in a corner. Load an appropriate weight.
Lift the free end of the barbell with both hands to shoulder height, keeping your arms extended in front of you. Take a wide stance. This is your starting position.
Rotate your torso and hips to swing the weight all the way down to one side. Keep your arms straight the entire time.
Reverse the motion and swing the weight all the way to the other side. Alternate sides until the end of the set.
Landmine_Linear_Jammer: Insert one end of the barbell into a landmine base or securely wedge it into a corner. Load an appropriate weight and attach a handle attachment to the barbell.
Lift the bar off the floor, bringing the handles up to your shoulders. This is your starting position.
In an athletic stance, squat down by bending your hips and sitting back while keeping your arms bent.
Powerfully extend your hips, knees, and ankles while simultaneously driving your arms straight. Explode out of the squat into full extension as explosively as possible.
Leg-Over_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell by the handle at your chest. Cross the leg of your working side over the other leg. You can extend your free arm out to the side for support.
Press the kettlebell up until your arm is fully extended.
Lower the kettlebell until your elbow touches the floor, keeping the weight stacked directly over your elbow.
Leg_Pull-In: Lie on a mat with your legs extended and your palms down beside your body or under your glutes. This is your starting position.
Exhale, bend your knees, and pull your thighs toward your belly until your knees are roughly chest-high. Squeeze your abs and hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and return to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your shins parallel to the floor the entire time.
Leverage_Chest_Press: Load an appropriate weight and adjust the seat to your height so that the handles align with your lower or mid-chest at the start.
Keep your chest lifted, head up, and shoulder blades pulled back. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows and press the handles forward.
After a brief pause at full extension, return the weight almost all the way to the starting position without resting it on the stops until your set is finished to maintain muscle tension.
Leverage_Deadlift: Load an appropriate weight and stand directly between the handles. Take a comfortable grip on the lower handles, inhale, and drop your hips. Look forward with your chest up. This is your starting position.
Return the weight to the starting position.
Leverage_Decline_Chest_Press: Load an appropriate weight and adjust the seat to your height so that the handles align with your lower chest at the start.
Keep your chest lifted, head up, and shoulder blades pulled back. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows and press the handles forward.
After a brief pause at full extension, return the weight almost all the way to the starting position without resting it on the stops until your set is finished to maintain muscle tension.
Leverage_High_Row: Load an appropriate weight and adjust the seat so you can just reach the handles overhead. Adjust the knee pad to hold your thighs down securely.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull the handles toward your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the bottom, then slowly return the handles to the starting position. Avoid letting the weight rest on the stops completely between reps to maintain muscle tension.
Leverage_Incline_Chest_Press: Load an appropriate weight and adjust the seat to your height so that the handles align with your upper chest at the start.
Keep your chest lifted, head up, and shoulder blades pulled back. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows and press the handles forward.
After a brief pause at full extension, return the weight almost all the way to the starting position without resting it on the stops until your set is finished to maintain muscle tension.
Leverage_Iso_Row: Load an appropriate weight and adjust the seat so the handles align with your chest. Grasp the handles with a neutral or overhand grip. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull the handles toward your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the peak and slowly return the handles to the starting position. Do not let the weight rest completely on the stops between reps to maintain muscle tension.
Leverage_Shoulder_Press: Load an appropriate weight and adjust the seat height so the handles align with the tops of your shoulders.
Keep your chest and head up, gripping the handles with an overhand grip. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows to press the handles overhead.
After a brief pause at the top, lower the weight almost back to the starting position, avoiding resting it on the stops until your set is finished to keep tension on the muscles.
Low_Pulley_Row_To_Neck: Sit at a low pulley cable station with a rope attachment. Grab the ends of the rope with an overhand grip, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Keep your torso nearly upright and your arms fully extended in front of you. This is your starting position.

Without moving your torso, exhale as you raise and bend your elbows, pulling the rope toward your neck. Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor, hands ending near your ears with elbows flared out wide.
Hold for about a second, then inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your torso completely still throughout the entire movement.
Lunge_Pass_Through: Stand upright holding a kettlebell in your right hand. This is your starting position.
Step forward with your left foot and lower your body by bending at your hips and knees, keeping your torso upright. Lower your back knee until it almost touches the floor.
At the bottom of the lunge, pass the kettlebell under your front leg into your other hand.
Push off your front heel to return to the starting position. Alternate legs.
Lunge_Sprint: Set the bar on a Smith machine to an appropriate height. Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders.
Unhook the bar and take a staggered stance with one foot forward and the other back. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and lower your hips until your back knee almost touches the floor.
Immediately reverse direction at the bottom by explosively pushing off your front heel, using your back leg for light support. Jump up and switch leg positions in the air.
Lying_Machine_Squat: Adjust the machine so you can get into it with your knees bent and thighs slightly below parallel.
Select your weight and lie face up in the machine with your back and head supported and shoulders under the pads. Your thighs should sit slightly below parallel to the platform.
Hold the handles, place your feet shoulder-width apart, and point your toes slightly outward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and push through the balls of your feet to fully extend your legs, squeezing your quads, and hold for a second. On the first rep, you can press your hands against your thighs for assistance.
Inhale and slowly lower down, stopping when your thighs are parallel to the platform with a 90-degree angle at your knees rather than returning all the way to the start.
Lying_T-Bar_Row: Load weight onto the chest-supported T-bar row machine and adjust the footplates (or step onto the correct tier) so the top of your chest rests at the edge of the pad.
Lie chest down on the pad and grip the handles with an overhand, underhand, or neutral grip, depending on which area of your back you want to emphasize.
Unrack the weight and extend your arms straight down. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you slowly row the weight up, keeping your elbows close to your torso, and squeeze your back muscles at the top. Keep your chest flat on the pad and avoid pulling with your biceps.
Hold the contraction at the top for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower back to the starting position.
Machine_Bench_Press: Sit in the chest press machine and select your weight.

Press the foot lever to bring the handles forward. Grip them with an overhand grip, lift your elbows so your upper arms are parallel to the floor, and extend your arms. This is your starting position.
Inhale as you bring the handles back toward your chest.
Exhale as you press the handles away, squeezing your chest muscles, and pause for a second.
Once finished, press the foot lever again and slowly guide the handles back.
Machine_Shoulder_Military_Press: Sit in the shoulder press machine and select your weight.
Grip the handles at your sides with your elbows bent and aligned with your torso. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you press the handles overhead until your arms are fully extended. Pause at the top for a second.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Monster_Walk: Place one resistance band around both ankles and another around both knees. The bands should be taut when your feet are shoulder-width apart.
Take short steps forward, alternating between your left and right legs.
After several steps, walk backward the same way to return to your starting position.
Narrow_Stance_Hack_Squats: Place your back firmly against the back pad and position your shoulders under the shoulder pads. Place your feet close together on the platform—about 8 cm or less apart—with toes pointing slightly outward.
Grasp the side handles and release the safety stops (usually by rotating the handles outward). Straighten your legs without locking your knees. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower down by bending your knees until the angle at your knees is slightly less than 90 degrees. Keep your head up and your back pressed firmly against the pad at all times.
Exhale and push through the platform mainly with your heels to return to the starting position.
Narrow_Stance_Leg_Press: Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet close together on the platform—about 8 cm or less apart—with your toes pointed slightly outward. Keep your head up and back flat against the pad.
Disengage the safety catches and press the platform until your legs are extended without locking your knees. Your torso and legs should form a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the platform until your knees reach a 90-degree angle.
Exhale and push primarily through your heels, engaging your quads, to return to the starting position.
Caution: When finished, securely lock the safety catches so the loaded platform does not slide down onto you.
Narrow_Stance_Squats: For safety, perform this exercise in a power rack. Set the barbell on the racks at shoulder level, load the weight, step under the bar, and place it across the back of your shoulders just below your neck.
Grip the bar with both hands and unrack it by extending your legs and straightening your torso.
Step back from the rack and place your feet in a narrow stance, about 8–15 cm apart, with your toes pointed slightly outward. Keep your head up and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale as you slowly lower down by bending your knees until the angle at your knees is slightly less than 90 degrees. Exhale and drive mainly through your heels to return to the starting position.
Natural_Glute_Ham_Raise: Kneel on the seat of a lat pulldown machine or preacher bench facing away from it, with your ankles secured under the roller pads. Keep your torso upright and your posture tall. This is your starting position.
Lower your body forward under control until your knees are almost fully extended.
Maintain control as you pull yourself back up to the starting position.
Tip: If you cannot complete a rep, assist yourself with a resistance band, a partner, or by pushing off a plyo box.
Neck_Press: Lie flat on a bench. Using a medium grip (where your elbows form a 90-degree angle halfway down), unrack the barbell and hold it directly over your neck with arms extended. This is your starting position.
Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell until you feel it lightly touch your neck.
After a one-second pause, exhale and press the barbell back up using your chest muscles. Lock out your arms at the top, squeeze your chest for a second, and slowly lower again.
Once finished, carefully return the barbell to the rack.
Tip: Lower the barbell at least twice as slowly as you press it.
One-Arm_Dumbbell_Row: Place dumbbells on both sides of a flat bench. Place your right knee on the edge of the bench, hinge forward until your torso is parallel to the floor, and support yourself with your right hand on the other end of the bench.
Pick up the dumbbell from the floor with your left hand, keeping your lower back straight and your palm facing your torso. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you row the dumbbell straight up to the side of your chest, keeping your upper arm close to your body and your torso still. Squeeze your back muscles at the top.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbell straight down to the starting position. Complete the set, then switch sides.
Tip: Pull with your back muscles rather than your arm; your forearm should only hold the dumbbell while your torso stays still.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean: Place a kettlebell between your feet. Hinge forward by pushing your hips back and look forward as you reach for the handle.
Clean the kettlebell up to your shoulder by extending your legs and hips, rotating your wrist as you pull.
Return the kettlebell to the starting position.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean_and_Jerk: Grasp the kettlebell by the handle. Clean it to your shoulder by extending your legs and hips, rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward.
Dip slightly by bending your knees while keeping your torso upright.
Immediately drive through your heels as if jumping, using the momentum to press the kettlebell overhead to a locked-out arm.
Receive the weight overhead by dropping into a shallow squat. Stand up tall while keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead.
Lower the kettlebell to the floor to begin the next rep.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell in one hand. Rest your upper arm on the floor with your palm facing inward.
Press the kettlebell straight up toward the ceiling, rotating your wrist as you push.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and repeat.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Jerk: Grasp the kettlebell by the handle and clean it to your shoulder by extending your legs and hips, rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Dip slightly by bending your knees while keeping your torso upright.

Immediately drive through your heels as if jumping, using the momentum to launch the kettlebell overhead to a locked-out arm. Catch the weight by dipping underneath it into a squat, then stand up while holding the kettlebell overhead.
Lower the kettlebell to prepare for the next rep.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Military_Press_To_The: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending your legs and hips, rotating your wrist so your palm faces inward. This is your starting position.
Looking at the kettlebell, press it up and slightly out to the side until your arm is fully locked out overhead.
Lower the kettlebell back to your shoulder under control and repeat.
Tip: For stability and strength, firmly engage your lats, glutes, and core.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Para_Press: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending your legs and hips, rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbow out to the side, press the kettlebell up and outward until your arm is fully extended overhead.
Lower the kettlebell back to your shoulder under control and repeat.
Tip: For stability and strength, firmly engage your lats, glutes, and core.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Push_Press: Grasp the kettlebell by the handle and clean it to your shoulder by extending your legs and hips, rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Dip slightly by bending your knees while keeping your torso upright.
Immediately drive through your heels as if jumping, using the momentum to press the kettlebell overhead to a locked-out arm. Lower the kettlebell to prepare for the next rep.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Row: Place the kettlebell in front of your feet. Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward, pushing your hips back as far as possible. This is your starting position.
Grasp the kettlebell and row it toward your stomach by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow. Keep your back straight.
See-Saw_Press_Alternating_Side_Press: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand up straight. Bring the dumbbells up to chest and shoulder height with your palms facing you, like in an Arnold press. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, press your left arm overhead while rotating your palm forward and flaring your elbows out. At the same time, lean your torso to the right.
Inhale at the top. Then, keeping the weight overhead on a straight arm while leaning right, begin the movement to the left side.
Tip: From the side, it should look like you are reaching with your left hand toward something overhead to your right.
Shotgun_Row: Attach a single handle to the low pulley cable.
Select your weight and take a step back into a wide split stance. Keep your arm extended and your shoulder stretched forward. This is your starting position.
Pull your shoulder back and bend your elbow, rotating your palm upward as you row.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
Shoulder_Press_-_With_Bands: Stand on the resistance band so that tension begins at arm's length. Grab the handles and bring them up to your shoulders at your sides.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward. Keep your elbows bent, with your upper arms and forearms aligned with your torso. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, press the handles overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Single-Arm_Linear_Jammer: Secure one end of the barbell in a landmine sleeve or firmly wedge it into a corner. Load an appropriate weight onto the other end.
Lift the bar from the floor to your shoulder using one or both hands. Set your feet wide. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbow and explosively press the bar upward, fully extending your hips and knees for maximum power.
Single-Arm_Push-Up: Lie face down on the floor and assume a plank position on your toes and one hand. Place your working arm straight, directly under your shoulder, with your legs straight and spread wider than in a standard push-up.
Maintain good posture and place your free hand behind your back. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbow and slowly lower your body until you touch the floor.
Extend your arm and push yourself back to the starting position.
Smith_Machine_Bench_Press: Place a flat bench inside the Smith machine and set the bar at a height reachable with almost fully extended arms while lying down. Load the weight and lie on the bench.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width, unhook it, and hold it above you with arms straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar to your mid-chest. Pause for a second, then exhale and press it back up using your pecs, lock out your arms, and hold for a second.
When finished, rack the bar back onto the hooks.
Tip: Lower the bar at least twice as slowly as you press it.
Smith_Machine_Bent_Over_Row: Set the Smith machine bar about two inches below your knees. Bend your knees slightly and hinge your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and unhook it so it hangs in front of you with straight arms. This is your starting position.

Keeping your torso stationary, exhale and row the bar up while keeping your elbows close to your body; your forearms should only support the weight. Squeeze your back muscles at the top and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Smith_Machine_Close-Grip_Bench_Press: Place a flat bench inside the Smith machine and set the bar at a height reachable with almost fully extended arms while lying down. Load the weight and lie on the bench.
Take a narrow overhand grip (about shoulder-width apart), unhook the bar, and hold it above you with straight arms. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar to your mid-chest. Pause for a second, then exhale and press it back up using your triceps, extend your arms, and hold for a second.
When finished, rack the bar back onto the hooks.
Tip: Unlike a standard bench press, keep your elbows close to your torso to engage your triceps more. Lower the bar at least twice as slowly as you press it.
Smith_Machine_Decline_Press: Position a decline bench inside the Smith machine so the bar aligns over your chest. Load an appropriate weight and lie on the bench.
Rotate the bar to unhook it and extend your arms. Keep a slight arch in your lower back with your shoulder blades retracted. This is your starting position.
Bend your arms and lower the bar toward your chest.
After a brief pause, extend your arms and press the weight back to the starting position.
Once you finish the set, rotate the bar to secure it on the hooks.
Smith_Machine_Hang_Power_Clean: Set the bar at knee height and load an appropriate weight. Grasp it with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and unhook it.
Keep your arms straight, head and chest up, elbows turned out, and shoulders pulled back and down. Hinge your hips back, loading your hamstrings. This is your starting position.
Powerfully extend your hips and knees to accelerate the bar. Keep your arms straight during this phase.
At full extension, drop down under the bar by bending your hips and knees. Flex your arms and swing your elbows around the bar to catch it on your shoulders.
Extend your hips and knees to stand up straight with the bar resting on your shoulders.
Smith_Machine_Incline_Bench_Press: Place an incline bench inside the Smith machine and set the bar at a height reachable with almost fully extended arms while lying down. Load the weight and position yourself so your upper chest is aligned under the bar.
Take an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width, unhook the bar, and hold it above you with arms straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar to your upper chest. Pause for a second, then exhale and press it back up using your pecs, extend your arms, and hold for a second.
When finished, rack the bar back onto the hooks.
Tip: Lower the bar at least twice as slowly as you press it.
Smith_Machine_Leg_Press: Set the Smith machine bar on the safety stoppers about two feet (60 cm) off the floor. Load an appropriate weight and lie down beneath the bar.
Place the arches of your feet against the bar, bringing your knees toward your chest. This is your starting position.
Press through your feet to push the bar upward, extending your hips and knees. Do not lock your knees out completely.
Pause briefly at the top, then return to the starting position.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Split_Jerk: Clean the kettlebell to shoulder height by extending your hips and legs, rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Dip down slightly by bending your knees while keeping your torso upright.
Immediately drive through your heels as if jumping, using momentum to press the kettlebell overhead to a straight arm.
Catch the weight overhead by dropping into a split stance, with one foot forward and the other back.
Keeping the kettlebell overhead, stand up and bring your feet together. Lower the kettlebell for the next rep.
One-Arm_Long_Bar_Row: Place one end of the barbell into a landmine attachment or secure it in a corner. Load an appropriate weight onto the free end.
Stand beside the barbell and grasp it with one hand near the sleeve. Stand up by extending your hips and legs.
Bend your knees and hinge at your hips with your chest up and arm straight. This is your starting position.
Pull the weight toward your side by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow. Avoid jerking the weight or swaying.
Pause briefly, then return to the starting position.
One-Arm_Open_Palm_Kettlebell_Clean: Place a kettlebell between your feet.
Grip the handle with one hand and pull the kettlebell up explosively, letting it flip so the ball rests in your open palm.
Push the kettlebell out in front of you and catch the handle with one hand.
Lower the kettlebell to the floor and repeat. Complete the reps on both arms.
One_Arm_Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Lie back on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in one hand on your thigh.
Use your thigh to help lift the dumbbell up to shoulder height, guiding it with your free hand. Turn your palm away from you. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell to your side with full control. Use your free hand only if needed for balance; otherwise, keep it at your side.
Exhale and press the dumbbell up using your chest muscles until your arm is extended, squeeze your chest, pause for a second, and lower it slowly again. Then switch arms.
Tip: Lower the dumbbell at least twice as slowly as you press it.
One_Arm_Floor_Press: Lie on your back on the floor or a mat with your knees bent.
Have a partner hand you the barbell in one hand. Keep your arm nearly straight, as in the start of a bench press, but with a neutral grip (palm facing your body). Rest your free arm along your side.
Inhale and lower the barbell until your elbow touches the floor.
Exhale and press the barbell back to the starting position. Complete the set and switch arms.
One_Arm_Lat_Pulldown: Set the weight and adjust the knee pad to secure you in place. Grasp the handle with an overhand grip. This is your starting position.
Pull the handle down by bending your elbow, keeping it close to your side.
Pause at the bottom and slowly return the handle to the starting position. Do not let the weight stack touch down between reps to maintain muscle tension.
Pallof_Press_With_Rotation: Attach a standard handle to the cable at shoulder height. Stand sideways to the machine, grab the handle with one hand, and step about an arm's length away to create tension on the cable.
Set your feet hip-width apart. Bring the handle to your chest and clasp it with both hands.
Looking straight ahead, press the handle away from your chest while bracing your core. Keeping your hips steady, rotate your torso a quarter turn away from the cable stack.
Maintaining a stable stance and straight arms, slowly return to the center. Bring your hands back to your chest and immediately extend them again — that is one rep.
Repeat for the rest of the set, then turn around and perform the movement on the other side.
Plie_Dumbbell_Squat: Hold a dumbbell with both hands by one end and stand upright. Place your feet wider than shoulder-width apart with knees slightly bent.
Turn your toes outward and keep your arms stationary throughout the exercise. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly bend your knees, lowering down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Exhale and drive mainly through your heels to return to the starting position.
Power_Clean: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out. Squat down and grip the bar with a pronated, closed grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, outside your knees, with your arms straight.
Position the bar about 1 in (2.5 cm) from your shins over the balls of your feet. Keep your back flat or slightly arched, chest up, shoulder blades retracted, head neutral, and eyes forward.

Exhale and lift the barbell off the floor by powerfully extending your hips and knees. Keep your torso angle constant without letting your hips rise faster than your shoulders. Keep the bar close to your shins with arms straight.

As the bar passes your knees, drive your hips forward, extend explosively onto your toes, and shrug your shoulders up with straight arms. Then pull with your elbows high and drop under the bar into a quarter squat.

Catch the bar on your clavicles and front deltoids with your elbows raised, core braced, and feet flat on the floor. Stand up fully, then lower the bar under control to your thighs and down to the floor.
Pull_Through: Stand facing away from a low pulley with a rope or handle attachment, about a meter out. Have the cable run between your legs with your feet wide.
Hinge at your hips and reach your hands through your legs as far back as comfortable, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Keeping your arms straight, extend your hips and stand up tall. Avoid pulling with your shoulders — the entire movement should come from your hips.
Push-Up_Wide: Get into a push-up position on your toes with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width. Keep your elbows extended, body straight, and hips level. This is your starting position.
Inhale, bend your elbows, and lower your chest toward the floor.
Exhale and press yourself back up to the starting position using your chest muscles, extending your elbows.
Pause at the top and repeat.
Push-Ups_-_Close_Triceps_Position: Lie facedown on the floor, place your hands narrower than shoulder-width apart, and push yourself up onto straight arms.
Inhale and lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Exhale and press back up to the starting position using your triceps and chest, squeezing your chest at the top.
Pause for a second at the top and repeat.
Push-Ups_With_Feet_Elevated: Lie face down on the floor, place your hands about 36 inches (90 cm) apart, and push up onto straight arms.
Place your toes on a flat bench. The higher the elevation, the harder the exercise.
Inhale and lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Exhale, push yourself back up to the starting position using your chest muscles, and squeeze your chest. Pause for a second and repeat.
Pushups: Lie face down on the floor, place your hands about 36 inches (90 cm) apart, and push up onto straight arms.
Inhale and lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Exhale and push yourself back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower yourself again.
Pushups_Close_and_Wide_Hand_Positions: Lie face down on the floor with your body straight, resting on your toes. Place your hands wider than shoulder-width for a wide grip or narrower for a close grip, holding your body up on straight arms.
Inhale and lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Exhale, push yourself back up to the starting position using your chest muscles, and squeeze your chest. Hold for a second at the top.
Reverse_Grip_Bent-Over_Rows: Stand straight, holding a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing up).

Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight. Let the barbell hang directly in front of you with straight arms. This is the starting position.
Keeping your torso still, exhale and row the barbell up, keeping your elbows close to your body; your forearms should only hold the weight. Squeeze your back muscles at the top and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Reverse_Triceps_Bench_Press: Lie on a flat bench. Using a shoulder-width reverse grip, unrack the barbell and hold it directly above you with straight arms. This is the starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell until it touches the middle of your chest.
After a one-second pause, exhale and press the bar back up using your triceps. Lock out your arms, hold for a second, and slowly lower it again.
Tip: Unlike a regular bench press, keep your elbows tucked close to your torso at all times to better engage your triceps. Take at least twice as long to lower the barbell as you do to lift it.
Romanian_Deadlift: Place a barbell on the floor in front of you and grab it with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Slightly bend your knees, keep your shins vertical, push your hips back, and keep your back straight. This is the starting position.
Keeping your back and arms straight, exhale and lift the barbell by driving your hips forward.
Once fully standing, lower the barbell by pushing your hips back with only a slight bend in the knees—not like in a squat.
Tip: Move smoothly and under control, keeping your chest up. Inhale at the start, hold your breath as you lower the weight, and exhale at the top. For heavy weights, wrist straps can be helpful.
Russian_Twist: Lie on the floor with your knees bent, anchoring your feet under something sturdy or having a partner hold them.
Raise your torso so it forms a V-shape angle with your thighs. Extend your arms straight out in front of you perpendicular to your torso, clasping your hands together. This is the starting position.
Exhale and twist your torso to the right until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Hold for a second and return to the starting position. Then repeat the movement to the other side.
Seated_Barbell_Military_Press: Sit on a press bench with the barbell racked behind your head. Grab it with an overhand grip or have a spotter help you unrack it to protect your shoulders.
Press the barbell overhead to straight arms and hold it slightly in front of your head. This is the starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell down to your collarbones.
Exhale and press the barbell back up to the starting position.
Tip: Use a grip wider than shoulder-width so your forearms and upper arms form a 90-degree angle at the bottom.
Seated_Cable_Shoulder_Press: Select an appropriate weight, sit down, and grab the handles. Keep your upper arms at a 90-degree angle to your torso, elbows bent at about 90 degrees, and chest and head up. This is the starting position.
Extend your elbows and press the handles upward, bringing them together overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then return the handles to the starting position, keeping tension on the cables.
Variation: Perform without back support and alternate arms.
Seated_Dumbbell_Press: Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on a bench with back support, resting the dumbbells upright on your thighs.
Raise the dumbbells to your shoulders one at a time using your thighs to help. Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward. This is the starting position.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up until they touch at the top.
After a one-second pause, inhale and slowly lower them back to the starting position.
Seated_Flat_Bench_Leg_Pull-In: Sit on a bench, extend your legs in front of you slightly below parallel to the floor, and hold onto the sides of the bench. Lean your torso back at about a 45-degree angle. This is the starting position.
Exhale and pull your knees in toward your chest while bringing your torso forward.
After a one-second pause, inhale and return to the starting position.
Seated_One-arm_Cable_Pulley_Rows: Sit at the machine with your feet against the platform and knees slightly bent. Hinge forward while keeping the natural arch in your back, and grab the handle with your left hand using an overhand grip.
With your arm extended, sit upright so your torso forms a 90-degree angle with your legs: keep a slight arch in your back, chest up, and lats fully stretched. This is the starting position.
Keeping your torso still, exhale and pull the handle toward your abdomen, keeping your arm close to your body and rotating your palm to face inward. Squeeze your back muscles firmly.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position. Repeat with your right arm.
Tip: Rotate your wrist back to a palm-down position as you return.
Squats_-_With_Bands: Stand on the middle of the band with both feet shoulder-width apart, and grip both ends so that the tension is equal on both sides.
Hold the handles with an overhand grip near your face, at the same height on both sides. This is your starting position.
Slowly bend your knees and lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Exhale, push through your heels, and return to the starting position.
Standing_Alternating_Dumbbell_Press: Stand holding dumbbells in your hands. Bring them up to shoulder level with palms facing forward and elbows out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Press one dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended, keeping the other arm in place. Avoid leaning or jerking the weight.
After a brief pause, return the dumbbell to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm, continuing to alternate sides.
Standing_Barbell_Press_Behind_Neck: This exercise is best performed inside a power rack. Set the barbell to your height, load the weight, step under the bar, and place it across the back of your shoulders just below your neck.
Grip the bar on both sides and unrack it by pushing with your legs and straightening your torso.
Step away from the rack with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward, and back straight. This is your starting position.
Exhale and press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Hold for a second, then inhale as you lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Standing_Bradford_Press: Set a loaded barbell on a rack at shoulder height. Grab it with an overhand, shoulder-width grip and unrack it onto the front of your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows to press the barbell overhead and move it behind your head, without fully locking out your elbows.
Lower the barbell behind your head until your elbows are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your elbows again to lift the bar back over your head and lower it to the starting position. Continue alternating in this manner until the end of the set.
Standing_Cable_Chest_Press: Set both pulleys at chest height and select the weight. Grab a handle in each hand and step 1–2 feet in front of the cables; take a staggered stance for stability if needed.
Keep your upper arms at a 90-degree angle with your shoulder blades retracted. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso still, extend your elbows to press the handles forward, bringing them together in front of you.
Hold at the end point for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Standing_Cable_Lift: Attach a standard handle to the low pulley. Stand sideways to the cable, grab the handle with one hand, and step about an arm's length away so the cable is taut. Keep your arm in line with the cable.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Squat down and grip the handle with both hands, keeping your arms straight.
In one fluid motion, pull the handle up and diagonally across your torso until your straight arms are overhead.
Keep your back straight and arms close to your body; pivot your back foot and straighten your legs to allow a full range of motion.
Return your arms first, then your torso—moving slowly and under control. Complete the set, then repeat on the other side.
Standing_Cable_Wood_Chop: Attach a standard handle to the high pulley. Stand sideways to the cable, grab the handle with one hand, and step about an arm's length away so the cable is taut. Keep your arm in line with the cable.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Reach up with your other hand and grip the handle with both hands, keeping your arms straight.
In one fluid motion, pull the handle down and diagonally across your torso toward your front knee, rotating your torso.
Keep your back and arms straight and your core engaged; pivot your back foot and bend your knees to allow a full range of motion.
Maintaining your stance and straight arms, slowly and under control return to the starting position. Complete the set, then repeat on the other side.
Standing_Dumbbell_Upright_Row: Grip the dumbbells with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width, resting them on your thighs. Keep your arms extended, elbows slightly bent, and back straight. This is your starting position.
Exhale and use your lateral deltoids to pull the dumbbells up along your body until they are nearly at your chin.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Lead the movement with your elbows—they should always remain higher than your forearms. Keep your torso still, and pause for a second at the top.
Standing_Military_Press: Set the barbell in a power rack at about chest height, load the weight, and take an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
Bend your knees slightly, position the barbell across your collarbones, and lift it off the rack, holding it at your chest. Step back with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Press the barbell overhead to fully extended arms, holding it slightly in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell down to your collarbones.
Exhale and press the barbell back up to the starting position.
Standing_Palm-In_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Press: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip, arm down by your side. Place your other hand on an incline bench for balance. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lift the dumbbell, bending your elbow to 90 degrees with your forearm perpendicular to the floor. Maintain the neutral grip throughout the exercise.
Slowly press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the weight until your arm is bent at 90 degrees again. Pause for a second, then exhale and press the weight back up. Switch arms once finished.
Tip: Hold onto the bench and keep your feet planted to maintain your balance.
Standing_Palms-In_Dumbbell_Press: Hold dumbbells with a neutral grip, arms down, feet shoulder-width apart. Raise the dumbbells, bending your elbows to 90 degrees with your forearms vertical. This is your starting position.
Maintaining the neutral grip, slowly press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells until your arms are bent at 90 degrees again.
Step-up_with_Knee_Raise: Stand facing a plyo box or bench of suitable height with your feet together. This is your starting position.
Place your left foot on the bench, and by extending your hip and knee, step up onto it. At the same time, drive your right knee up as high as possible.
Step back down in reverse order and repeat on the other leg.
Stiff-Legged_Barbell_Deadlift: Grasp a barbell using an overhand grip. You may want to use wrist straps for heavier weights.
Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower and your knees slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Keeping your knees fixed, inhale and hinge at the hips with a flat back, lowering the bar toward your feet until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Exhale as you extend your hips and return to the starting position.
Stiff_Leg_Barbell_Good_Morning: For safety, perform this exercise inside a power rack. Set the barbell to your height, load the weight, step under the bar, and rest it across the back of your shoulders just below your neck.
Grip the bar firmly with both hands, push through your legs, and straighten your torso to unrack the bar.
Step back from the rack with your feet shoulder-width apart. Keep your head up—looking down disrupts your balance—and maintain a flat back. This is your starting position.
Keeping your legs stationary, inhale and hinge forward at your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Exhale as you raise your torso back up to the starting position.
Straight-Arm_Dumbbell_Pullover: Place a dumbbell standing upright on a flat bench. Lie crosswise over the bench with only your shoulders supported: your hips should be below the bench, knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and head hanging over the edge.
Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight above your chest, with palms pressed against the underside of the top plate. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back in an arc over your head until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale as you bring the dumbbell back along the same arc to the starting position and hold for a second.
Caution: ensure the dumbbell is securely assembled. Loose plates can slide off and cause injury.
Straight_Bar_Bench_Mid_Rows: Place a loaded barbell near the end of a flat bench. Stand on the bench behind it and take a medium overhand grip. Push your hips back, keep your chest lifted, and maintain a flat back. This is your starting position.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and bend your elbows to pull the barbell toward your torso. Move in a controlled manner without jerking.
After a brief pause, slowly lower the barbell through the full range of motion back to the starting position.
T-Bar_Row_with_Handle: Secure one end of the barbell into a landmine attachment or wedge it firmly into a corner. Load the appropriate weight onto the free end.
Straddle the bar and slide a double D-row handle underneath it right behind the collar. Lift the weight into position by driving through your hips and legs.
Take a wide stance, push your hips back, lift your chest, and keep your arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and bend your elbows to pull the weight toward your upper abdomen. Do not jerk the weight or use momentum from your torso.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
Two-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean: Place two kettlebells between your feet. Push your hips back and look straight ahead. This is your starting position.
Drive through your legs and hips to pull the kettlebells up to your shoulders, rotating your wrists as you catch them.
Lower the kettlebells back to the starting position.
Two-Arm_Kettlebell_Jerk: Clean two kettlebells to your chest by driving through your legs and hips, rotating your wrists so your palms face forward.
Dip into a shallow squat and immediately drive the kettlebells explosively overhead.
As the kettlebells rise, dip under them quickly into a shallow squat to catch them with straight arms.
Lock out the kettlebells overhead and stand up fully.
Two-Arm_Kettlebell_Military_Press: Clean two kettlebells to your chest by driving through your legs and hips, rotating your wrists so your palms face forward.
Press the kettlebells up and slightly outward. As they clear your head, lean your torso slightly forward so the weights lock out just behind your head.
Engage your lats, glutes, and core for stability throughout the movement.
Two-Arm_Kettlebell_Row: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward, pushing your hips back as far as possible. This is your starting position.
Grasp the kettlebells and pull them toward your abdomen by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows, keeping your back flat. Then lower the kettlebells.
Underhand_Cable_Pulldowns: Sit at a lat pulldown station with a wide bar and adjust the knee pads to your height. Take an underhand grip (palms facing you) slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
With your arms fully extended, lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back slightly, and bring your chest forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you pull the bar down to touch your upper chest by depressing your shoulders and driving your elbows down and back. Hold for a second.
Inhale as you slowly return the bar to the starting position until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
Tip: squeeze your back muscles at the bottom and keep your elbows close to your torso. Keep your upper body stationary—only your arms should move, while your forearms simply hold the bar.
Upright_Barbell_Row: Grip a barbell with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width, resting it against your thighs. Keep your arms straight with a slight bend in your elbows and your back flat. This is your starting position.
Exhale and use your lateral delts to pull the barbell straight up along your body, driving your elbows up and out to the sides until the bar is near your chin.
Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Tip: lead the movement with your elbows—they should always remain higher than your forearms. Keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top.
Upright_Cable_Row: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and grasp it with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width, resting it on your thighs. Keep your arms extended with a slight bend in the elbows and maintain a flat back. This is your starting position.
Exhale and use your lateral delts to pull the handle straight up along your body until it is near your chin.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Tip: lead the movement with your elbows—they should always stay higher than your forearms. Keep your torso still and pause for a second at the top.
Smith_Machine_One-Arm_Upright_Row: Set the barbell to hip height and load it with an appropriate weight.
Take a wide grip, unrack the bar, and place your free hand at your side. Stand tall with your working arm extended, head up, and chest lifted. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbow and pull the bar up, leading with your elbow out to the side until your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly, then lower the weight back to the starting position. Once you finish the set, rack the bar.
Smith_Machine_Overhead_Shoulder_Press: Place a bench inside the Smith machine, ideally one with back support. Adjust the bar height so you can reach it with nearly straight arms while seated.
Sit slightly behind the bar so it aligns with the tip of your nose, keeping your feet firmly on the floor. Unrack the bar using an overhand grip and extend your arms. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar to chin level.
Exhale and press the bar back to the starting position using your shoulder muscles.
Smith_Machine_Pistol_Squat: Adjust the bar to your height. Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Take an overhand grip and unrack the bar by extending your legs.
Place one foot about 12 inches ahead of the bar and extend the other leg forward without touching the floor. Look forward with your back straight or slightly arched. This is your starting position.
Maintaining good posture, lower your body by bending your knee and hip as deep as your flexibility allows.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through your heel and extend your knee and hip to return to the starting position.
Smith_Machine_Squat: Set the bar to match your height, load the weight, and step underneath, resting it across your shoulders just below your neck. Unrack the bar with an overhand grip by driving through your legs and straightening your torso.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned slightly out. Keep your head up and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your body by bending your knees until your thighs are slightly below parallel to the floor (knees bent a bit past 90 degrees).
Exhale, drive through your heels to extend your legs, and return to the starting position.
Tip: You can also choose a different foot stance.
Smith_Machine_Stiff-Legged_Deadlift: Set the bar at about mid-thigh height and load the weight. Take an overhand, shoulder-width grip. You may want to use wrist wraps for heavy weights.
Unrack the bar with straight arms and a flat back. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart or narrower, knees slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Keeping your knee angle fixed, exhale, hinge at your hips with a flat back, and lower the bar toward your feet until you feel a good stretch in your hamstrings.
Once you feel the stretch, inhale, extend your hips, and return to the starting position.
Smith_Machine_Upright_Row: Set the bar at about mid-thigh height and load the weight. Take an overhand, shoulder-width grip. You may want to use wrist wraps for heavy weights.
Unrack the bar with straight arms, your back flat, and elbows slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Exhale and use your side delts to pull the bar up along your body until it nearly reaches your chin.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Tip: Lead with your elbows—they should always stay higher than your forearms. Keep your torso still and pause for a second at the top.
Smith_Single-Leg_Split_Squat: Place a bench 2–3 feet behind the Smith machine, adjust the bar to your height, and load the weight. Step under the bar, rest it on your shoulders, and unrack it with an overhand grip.
Place one foot slightly forward under the bar, extend your other leg back, and rest the top of your foot on the bench. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your body by bending your front knee, keeping your back straight and head up, until your thigh is just below parallel to the floor.
Exhale, drive primarily through your front heel, straighten your leg, and return to the starting position. Then switch legs.
Snatch_Pull: With the bar resting on the floor close to your shins, take a wide snatch grip. Lower your hips with your weight on your heels, keeping your back flat, chest up, eyes forward, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: Drive through your heels to extend your knees, maintaining your back angle with straight arms. Guide the bar smoothly above your knees under control.
Second pull — main acceleration: As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jumping motion, driving the bar upward.
Do not actively pull with your arms. At the end of the second pull, your body should be fully extended and leaning slightly back. Make the extension sharp and explosive without dragging it out.
Spell_Caster: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip. Stand with your feet wide and your hips and knees straight. This is your starting position.
Rotate your torso and bring both dumbbells to one side near your hip.
Keeping your arms straight and the dumbbells parallel to the floor, rotate your torso to swing them across to the opposite side.
Continue alternating side to side until the end of the set.
Spider_Crawl: Get into a push-up position on your hands and toes with your feet together, body forming a straight line, and elbows bent at 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Lift one foot off the floor, rotate your leg outward, and bring your knee forward toward your elbow as far as possible.
Return your foot to the starting position and repeat with the other leg.
Split_Squat_with_Dumbbells: Get into a staggered stance with your rear foot elevated and front foot forward. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang at your sides. This is your starting position.
Lower down by bending your front knee and hip. Maintain an upright posture and keep your front knee in line with your foot.
At the bottom, drive through your front heel, extending your knee and hip to return to the starting position.
Squat_with_Plate_Movers: Rack a barbell just below shoulder height and place a weight plate on the floor about 2 feet behind the rack. Load the bar, step underneath, and rest it across the back of your shoulders.

Unrack the bar by pushing through your legs and straightening your torso. Step back into a wide stance with toes slightly flared, placing one foot on the plate. Keep your head up. This is your starting position.
Slowly lower down by bending your knees and hips until your knees are bent slightly past 90 degrees. Exhale, drive through your heels, and extend your hips and knees.
At the top, take a side step to bring your feet together on the other side of the plate.
Use your inside foot to slide the plate across the floor back to its starting spot, step onto it, and reset into a wide stance for the next rep.
Cable_Incline_Triceps_Extension: Lie on an incline bench facing away from the high pulley fitted with a straight bar.
Grab the bar overhead with a close overhand grip (narrower than shoulder-width), keeping your elbows tucked in. Your upper arms should be at about a 25-degree angle to the floor.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and extend your arms, squeezing your triceps, and hold for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Cable_Iron_Cross: Set the pulleys to the highest position, select your weight, and hold a handle in each hand.
Stand directly between the pulleys with your arms out to your sides in a "T" position, chest and head up. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows straight, lower your arms straight down to your sides.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then return your arms to the starting position.
Cable_Lying_Triceps_Extension: Lie on a flat bench and grab the straight bar of the low pulley with a close overhand grip.
Extend your arms directly above your torso so they are at a 90-degree angle to your body. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked in, inhale and bend your arms until the bar lightly touches your forehead.
Exhale, contract your triceps, and return the bar to the starting position. Hold for a second.
Tip: It is easiest to have a spotter hand you the bar once you lie down.
Cable_One_Arm_Tricep_Extension: Stand facing the weight stack and grab the single handle of the high pulley with your right hand using an underhand grip.
Pull the handle down, tucking your upper arm and elbow tight to your side with your elbow bent at less than 90 degrees. You can adopt a staggered stance for balance. This is your starting position.
Exhale, engage your tricep, and extend your arm fully downward. Squeeze your tricep and hold for a second.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position. Complete your reps, then switch arms.
Tip: Only your forearm should move; keep your upper arm completely still throughout.
Cable_Preacher_Curl: Place a preacher bench about 2 feet (60 cm) in front of the cable machine and attach a straight bar to the low pulley.
Sit on the bench, resting your elbows and upper arms firmly against the pad, and have a partner hand you the bar.
Grab the bar and extend your arms fully over the pad. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you curl the weight toward your shoulders, give your biceps a hard squeeze at the top, and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Cable_Rear_Delt_Fly: Set the pulleys above head height and select your weight.
Grab the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand, crossing your arms in front of you. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, draw them back and out to the sides.
Pause at the end of the movement, then return the handles to the starting position.
Cable_Reverse_Crunch: Attach ankle straps to the low pulley and place a mat in front of it. Sit down facing the pulley and strap the cable to your ankles.
Lie down, raise your legs, and bend your knees to 90 degrees. Your legs and the cable should form a straight line; adjust the pulley height up or down if needed.
Place your hands behind your head, pull your knees toward your chest, and lift your hips off the floor.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your hips with control back to the 90-degree position, keeping your abs engaged. Continue for the remainder of the set.
Cable_Rope_Overhead_Triceps_Extension: Attach a rope to the low pulley.

Grip the rope with both hands using a neutral grip and extend your arms overhead. Keep your elbows close to your head, upper arms perpendicular to the floor, and knuckles pointing to the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, inhale and slowly lower the rope behind your head, pausing once your triceps are fully stretched.
Exhale, contract your triceps, and return to the starting position.
Cable_Seated_Crunch: Sit on a flat bench facing away from the high pulley.
Grasp the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and hold your hands firmly against your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Keeping your hips still, exhale and crunch at your waist, driving your elbows down toward your hips.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: In the starting position, allow the weight to slightly arch your lower back.
Cable_Seated_Lateral_Raise: Place a flat bench across and between two low pulleys, then select your weight. Sit on the edge of the bench with your feet in front of your knees, hinge forward with a flat back, and rest your torso on your thighs.
Have a partner hand you the handles: hold the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand. The cables should run underneath your knees.
Extend your arms with palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows. This is your starting position.
Maintaining the elbow angle, exhale and raise your arms out to the sides up to shoulder height, holding for a second. Inhale and slowly lower them down.
Tip: Keep your upper arms perpendicular to your torso and maintain a fixed 10- to 30-degree bend in your elbows throughout.
Cable_Shrugs: Grip the straight bar of the low pulley with an overhand grip, shoulder-width or slightly wider. Stand tall close to the pulley with your arms extended down in front of you. This is your starting position.
Exhale, shrug your shoulders as high as possible, and hold for a second.
Lower the bar back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your arms straight at all times without pulling with your biceps. Move only your shoulders straight up and down.
Cable_Wrist_Curl: Place a flat bench in front of a low pulley attached with a straight bar.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, from narrow to shoulder-width, sit down, and rest your forearms on your thighs. Your wrists should hang just past your knees.
Exhale, curl your wrists upward, and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower your wrists back to the starting position. Keep your forearms still—only your wrists should move.
Upright_Row_-_With_Bands: Stand on the resistance band so the tension begins at arm's length. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width, holding them at your thighs.
Keep your arms extended with a slight bend in your elbows and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Exhale and use your side delts to pull the handles straight up along your body until they are nearly level with your chin.
Inhale as you slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Tip: Let your elbows drive the movement—they should always stay higher than your forearms. Keep your torso still, and pause for a second at the top.
V-Bar_Pulldown: Sit at a lat pulldown machine equipped with a V-bar (triangle handle) and adjust the knee pads to your height so they prevent you from lifting off the seat.
Grasp the handle with a neutral grip. Bring your chest forward and lean back about 30 degrees to better engage your lats. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the handle down using your lats, squeezing your shoulder blades together until it nearly touches your chest.
Pause for a second, then inhale as you slowly return the handle to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your torso stationary throughout the entire movement.
V-Bar_Pullup: If your pull-up bar doesn't have neutral-grip handles, drape a V-bar over the top of the bar with the handles facing down.
Once it is securely set, grasp the handles on both sides and hang freely. Bring your chest forward and lean back slightly to better engage your lats. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up using your lats, tilting your head slightly back so you do not hit the bar, until your chest nearly touches the handle.
Pause for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower yourself to the starting position.
Weighted_Jump_Squat: Place a light barbell across the back of your shoulders. You can also use a weighted vest, sandbag, or other resistance.
The weight should be light enough that it does not noticeably slow you down. Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, head and chest up. This is your starting position.
Perform a partial squat and immediately jump up explosively, extending your hips, knees, and ankles. Maintain good posture throughout the jump.
Cushion the landing by bending your legs as you come down.
Wide-Grip_Barbell_Bench_Press: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Take a wide overhand grip: each hand should be about 3 inches (8 cm) wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell and hold it directly over your chest with your arms straight. This is your starting position.

Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell to the middle of your chest. Pause for a second, then exhale and press it back up using your pecs, straighten your arms, squeeze your chest, and hold for a second.
Tip: Lower the barbell at least twice as slowly as you press it up.
Wide-Grip_Decline_Barbell_Bench_Press: Lie on a decline bench with your feet securely locked under the pads. Take a wide overhand grip: each hand should be about 3 inches (8 cm) wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell and hold it directly over you with your arms straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell to your lower chest. Pause for a second, then exhale and press it back up using your pecs, straighten your arms, squeeze your chest, and hold for a second.
Tip: Lower the barbell at least twice as slowly as you press it up.
Wide-Grip_Decline_Barbell_Pullover: Lie on a decline bench with your legs securely locked in place. Reach behind your head and take an overhand grip wider than shoulder width. Slowly lift the barbell off the floor using your arms.
Extend your arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Inhale as you lower the barbell back in a semicircular arc, as if placing it on the floor, stopping when your arms are parallel to the floor.
Exhale and return the barbell to the starting position under full control. Once you finish the set, slowly lower the barbell to head level and release it.
Tip: Keep your arms straight throughout the movement; all the motion should come from your shoulder joints.
Wide-Grip_Pulldown_Behind_The_Neck: Sit at a lat pulldown machine equipped with a wide bar and adjust the knee pads to your height. Take an overhand grip: wide (wider than shoulders), medium (shoulder-width), or close (narrower).
With your arms extended, tilt your torso and head slightly forward so the center of the bar aligns with the back of your neck. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the bar down until it touches the back of your neck by drawing your shoulders down and driving your elbows down and back.
Pause for a second, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then inhale as you slowly return the bar upward until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
Tip: Squeeze your back muscles at the bottom. Keep your upper body still and move only your arms; don't pull with your forearms—they are only there to hold the bar.
Wide-Grip_Rear_Pull-Up: Grip the pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip.
Hanging with straight arms, tilt your torso and head slightly forward so the bar aligns with the back of your neck. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up until the bar reaches the back of your neck by drawing your shoulders down and driving your elbows down and back, tilting your head slightly forward.
Pause for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower yourself to the starting position until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
Tip: Squeeze your back muscles at the top. Move only with your arms without swinging your torso; your forearms should only hold the bar.
Wide_Stance_Barbell_Squat: For safety, perform this exercise in a power rack. Set the barbell to your height, load the weight, step under the bar, and place it across the back of your shoulders just below the neck.

Unrack the bar by pushing through your legs and straightening your torso. Step back, set your feet wider than shoulder-width with your toes pointed slightly outward. Keep your head up and back straight. This is your starting position.
Inhale as you slowly lower yourself by bending your knees until your thighs are slightly below parallel to the floor (knees bent slightly past 90 degrees).
Exhale and drive through your heels to straighten your legs and return to the starting position.
Tip: Do not look down, as this throws off your balance.
Wind_Sprints: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms and legs extended. This is your starting position.
Quickly drive one knee up as high as possible without swinging your torso or legs.
Immediately lower that leg back to the starting position while driving the other knee up as high as possible.
Continue alternating legs until the end of the set.
Ab_Crunch_Machine: Select a light weight and sit in the crunch machine with your feet under the pads and hands holding the upper handles. Keep your arms bent at 90 degrees with your triceps resting on the pads. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you crunch your upper body forward while simultaneously lifting your legs.
Pause for a second, then inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Move slowly and with control. Move the weight using your abs, keeping your legs and feet relaxed.
Calf-Machine_Shoulder_Shrug: Position yourself in a calf machine with the shoulder pads resting on top of your shoulders. Keep your torso straight and your arms hanging down naturally at your sides. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, raise your shoulders toward your ears and hold for a full second.
As you inhale, slowly return to the starting position.
Calf_Press: Adjust the seat so your legs are only slightly bent in the starting position. Place the balls of your feet firmly on the platform.
Set an appropriate weight and grip the handles. This is your starting position.
Straighten your knees to lift the weight slightly, with your feet fully dorsiflexed and toes pointing up. Then press down through the balls of your feet as far as you can.
After a brief pause, return to the start and repeat.
Calf_Press_On_The_Leg_Press_Machine: Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet flat on the platform in front of you, shoulder-width apart.
Disengage the safety bars and press the platform up until your legs are fully extended, without locking your knees. Your torso and legs should form a 90-degree angle.

Carefully shift your toes and the balls of your feet to the bottom edge of the platform with your heels hanging off. Point your toes straight, slightly outward, or inward. This is your starting position.

As you exhale, press the platform as high as possible using your toes, squeezing your calves; keep your knees straight. Hold for a second, and as you inhale, slowly lower your heels until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Tip: if the machine allows, leave the safety bars engaged for extra safety.
Calf_Raise_On_A_Dumbbell: Hold onto a sturdy support for balance and step onto the handle of a dumbbell, ideally one with round plates: it rolls, making balance more challenging and the exercise more effective.
Roll your foot slightly forward to get a good stretch in your calf. This is your starting position.
