As you exhale, rise onto your toes, rolling your foot across the handle into full extension. Squeeze your calf hard at the top and hold for a second.
As you inhale, lower down while gently rolling the dumbbell forward to deepen the stretch.
Tip: as you rise up, slightly roll the dumbbell backward.
Calf_Raises_-_With_Bands: Stand on the resistance band with the balls of your feet, making sure both sides of the band are equal in length.
Holding the handles, bring your hands up by your head as if setting up for an overhead press: palms forward, elbows bent and out to the sides, band taut. This is your starting position.
Keeping your hands near your shoulders, exhale and rise onto your toes, squeezing your calves firmly at the top.
Hold for a second, then slowly lower back to the starting position.
Car_Drivers: Stand tall and hold a weight plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Your palms should face each other with your arms extended straight out in front of you. This is your starting position.
Rotate the plate as far as you can to one side, just like turning a steering wheel.
Rotate it fully to the opposite side.
Close-Grip_EZ-Bar_Curl_with_Band: Attach a resistance band to both ends of an EZ bar and stand on the center of the band with one foot. Stand tall and grip the bar with a narrow underhand grip, keeping your elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar upward.
Lift the bar to shoulder height until your biceps are fully contracted. Hold for a second and squeeze your biceps hard.
As you inhale, slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Close-Grip_EZ_Bar_Curl: Stand tall and grip the inner bends of an EZ bar. Your palms should face forward and slightly inward due to the bar's shape, with your elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar upward, contracting your biceps.
Lift the bar to shoulder height until your biceps are fully contracted. Hold for a second and squeeze firmly.
As you inhale, slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Tip: only your forearms should move.
Close-Grip_Standing_Barbell_Curl: Grip a barbell with an underhand grip, placing your hands just a few inches apart.
Stand tall with your chest up, feet shoulder-width apart, and elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, curl the barbell up in an arc until your forearms touch your biceps. Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a second.
As you inhale, slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Tip: keep your upper arms and elbows stationary; only your forearms should move. Avoid arching your back or swinging the weight.
Concentration_Curls: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell on the floor between your legs. Keep your legs apart, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor.

Grab the dumbbell with your right hand, rest the back of your upper arm against the inside of your right thigh, and turn your palm forward, away from your thigh. Your arm should be extended with the dumbbell off the floor. This is your starting position.

Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and curl the weight until your bicep is fully contracted and the dumbbell reaches shoulder level. Move only your forearm. Hold for a second and squeeze your bicep.
As you inhale, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Then repeat on your left arm.
Tip: at the top of the curl, your pinky should be slightly higher than your thumb to maximize bicep contraction. Caution: avoid swinging your body.
Cross_Body_Hammer_Curl: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing inward toward your body.
Without rotating your wrist or twisting your arm, exhale and curl the right dumbbell across your torso toward your left shoulder. Lightly touch the top of your shoulder and hold for a second.
As you inhale, slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path and repeat with your left arm. Continue alternating sides.
Crunch_-_Hands_Overhead: Lie on your back on the floor, keeping your lower back flat and knees bent so the angle between your hamstrings and calves is about 60 degrees.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and extend your arms straight overhead, clasping your hands together. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, crunch forward by lifting your shoulder blades off the floor, and hold for a second. Keep your arms aligned with your head, neck, and shoulders at all times—do not bring them forward.
As you inhale, slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Advanced_Kettlebell_Windmill: Clean a kettlebell to your chest and press it overhead with one arm.
Keeping your arm locked overhead, shift your hips toward that side. Place your free arm behind your back and turn your feet 45 degrees away from the loaded side.
Hinge and lower your torso as far down as comfortably possible.
Pause for a second, then return to the starting position.
Alternate_Hammer_Curl: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Keep your elbows close to your torso and palms facing inward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and curl the right dumbbell while squeezing your bicep until it reaches shoulder level. Pause for a second at the top.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat with your left arm to complete one rep. Continue alternating sides.
Alternate_Heel_Touchers: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about 45–60 cm apart. Keep your arms extended by your sides. This is your starting position.
Exhale, lift your torso forward and up about 7–10 cm, crunch to the right to touch your right heel, and hold for a second.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat on the left side to touch your left heel. Touching both heels counts as one rep.
Alternate_Incline_Dumbbell_Curl: Sit back on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging down. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and curl the right dumbbell while turning your palm upward until the dumbbell is near shoulder level. Pause for a second and squeeze your bicep.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat with your left arm to complete one rep. Continue alternating sides.
Tip: Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and move only your forearms.
Alternating_Deltoid_Raise: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells forward to shoulder level without swinging or using momentum.
On the next rep, raise the dumbbells out to the sides to about shoulder level.
Lower the dumbbells and continue alternating between front and lateral raises.
Alternating_Kettlebell_Row: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back, and hinge forward to grip the handles. This is your starting position.
Keeping one kettlebell grounded, lift the other by pulling your shoulder blade back and bending your elbow toward your ribs or waist.
Lower the kettlebell and repeat with the other arm.
Band_Hip_Adductions: Anchor a resistance band around a sturdy post or support.
Stand with your left side toward the post and loop the band around your right ankle.
Stand tall, holding onto the post for balance if needed. This is your starting position.
Keeping your knee straight, move your right leg out to the side as far as possible.
Return to the starting position. Complete your reps, then switch sides.
Band_Pull_Apart: Extend your arms straight in front of you, holding the resistance band with both hands.
Pull the band apart horizontally until it touches your chest. Keep your elbows straight and pull your shoulders back.
Pause briefly at the peak, then return to the starting position with control.
Band_Skull_Crusher: Secure a resistance band to the base of a rack or bench. Lie flat on the bench with your head aligned with the band.
Grasp the band and raise your elbows so your upper arms are perpendicular to the floor. With your arms bent and the band overhead, this is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, extend your elbows. Hold at the top, then return to the starting position.
Barbell_Curls_Lying_Against_An_Incline: Lie against an incline bench holding a barbell with your arms hanging straight down. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and curl the barbell as high as possible, squeezing your biceps.
Hold the contraction for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower the barbell all the way down.
Tip: Move only your forearms and avoid swinging your arms.
Barbell_Seated_Calf_Raise: Place a foot block about 30 cm in front of a flat bench. Sit on the bench and place the balls of your feet on the block.
Have a partner place a barbell across your thighs about 8 cm above your knees and help hold it. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: For best results, get a full stretch in your calves at the bottom.
Barbell_Shrug: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell in front of you with an overhand grip (palms facing your thighs). This is your starting position.
Exhale, shrug your shoulders as high as possible, and hold for a second.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Use a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, and feel free to use lifting straps for a secure hold. Do not pull with your biceps.
Barbell_Shrug_Behind_The_Back: Stand straight with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip (palms facing back). This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your shoulders as high as possible, holding for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Use a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, and feel free to use wrist wraps for a secure grip. Do not pull with your biceps; keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Barbell_Side_Bend: Stand straight with the barbell resting across the back of your shoulders just below your neck, feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Keeping your back straight and head up, inhale and bend at the waist to the right as far as comfortable. Hold for a second, then exhale and return to the starting position.
Repeat the bend to your left side, hold for a second, and return to the starting position.
Tip: Keep the rest of your body still.
Bent_Over_Low-Pulley_Side_Lateral: Select your weight and grab the low-pulley handle with your right hand.

Bend at your waist until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, and place your left hand on your left thigh. Let your right arm hang down in front of you with a slight bend in the elbow. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your right arm out to the side until it is parallel to the floor and aligned with your right ear.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back to the starting position. Then repeat with the other arm.
Body-Up: Get into a plank position on your forearms and toes, keeping your body straight and forearms shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Press your palms into the floor and extend your elbows to push your body up. Keep your core tight.
Bend your elbows and slowly lower your forearms back to the floor.
Body_Tricep_Press: Set a barbell in a rack at chest height.
Grip the bar shoulder-width apart and step back 3 to 6 feet, keeping your feet together, arms straight, and leaning your weight against the bar. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself toward the bar.
Pause, then push back up by extending your elbows.
Variation: To make it more challenging, drape chains over your shoulders.
Bodyweight_Flyes: Place two equally loaded EZ bars on the floor next to each other so they can roll.
Get into a push-up position over the bars on your toes and hands, with your arms and body straight. Place your palms on the bars. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly roll the bars out to the sides in a controlled motion, spreading your arms away from your body.
Once you have rolled out as wide as you comfortably can, exhale and pull the bars back together to the starting position.
Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Bends: Attach a standard handle to each low cable pulley. Place a Bosu ball centered in front of the machine.
Lie back on the Bosu ball, positioning your lower back over the dome, with your hips close to the floor without touching it. Reach back and grab a handle in each hand.
Set your feet wide and extend your straight arms forward between your knees, hands at knee height. Keep your arms in line with the cables.
Without dropping or bending your arms, curl your torso up into a crunch. Slowly lower back down, arching over the Bosu ball to stretch your abs. Continue for the remainder of the set.
Then, bracing your core, hold your torso in a bridge over the Bosu ball, lower your straight arms along your sides, and perform alternating side bends, reaching toward your heels.
Butterfly: Sit on the machine with your back flat against the backrest. Grab the handles. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly bring the handles together, squeezing your chest in the center, and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position until you feel a full stretch in your chest.
Tip: Your upper arms should be parallel to the floor—adjust the machine settings to fit your body.
Cable_Crossover: Set the pulleys to the highest position above your head, select your weight, and grab a handle in each hand.
Step forward past the imaginary line between the pulleys, bringing your hands together in front of you. Lean your torso slightly forward. This is your starting position.
With a slight bend in your elbows to protect your biceps tendons, inhale and open your arms out in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms back along the same arc to the starting position, holding for a second.
Tip: Keep your arms and torso still; the movement should come entirely from your shoulder joints.
Cable_Hammer_Curls_-_Rope_Attachment: Attach a rope to the low pulley and stand facing the machine, about 12 inches away.

Grasp the rope with a neutral grip and stand straight, keeping the natural arch in your back. Tuck your elbows into your sides and keep them stationary throughout the exercise. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the rope using your biceps until your forearms touch your biceps.
Hold for a second, squeezing your biceps, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Only move your forearms—keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your upper arms still.
Cable_Hip_Adduction: Stand sideways by the low pulley with one leg closer to the machine and the other further away. Attach the ankle strap to the cable and to the ankle of the leg closest to the pulley.
Step away from the pulley, take a wide stance, and hold onto the machine frame for balance.
Support your weight on the far leg, allowing the strapped leg to be pulled slightly toward the pulley. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the strapped leg across in front of your supporting leg using your inner thigh.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position. After completing your reps, switch legs.
Cable_Incline_Pushdown: Lie back on an incline bench facing away from a high pulley equipped with a straight bar.
Reach overhead to grab the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip, and extend your arms in front of you with the bar about 2 inches off your thighs. This is your starting position.
Inhale and bring your arms back in a semicircular motion until the bar is directly over your head.
Exhale and use your lats to slowly pull the bar back to the starting position, pausing at peak contraction.
Incline_Hammer_Curls: Sit back firmly against the pad of an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, feet together. Let the dumbbells hang down at your sides using a neutral grip. This is your starting position.
Curl the weights up while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Incline_Inner_Biceps_Curl: Grab a pair of dumbbells and lie back on an incline bench. Let your arms hang straight down at your sides with your palms facing out. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells outward and up, keeping your forearms aligned with your side delts until the weights reach shoulder level beside your shoulders.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back along the same path.
Tip: at the top of the movement, your position resembles a front double-biceps pose.
Internal_Rotation_with_Band: Loop a resistance band around a rack at elbow height. Stand sideways to it with your right side facing the anchor, about 2 feet away.
Grasp the band with your right hand and keep your elbow pinned firmly to your side. Bend your elbow to 90 degrees with your forearm pointed away from your body. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbow in place, rotate your arm inward across your body as far as comfortable. Hold briefly, then return to the starting position.
Tip: place a rolled towel or small pad between your elbow and your side to keep your arm firmly positioned.
Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Front_And_Back: Keep your head and neck in a neutral position (head straight, looking forward) and place both palms on your forehead.
Gently press your head forward into your hands, bracing your neck muscles so your head doesn't move. Start with light effort and gradually increase pressure. Breathe steadily.
Hold for the target number of seconds, then slowly release the tension.
Rest briefly and repeat with your hands placed behind the back of your head.
Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Sides: Keep your head and neck in a neutral position (head straight, looking forward) and place your left palm against the left side of your head.
Gently press your head to the left, bracing the muscles on the left side of your neck so your head doesn't move. Start with light effort and gradually increase pressure. Breathe steadily.
Hold for the target number of seconds, then slowly release the tension.
Rest briefly and repeat with your right palm against the right side of your head.
Janda_Sit-Up: Lie on your back in a standard sit-up position with your knees bent at 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor, and arms crossed over your chest or along your sides. This is your starting position.
Strongly contract your glutes and hamstrings, fill your lungs with air, and slowly roll up over 3 to 6 seconds while exhaling smoothly.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself back down with control to the starting position.
Tip: actively tensing your glutes and hamstrings is key, as it reflexively relaxes your hip flexors through reciprocal inhibition.
Kettlebell_Figure_8: Place a kettlebell between your legs with your feet set wider than shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward by pushing your hips back, keeping your back flat.
Pick up the kettlebell and pass it between your legs to your other hand, reaching from behind the opposite leg to receive it. Continue weaving the kettlebell back and forth in a figure-eight pattern.
Kneeling_Cable_Crunch_With_Alternating_O: Attach a rope to a high pulley and place an exercise mat in front of it. Grab the rope with both hands and kneel down about 2 feet away from the stack.
Hold the rope behind your head with your hands near your ears.
Keeping your hands in place, brace your abs and crunch down until your elbows touch your knees. Pause briefly, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
On the next crunch, twist midway through the movement, aiming one elbow toward the opposite knee. Pause, then slowly return up.
On the following rep, twist your other elbow toward the opposite knee. Continue alternating sides throughout the set.
Kneeling_Cable_Triceps_Extension: Place a bench horizontally in front of a high pulley. Grab a straight bar with an overhand grip, hands about 6 inches apart.
Kneel facing away from the machine and rest the back of your head and shoulders on the bench. Bend your elbows so your forearms point back toward the pulley. This is your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms close to your head and elbows tucked in, exhale and press the bar in a semicircular arc until your arms are straight and parallel to the floor. Squeeze your triceps hard for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Lateral_Raise_-_With_Bands: Stand on the resistance band so there is tension even with your arms down. Hold the handles with a slightly narrower-than-shoulder-width grip, palms facing your thighs, with the handles at your sides.
Keep your arms extended with a slight bend in your elbows and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise the handles out to the sides using your side delts until your arms are slightly above parallel to the floor. Hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Tip: as you lift, slightly tilt your hands forward as if pouring water from a pitcher. Keep your arms extended and your torso still.
Leg_Extensions: Select your weight and sit on the leg extension machine with your legs tucked under the pad, toes pointing forward, and hands gripping the side handles. This is your starting position.
Adjust the pad so it rests on your lower shins just above your feet, creating a 90-degree angle between your shins and thighs.
Exhale and use your quads to fully extend your legs, keeping the rest of your body firmly on the seat. Hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back down, stopping before your knees bend past 90 degrees.
Caution: going past a 90-degree bend places excess stress on the knee joint. If the machine cannot be adjusted, use another machine or limit your range of motion.
Leg_Lift: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Hold onto a sturdy support—such as a squat rack or the back of a chair—for balance.
With or without an ankle weight, exhale and curl one heel up toward your glutes, performing a standing leg curl. Keep your supporting leg straight.
Inhale and slowly lower your foot back to the floor. Complete all reps for the set, then switch sides.
Leverage_Shrug: Set the desired weight and stand squarely between the handles.
Grasp the upper handles with a comfortable grip, and lower your hips as you inhale. Keep your gaze forward and chest up.
Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees and stand up. Keep your arms straight at all times, with your shoulders drawn back at the top. This is your starting position.
Lift the weight by shrugging your shoulders toward your ears in a straight up-and-down motion. Pause briefly at the top, then return to the starting position.
Low_Cable_Crossover: Set the pulleys to the lowest position, select the weight, and take a handle in each hand.
Step forward to create tension on the cables. Turn your palms forward with your hands below your waist and arms straight. This is your starting position.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, bring your hands up toward the midline of your body until they meet in front of your chest with palms facing up.
Pause briefly, then return your arms to the starting position.
Low_Cable_Triceps_Extension: Select the weight and lie on your back on a low row bench with a rope attachment, with your head toward the pulley.
Grasp the ends of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).

Bend your elbows to 90 degrees so your upper arms are perpendicular to your torso pointing toward the ceiling, your forearms point toward the pulley behind your head, and your elbows are tucked in. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, extend your forearms to a vertical position. Keep your upper arms and elbows still; only your forearms should move. Squeeze your triceps hard for a second.
As you inhale, slowly return to the starting position.
Lying_Cable_Curl: Attach a straight or EZ bar to the low pulley and grasp it with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
Lie on your back on a mat facing the weight stack, with your legs straight and feet braced against the machine frame.
Extend your arms with your elbows by your sides, keeping a slight bend in the elbows. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked in, exhale and slowly curl the bar toward your chest, squeezing your biceps.
Hold for a second at the top, then slowly return to the starting position.
Lying_Cambered_Barbell_Row: Place a cambered barbell underneath the bench.
Lie face down on the bench and grasp the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder width. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, pull the bar upward while keeping your elbows close to your body: pull toward your chest to target your mid-upper back, or toward your stomach to target your lats.
Hold at the top for a second, then slowly lower the bar to the starting position as you inhale.
Lying_Close-Grip_Bar_Curl_On_High_Pulley: Position a flat bench in front of a high pulley. Grasp the straight bar attachment with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart.

Lie on your back with your head slightly beyond the edge of the bench. Extend your arms above your shoulders at 90 degrees to your torso, keeping your elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, bend your arms and curl the bar in a semi-circular motion until it touches your chin. Squeeze your biceps for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Only your forearms should move—keep your upper arms stationary and perpendicular to your torso throughout the exercise.
Lying_Close-Grip_Barbell_Triceps_Extensi: Grasp a straight barbell or EZ bar with an overhand grip and lie on a flat bench with your head at the edge. Hold the barbell shoulder-width apart, or use the inner grips on an EZ bar.
Extend your arms in front of you, then slowly lower the bar behind your head in a semi-circular arc without bending your arms until they are parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.
As you inhale, bend your elbows without moving your upper arms, lowering the bar until your forearms are perpendicular to the floor.
As you exhale, press the bar back along the semi-circular arc to the starting position until your forearms are parallel to the floor again. Squeeze your triceps hard at the top for a second.
Tip: Keep your elbows tucked in at all times; only your forearms should move while your upper arms stay still.
Lying_Close-Grip_Barbell_Triceps_Press_T: Grasp a straight barbell or EZ bar with an overhand grip and lie on a flat bench with your head extending off the edge. Hold the straight bar shoulder-width apart, or use the inner grips of the EZ bar.
Extend your arms directly over your chest, perpendicular to your torso. This is your starting position.
As you inhale, bend your arms in a semi-circular motion to lower the bar toward your chin until it lightly touches, keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked in.
As you exhale, press the bar along the same semi-circular path back to the starting position. Squeeze your triceps hard at the top for a second.
Tip: Only your forearms should move; keep your upper arms completely still throughout the rep.
Lying_Dumbbell_Tricep_Extension: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells extended above you on straight arms, perpendicular to your torso and the floor. Keep your palms facing each other and elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly lower the dumbbells toward your ears without moving your upper arms and keeping your elbows tucked in.
As you exhale, engage your triceps to press the dumbbells back to the starting position while keeping your upper arms and elbows steady.
Lying_High_Bench_Barbell_Curl: Lie face down on a high flat bench with the top of your chest extending just past the edge. Grasp a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, or use the inner grips of an EZ bar.
Let the bar hang down on straight arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows tucked in and upper arms still, exhale and curl the bar upward in a semi-circular motion, squeezing your biceps. Hold at the top for a second.
As you inhale, slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Maintain full control of the weight and avoid swinging—only your forearms should move.
Lying_One-Arm_Lateral_Raise: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and lie face down on a flat bench. You can hold onto a bench leg with your free hand for stability.
Hold the dumbbell with a neutral grip (palm facing your body) on an extended arm with a slight bend in the elbow. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, raise your arm out to the side until your elbow is at shoulder level and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
As you inhale, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your arm extended and perpendicular to your torso at all times.
Lying_Rear_Delt_Raise: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie face down on a flat bench.
Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) on extended arms with a slight bend in the elbows. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, raise your arms out to the sides until your elbows are at shoulder level and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
As you inhale, slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your arms extended and perpendicular to your torso at all times.
Flat_Bench_Cable_Flyes: Place a flat bench between two low pulleys so that when lying down, your chest aligns with the pulleys. Lie down with your feet flat on the floor.
Ask someone to hand you the handles and grip them with your palms facing up.
Extend your arms out to the sides parallel to the floor with a slight bend in your elbows—maintain this bend throughout the movement. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, bring your hands together in a semicircle in front of you until they meet at the top, squeezing your chest. Hold for a second and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: At the top, your arms should be perpendicular to your torso and the floor, touching directly over your chest.
Flat_Bench_Lying_Leg_Raise: Lie on your back on a bench with your legs extended off the edge.
Place your hands under your glutes palms down, or grip the sides of the bench. This is your starting position.
Keeping your legs as straight as possible with your knees slightly bent and locked, exhale and raise your legs until they form a 90-degree angle with the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Flexor_Incline_Dumbbell_Curls: Sit on a 45-degree incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand. Grip the dumbbells closer to the outer ends so more weight sits toward your body.

Lower your arms by your sides with your elbows close to your body, palms facing forward, and thumbs pointing away. Extend your wrists fully back to take the strain off them. This is your starting position.
Exhale and simultaneously curl the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Do not rotate your wrists during the curl. Avoid swinging or using momentum—keep the movement controlled.
Frog_Sit-Ups: Lie on your back on the floor or a mat with your legs extended. Bend your knees, let your outer thighs drop toward the floor, and bring the soles of your feet together.
Pull your joined feet as close to your body as possible, keeping the outer sides of your thighs on or close to the floor. Your legs should form a diamond shape.
Cross your arms over your chest, placing your hands on opposite shoulders. This is your starting position.
Exhale, press your lower back into the floor, and curl your torso up—about the first quarter of a standard sit-up. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Front_Cable_Raise: Select the weight on a low pulley and grab a single handle with your left hand.
Stand facing away from the pulley with your arm extended down and the handle in front of your thighs, palm facing your thighs. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso still, exhale and raise your left arm forward with a slight bend in the elbow, palm facing down, until it is just above parallel to the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower your arm back to the starting position. Complete the set, then switch sides.
Front_Dumbbell_Raise: Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand upright with the weights in front of your thighs on straight arms, palms facing your thighs. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso still, exhale and raise the left dumbbell forward with a slight bend in your elbow, palm facing down, until it is just above parallel to the floor. Hold for a second and inhale.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position while simultaneously raising the right one.
Front_Incline_Dumbbell_Raise: Sit on an incline bench set between 30 and 60 degrees, holding dumbbells in your hands.
Extend your arms in front of you with palms facing down and the dumbbells about 2–3 cm above your thighs. This is your starting position.
Without bending your elbows, exhale and slowly raise the dumbbells straight up until they are just above shoulder level. Squeeze at the top for a second.
Inhale and lower your arms back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your head against the bench and feet flat on the floor at all times. Adjust the bench incline to target the muscle from slightly different angles.
Front_Two-Dumbbell_Raise: Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand upright with the weights in front of your thighs on straight arms, palms facing your thighs. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso still, exhale and raise the dumbbells forward with slightly bent elbows, palms facing down, until they are just above parallel to the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Hammer_Curls: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides with your elbows close to your torso and palms facing inward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps until the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold for a moment, squeezing your biceps.
After a brief pause, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your elbows stationary; move only your forearms.
Incline_Barbell_Triceps_Extension: Grip a barbell with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width, and lie on an incline bench set between 45 and 75 degrees.
Raise the barbell overhead on extended arms, elbows tucked in, with your arms continuing the line of your torso. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the barbell in a semicircle behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps.
Exhale, engage your triceps to return to the starting position, and hold for a second.
Tip: Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your head throughout—only your forearms should move.
Incline_Bench_Pull: Grab a pair of dumbbells and lie chest-down on an incline bench set to about 30 degrees.
Extend your arms toward the floor with an overhand grip (palms facing down) and point your elbows out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the dumbbells upward as if doing a reverse bench press: bend your elbows and raise your upper arms while your forearms hang down. Pull until your upper arms are level with your back.
Hold at the top for a second, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Flare your elbows out to the sides so your upper arms and torso form a "T" at the top of the movement.
Incline_Cable_Flye: Set the pulleys to the lowest position below your torso. Place a 45-degree incline bench between them, select your weight, and grab the handles.
Lie back on the bench and bring your arms straight up in front of your face. This is your starting position.
With a slight bend in your elbows to take the strain off the biceps tendon, inhale and lower your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and return your arms along the same arc to the starting position, squeezing your chest. Hold for a second.
Tip: Keep the angle in your elbows locked—the movement should occur only at the shoulder joints.
Crunch_-_Legs_On_Exercise_Ball: Lie on your back with your feet on an exercise ball and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Keep your feet 7–10 cm apart with your toes turned inward and touching.
Place your hands on the sides of your head and bring your elbows in. Press your lower back into the floor to better isolate your abs. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, begin lifting your shoulders off the floor while pressing your lower back down as firmly as you can. Lift your shoulders only about 10 cm, keeping your lower back on the floor.
Squeeze your abs hard at the top and hold for a second. Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Do not interlace your fingers behind your head. Move slowly and with control, without using momentum.
Crunches: Lie on your back with your knees bent at a 90-degree angle and your feet flat on the floor or resting on a bench. If using a bench, place your feet 7–10 cm apart with your toes turned inward until they touch.
Place your hands on the sides of your head and bring your elbows in.
Press your lower back into the floor to isolate your abs, and exhale as you lift your shoulders about 10 cm off the floor, engaging your abs. Keep your lower back on the floor.
Squeeze your abs firmly at the top for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower back to the starting position.
Tip: Do not interlace your fingers behind your head. Move slowly and with control, without using momentum.
Decline_Crunch: Secure your feet at the top of a decline bench and lie back.
Place your hands on the sides of your head and bring your elbows in.
Press your lower back into the bench to isolate your abs, and exhale as you lift your shoulders about 10 cm off the bench, engaging your abs. Keep your lower back on the bench.
Squeeze your abs firmly at the top for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower back to the starting position.
Tip: Do not interlace your fingers behind your head. Move slowly and with control, without using momentum.
Decline_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extension: Secure your feet at the end of a decline bench and lie down, holding dumbbells on your thighs with your palms facing each other.
Once lying down, bring the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width: palms facing each other, arms straight and perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Inhale and, keeping your upper arms still and elbows tucked in, slowly lower the dumbbells in a semicircular motion toward you until your thumbs are near your ears.
Exhale and engage your triceps to return the dumbbells to the starting position.
Decline_EZ_Bar_Triceps_Extension: Secure your feet at the end of a decline bench and slowly lie down.

Using a close grip (slightly narrower than shoulder-width), unrack the EZ bar and hold it above you with straight arms, elbows tucked in, and arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Inhale and, keeping your upper arms still, slowly lower the bar in a semicircular motion toward you until it lightly touches your forehead.
Exhale and engage your triceps to return the bar to the starting position.
Tip: To protect your rotator cuff, it is best to unrack the bar with the help of a spotter.
Double_Kettlebell_Windmill: Place a kettlebell in front of your lead foot. Clean and press the other kettlebell overhead using your opposite arm.
To clean the weight, extend your hips and legs, pulling the kettlebell up to your shoulder, and rotate your wrist so your palm faces forward.
Keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead, push your hips out in the direction of that arm. Turn your feet 45 degrees away from the overhead kettlebell.
Hinge laterally at your hips and push them back as you slowly lower your torso to pick up the kettlebell from the floor. Keep your eyes on the overhead kettlebell the entire time.
Once you grip the bottom kettlebell, pause for a second and return to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Alternate_Bicep_Curl: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides, elbows close to your torso and palms facing your thighs.

Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and curl the right dumbbell forward while rotating your palm up until your bicep is fully contracted at shoulder level. Hold for a second as you squeeze your bicep.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell, rotating your palm back toward your thigh.
Repeat with your left arm to complete one rep. Continue alternating sides.
Tip: Only your forearms should move.
Dumbbell_Flyes: Lie flat on a bench with dumbbells resting on your thighs, palms facing each other.

Using your thighs to help lift them, raise the dumbbells one at a time and press them above your chest at shoulder width, palms facing each other. Stop just short of locking your elbows. This is your starting position.
With a slight bend in your elbows to protect your biceps tendons, inhale and lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms back along the same arc to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles. Hold for a second at the top.
Tip: Keep the angle in your elbows fixed—the movement should come only from your shoulder joints.
Dumbbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise: Sit on an incline bench with dumbbells resting on your thighs.

Use your knees to kick the dumbbells up to shoulder level and lean back. Extend your arms directly above your shoulders perpendicular to the floor, palms facing forward and knuckles pointing to the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, exhale and push the dumbbells upward by lifting your shoulders off the bench.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Lying_One-Arm_Rear_Lateral_Rais: Holding a dumbbell in one hand, lie chest down on an adjustable bench set to a low incline (about 15 degrees from the floor). You can hold the bench leg with your free hand.
Hold the dumbbell with a neutral grip (palm facing your body), arm extended with a slight bend in your elbow. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your arm out to the side until your elbow is at shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your arm extended and perpendicular to your torso throughout the movement.
Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation: Lie face down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in one hand. Bend your other arm and place it on the bench under your head.
Bend the arm holding the dumbbell at a 90-degree angle at the elbow.
Raise your upper arm so it is parallel to the floor and at a 90-degree angle to your torso, with your forearm hanging perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Exhale and rotate your forearm upward and forward, maintaining the 90-degree elbow bend, until your forearm is parallel to the floor. Hold for a second.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Lying_Rear_Lateral_Raise: Holding a dumbbell in each hand, lie chest down on an adjustable bench set to a low incline (about 15 degrees from the floor).
Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing your body), arms extended with a slight bend in your elbows. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your arms out to the sides until your elbows are at shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your arms extended and perpendicular to your torso throughout the movement.
Lying_Supine_Dumbbell_Curl: Lie on your back on a flat bench with the dumbbells resting on your thighs.
Lower the dumbbells down by your sides with arms extended, palms facing your thighs (neutral grip).

Keeping your arms close to your torso and elbows tucked in, slowly lower your arms—keeping a slight bend in the elbows—as low toward the floor as you comfortably can. Lock your upper arms in place; this is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly curl your arms, rotating your palms up, until your biceps are fully contracted, and squeeze hard for a second. Then return very slowly to the starting position.
Tip: Only your forearms should move; keep your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked in.
Lying_Triceps_Press: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. An EZ-bar or straight bar should be on the floor behind your head.
Reach back and grab the bar with a medium overhand grip, then lift it over your chest on straight arms—perpendicular to your torso and the floor, elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar until it lightly touches your forehead, keeping your upper arms and elbows stationary.
Exhale and use your triceps to press the bar back up to the starting position.
Machine_Bicep_Curl: Adjust the seat height and select the weight. Rest your upper arms against the pad and grip the handles. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows, curling your forearms toward your shoulders.
Pause at the top, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Do not let the weight stack touch down until the end of the set to keep tension on the muscles.
Machine_Preacher_Curls: Sit on the preacher curl machine and select the weight.
Rest the back of your upper arms (triceps) on the pad and grip the handles with an underhand grip, keeping your elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the handles up by squeezing your biceps. Hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Tip: Only your forearms should move; keep your upper arms still and flat on the pad throughout the movement.
Machine_Triceps_Extension: Adjust the seat height and select the weight. Rest your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows, pushing your forearms away from your shoulders.
Pause at full extension, then slowly return to the starting position.
Tip: Keep the weight stack hovering until the end of the set to keep constant tension on the muscles.
Middle_Back_Shrug: Lie chest-down on an incline bench holding dumbbells. Let your arms hang straight toward the floor with your palms facing each other. This is your starting position.
Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together, holding the squeeze for a full second.
Inhale and return to the starting position.
Tip: The motion feels like a reverse hug or a bent-over fly performed without bending your elbows.
Oblique_Crunches: Lie on the floor with your lower back pressed down. Place one hand by your head and the other out to the side on the floor.
Elevate your feet and rest them on a flat, raised surface.
Exhale, raise the shoulder of the arm behind your head, and curl your torso up until your elbow touches the opposite knee (e.g., right elbow to left knee).
After touching your knee, inhale and lower yourself back to the starting position.
Alternate sides on the next rep: curl your left elbow toward your right knee.
Oblique_Crunches_-_On_The_Floor: Lie on your right side with your legs stacked and knees slightly bent. Place your left hand behind your head.
Exhale and crunch your torso sideways, driving your left elbow up with the focus on your obliques.
Crunch up as high as you can, hold for a second, and inhale as you slowly lower back down.
One-Arm_Flat_Bench_Dumbbell_Flye: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in one hand resting on your thigh with a neutral grip.
Use your thigh to help bring the dumbbell up over your chest on a straight arm with a neutral grip. Hold the side of the bench with your free hand for support. This is your starting position.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow to protect your bicep tendon, then inhale and lower the arm out in a wide arc until you feel a gentle stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring your arm back along the same arc to the starting position, squeezing your chest. Hold for a second. Switch arms once you complete the set.
Tip: Keep the angle at your elbow fixed—the movement should only happen at the shoulder joint.
One-Arm_High-Pulley_Cable_Side_Bends: Attach a single handle to the highest pulley setting. Stand sideways to the cable stack and grab the handle with an underhand grip.
Pull the handle down until your elbow touches your side and your hand is by your shoulder. Keep your feet hip-width apart and rest your free hand on your waist to help identify the pivot point.
Keeping your arm stationary, engage your obliques and crunch sideways to pull the weight down.
Once fully contracted, slowly return to the starting position. Do not let the stack touch down to keep constant tension.
Repeat for the target reps, then turn around and perform the same on the other side.
One-Arm_Incline_Lateral_Raise: Lie sideways on an incline bench holding a dumbbell. Keep your bottom shoulder against the pad and your lower arm resting across your body, hand near your belly button.
Hold the dumbbell with your top arm extended in front of you, parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping the dumbbell parallel to the floor, exhale and raise your arm out to the side until it points straight up at the ceiling. Hold for a second.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell back across your body to the starting position. Switch arms after completing the set.
One-Arm_Side_Laterals: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and grab a sturdy support, like an incline bench, with the other. Lean slightly away from the support toward the working arm to improve balance.
Keep your torso straight and let the dumbbell hang at your side on an extended arm, palm facing in. This is your starting position.

Without swinging, exhale and raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor, with a slight bend in the elbow and your hand tilted slightly forward as if pouring water. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Switch arms once you finish the set.
Dumbbell_Lying_Supination: Lie on your side on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in one hand. Bend your other arm and place it on the bench under your head.

Bend the arm with the dumbbell at 90 degrees. Keep your upper arm still against your torso and parallel to the floor, with your forearm straight in front of you, parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
Exhale and rotate your forearm outward, raising the dumbbell in a semicircle while maintaining the 90-degree angle, until your forearm is perpendicular to the floor. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, then switch arms.
Dumbbell_One-Arm_Triceps_Extension: Grab a dumbbell and sit on a bench with back support, resting the dumbbell vertically on your thigh, or stand upright.
Bring the dumbbell to your shoulder and extend your arm overhead, perpendicular to the floor. Keep your other hand out to the side, on your waist, or use it to support your working arm.
Turn your wrist so your palm faces forward, with your pinky toward the ceiling. This is the starting position.

Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head without moving your upper arm until your triceps is fully stretched. Exhale, engage your triceps, and return to the starting position. Then switch arms.
Tip: Only your forearm should move; keep your upper arm still next to your head the entire time.
Dumbbell_Prone_Incline_Curl: Grab a pair of dumbbells and lie chest-down on an incline bench with your shoulders at the top edge. You can rest your knees on the seat or straddle your legs.
Let your arms hang straight down, perpendicular to the floor. Keep your elbows tucked to your sides with your palms facing forward. This is the starting position.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells up, squeezing your biceps until your arms are fully bent. Only your forearms should move—keep your upper arms stationary throughout.
Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended.
Dumbbell_Scaption: This exercise strengthens the muscles that stabilize the shoulder blades. Grab a pair of light dumbbells, let your arms hang at your sides, and point your thumbs upward.
Raise your straight arms forward at about a 30-degree angle from your center.
Lift until your arms are parallel to the floor, then return to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Seated_One-Leg_Calf_Raise: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches (30 cm) in front of a flat bench.
Sit on the bench and place a dumbbell on your left thigh, about 3 inches (8 cm) above your knee. Position the ball of your left foot on the block. This is the starting position.
Exhale and raise your heel as high as possible, squeezing your calf. Hold for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position, dropping your heel as low as possible for a stretch. Then repeat on your right leg.
Dumbbell_Shrug: Stand upright with dumbbells hanging at your sides, palms facing inward.
Exhale and shrug your shoulders as high as possible, holding at the top for a second.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your arms straight the entire time and avoid pulling with your biceps. Move only your shoulders—up and down.
Dumbbell_Side_Bend: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in your left hand with your palm facing in, right hand on your waist, and feet shoulder-width apart. This is the starting position.
Keeping your back straight and head up, inhale and bend at the waist to the right as far as comfortable. Hold for a second, then exhale and return to the starting position.
Repeat the bend to the left, hold for a second, and return to the starting position. After completing the set, switch hands.
Tip: Keep the rest of your body completely still.
Dumbbell_Tricep_Extension_-Pronated_Grip: Lie on a flat bench with the dumbbells directly above your shoulders. Keep your arms extended and perpendicular to your torso and the floor.
Palms face forward with your elbows tucked in. This is the starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells toward your ears. Keep your upper arms still and your elbows tucked in.
Exhale and use your triceps to press the dumbbells back to the starting position.
EZ-Bar_Curl: Stand upright and grip the EZ bar on the wide outer curves. Your palms should face forward and slightly inward due to the bar shape, with your elbows close to your torso. This is the starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and curl the bar while squeezing your biceps. Only your forearms should move.
Lift the bar to shoulder level until your biceps are fully contracted. Hold for a moment, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
External_Rotation: Lie on your side on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in one hand. Bend your other arm and place it on the bench under your head.

Bend the arm with the dumbbell at 90 degrees. Keep your upper arm still against your torso and parallel to the floor, with your forearm straight in front of you, parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
Exhale and rotate your forearm outward, raising the dumbbell in a semicircle while maintaining the 90-degree angle, until your forearm is perpendicular to the floor. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, then switch arms.
External_Rotation_with_Cable: Set the cable pulley to elbow height. Stand with your left side toward the machine, about 2 feet (60 cm) away.
Grasp the handle with your right hand and keep your elbow pinned to your side. Bend your elbow at 90 degrees with your hand in front of your torso. This is the starting position.
Without moving your elbow, rotate your forearm outward, away from your torso.
Tip: Tuck a rolled towel or pad between your elbow and torso to keep your elbow securely in place.
Finger_Curls: Grip a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Place your feet on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. This is the starting position.
Open your fingers to lower the bar as far as possible, letting it roll down your palms until you hold it with your fingertips.
Exhale, close your hands, and curl the bar up as high as you can. Hold at the top.
Seated_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Palms-Up_Wrist_C: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Place your feet on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean forward and rest your right forearm on your right thigh with your palm facing up, the back of your wrist resting on your knee. This is the starting position.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell as far as possible while keeping a secure grip on it.
Exhale and curl the dumbbell as high as possible, contracting your forearm. Hold for a second and then lower it again. Move only your wrist.
After finishing the set, switch arms and repeat.
Seated_Palms-Down_Barbell_Wrist_Curl: Grasp a barbell with both hands using an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart. Place your feet on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean forward and rest your forearms on your thighs with palms facing down, the fronts of your wrists resting on your knees. This is the starting position.
Inhale and lower the barbell as far as possible while keeping a firm grip on the bar.
Exhale and curl the barbell as high as possible, contracting your forearms, and hold at the top for a second. Move only your wrists.
Seated_Side_Lateral_Raise: Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on the edge of a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Let your arms hang at your sides, palms facing inward. This is the starting position.
Without swinging your torso, exhale and raise the dumbbells out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows, tilting your hands forward slightly as if pouring water into a glass.
Lift until your arms are parallel to the floor, and hold at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Seated_Triceps_Press: Sit on a bench with back support, grasp a dumbbell with both hands, and raise it overhead with your arms extended.
Hold the dumbbell in your palms with your thumbs wrapped around it, palms facing inward. This is the starting position.
Keeping your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor, inhale and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Move only your forearms.
Exhale and use your triceps to press the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Tip: if the dumbbell is heavy, it is best to have a spotter hand it to you.
Seated_Two-Arm_Palms-Up_Low-Pulley_Wrist: Place a bench in front of a low pulley with a straight bar or EZ-bar attached. Position it so the cable is taut when the handle rests on your thighs.
Grasp the handle with both hands, palms facing up and shoulder-width apart, step back, and sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor at shoulder width.
Lean forward and rest your forearms on your thighs with the backs of your wrists just past your knees. This is the starting position.
Inhale and lower the handle as far as possible while keeping a secure grip. Then curl it as high as possible, contracting your forearms. Move only your wrists.
Hold at the top for a second, then inhale and return to the starting position.
Side_Laterals_to_Front_Raise: Stand tall with dumbbells hanging at your sides. This is the starting position.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells to shoulder height without swinging or jerking.
At the top, bring the dumbbells together in front of you without bending your arms, then lower them under control.
On the next rep, raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, then spread them out to the sides and lower them to the starting position.
Single-Arm_Cable_Crossover: Set the pulleys to the high position, select your weight, and grab a handle in each hand.
Step forward, extend your arms out in front, and bring your hands together. Keep your head and chest up, torso leaning slightly forward, and feet in a staggered stance. This is the starting position.
Holding your left arm in place, open your right arm out to the side with a slight bend in the elbow until it is perpendicular to your torso at about shoulder level.
Bring your arm back to the starting position, returning your hand to the midline of your body.
Pause for a second and repeat with the other arm. Alternate sides.
Single-Leg_Leg_Extension: Sit on the machine and adjust it: the pad should rest against your lower shin just above the ankle, and the pivot point should align with your knee. Select a manageable weight.
Maintaining good posture, fully extend one leg and hold at the top.
Return to the starting position without letting the weight stack touch down, keeping tension on the muscle.
Single_Dumbbell_Raise: Stand with a wide stance and hold a dumbbell with both hands by the plate rather than the handle. Keep your arms straight and lowered near your waist. This is the starting position.
Without bending your arms, raise the dumbbell above shoulder level. Keep your torso and hips stationary.
Sit-Up: Lie on the floor and hook your feet under a secure anchor, or have a partner hold them down. Bend your knees.
Place your hands behind your head and interlace your fingers. This is the starting position.
Exhale and lift your torso until it forms an acute angle with your thighs.
Once you feel the contraction, hold for a second, then inhale as you lower your torso back to the starting position.
Smith_Incline_Shoulder_Raise: Place an incline bench inside a Smith machine and set the bar to a height reachable with nearly straight arms while lying down. Load your weight and lie on the bench with your shoulders directly under the bar.
Grasp the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, unrack it, and hold it above you with elbows slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Exhale and press the bar up until your arms are fully extended. You should feel the contraction in your shoulders.
Pause for a second, then inhale as you lower the bar back to the starting position.
Once finished, rack the bar back onto the safety catches.
Smith_Machine_Behind_the_Back_Shrug: Set the bar to hip height and load the desired weight.
Stand facing away from the bar, grasp it with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and unrack it. Stand tall with your chest up, head straight, and arms extended. This is the starting position.
Shrug your shoulders straight up. Do not bend your elbows or wrists.
After a brief pause, lower the weight back to the starting position. Once you finish the set, re-rack the bar.
Smith_Machine_Calf_Raise: Place an aerobic step or a weight plate under the Smith machine bar and adjust the bar height to match your stature. Add the desired weight, step onto the plate with the balls of your feet, and rest the bar across the back of your shoulders.
Grip the bar with both hands using an overhand grip, palms facing forward, and rotate the bar to unrack it. This is your starting position.
Push through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves. Keep your knees straight. Hold the peak contraction for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower your heels back to the starting position.
Smith_Machine_Hip_Raise: Place a flat bench inside the Smith machine and load the desired weight. Lie on your back on the bench and place the soles of your feet against the bar.
Unrack the bar and extend your legs, using your hands to help if needed. Grip the machine's uprights for stability. This is your starting position.
Roll your pelvis up and flex your spine to lift your hips off the bench. Keep a slight bend in your knees throughout the movement.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your hips back onto the bench.
Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises: Adjust the Smith machine bar to your height and place an elevated platform directly beneath it.
Step onto the platform with your heels, letting the balls of your feet hang off the edge. Point your toes forward with feet shoulder-width apart.
Position yourself under the bar and stand up by extending your legs. Keep a soft bend in your knees without locking them out. This is your starting position.
Exhale and lift your toes as high as possible, flexing the front of your shins. Keep your knees still. Pause for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower your toes.
Tip: Use the bar on your shoulders only to maintain balance.
Speed_Band_Overhead_Triceps: Anchor the resistance band low, such as around the base of an incline bench while straddling it, or simply stand on the band.
Bring the band behind your head holding it with an overhand grip, pointing your elbows straight up. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows to press the band upward, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the top, then return to the starting position.
Spider_Curl: Place a barbell securely on the seat of a preacher bench so it won't roll off.
Stand on the front side of the bench where your arms would normally rest, and lie against it at a 45° angle, pressing your chest and stomach against the slanted pad.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor, especially the balls of your feet, and place your upper arms against the inside pad of the bench.
Grip the barbell with an underhand grip shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower. Exhale as you curl the bar up and hold for a second, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Standing_Barbell_Calf_Raise: For safety, perform this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar at shoulder height, add weight, step under the bar, and rest it across the back of your shoulders just below your neck.
Grip the bar with both hands, unrack it by extending your legs, and straighten your torso.

Step back from the uprights with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward. Keep your chest up, back straight, and knees slightly bent without locking them out. This is your starting position.

Exhale and raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves while keeping your knees stationary. Pause for a second, then inhale and slowly lower your heels until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Tip: For a greater range of motion, place the balls of your feet on a sturdy wooden block, though it will require more balance.
Standing_Bent-Over_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Tric: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing your torso. Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Keep your upper arm tight against your side and parallel to the floor, with your forearm pointing down at a 90° angle. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and use your triceps to extend your arm back until your forearm is parallel to the floor. Move only your forearm.
Hold the peak contraction for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Switch arms once you complete the set.
Standing_Bent-Over_Two-Arm_Dumbbell_Tric: Hold dumbbells with your palms facing your torso. Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Keep your upper arms tight against your sides and parallel to the floor, with your forearms pointing down at a 90° angle. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and use your triceps to extend your arms back until your forearms are parallel to the floor. Move only your forearms.
Hold the contraction for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Standing_Biceps_Cable_Curl: Stand tall and grasp a low cable straight bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar upward while contracting your biceps; move only your forearms.
Raise the bar to shoulder level, fully contract your biceps, and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Standing_Concentration_Curl: Hold a dumbbell in your working hand and lean forward at the hips. Let your working arm hang perpendicular to the floor, with your elbow turned slightly outward. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder. Squeeze your bicep at the top and pause briefly.
Lower the dumbbell smoothly back to the starting position.
Standing_Dumbbell_Calf_Raise: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides. Place the balls of your feet on a sturdy block 2–3 inches (5–8 cm) high, letting your heels hang off and touch the floor. This is your starting position.
Point your toes forward for even development, inward to emphasize the outer calf, or outward to target the inner calf.
Exhale as you rise up onto your toes, squeezing your calves, and hold at the top for a second.
Inhale as you slowly lower your heels back to the starting position.
Standing_Dumbbell_Reverse_Curl: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with an overhand grip and extended arms. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbells upward while contracting your biceps; move only your forearms.
Bring the weights up to shoulder level, fully squeeze your biceps, and pause for a second.
Inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
One-Legged_Cable_Kickback: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and fasten it around your ankle.
Face the cable machine about 2 feet (60 cm) away and hold onto the frame for support.
Keeping your knees and hips slightly bent and your core engaged, exhale, squeeze your glutes, and slowly kick the working leg backward in a semicircular arc as high as comfortable.
Slowly bring your leg back to the starting position, resisting the pull of the cable. Complete the set, then switch legs.
Tip: Squeeze your glutes for a second at full extension for peak contraction.
One_Arm_Dumbbell_Preacher_Curl: Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and place your upper arm on a preacher bench or incline bench, with the dumbbell at shoulder height. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell until your arm is fully extended and your bicep is stretched.
Exhale and curl the dumbbell up using your bicep to shoulder level and full contraction. Keep your pinky higher than your thumb to achieve a full contraction.
Squeeze your bicep hard at the top for a second. Complete the set, then switch arms.
One_Arm_Pronated_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extens: Lie on a bench with the dumbbell held on a straight arm perpendicular to your body. Your palm should face your feet in an overhand (pronated) grip.
Support the bicep of your working arm with your free hand.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell.
Exhale and press the dumbbell back up by contracting your triceps. Complete the set, then switch arms.
One_Arm_Supinated_Dumbbell_Triceps_Exten: Lie on a bench with the dumbbell held on a straight arm perpendicular to your body. Your palm should face toward your face in an underhand (supinated) grip.
Support the bicep of your working arm with your free hand.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell.
Exhale and press the dumbbell back up by contracting your triceps. Complete the set, then switch arms.
Overhead_Cable_Curl: Set both cable pulleys above shoulder height and select an equal, comfortable weight on each side.

Stand in the center and grip the handles with an underhand grip (palms up). Keep your arms straight and parallel to the floor, feet shoulder-width apart, and your body centered between the pulleys. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly curl your arms, squeezing your biceps until your forearms touch your biceps.
Inhale and slowly return your forearms to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your entire body still—only your forearms should move.
Palms-Down_Dumbbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Be: Place two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench and kneel facing the bench.
Pick up the dumbbells with an overhand grip (palms down) and rest your forearms on the bench, letting your hands hang over the edge.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your forearms stationary—only your wrists should move.
Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Bench: Place a barbell on one side of a flat bench and kneel facing the bench.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip (palms down) and rest your forearms on the bench, letting your hands hang over the edge.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your forearms stationary—only your wrists should move.
Palms-Up_Barbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Bench: Place a barbell on one side of a flat bench and kneel facing the bench.
Grip the barbell with an underhand grip (palms up) and rest your forearms on the bench, letting your hands hang over the edge.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your forearms stationary—only your wrists should move.
Palms-Up_Dumbbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Benc: Place two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench and kneel facing the bench.
Pick up the dumbbells with an underhand grip (palms up) and rest your forearms on the bench, letting your hands hang over the edge.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your forearms stationary—only your wrists should move.
Power_Partials: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides, elbows close to your torso, palms facing in, and feet about shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight and your torso still, exhale and raise the dumbbells out to the sides to about shoulder height.
Hold for a second to feel the contraction, then inhale and lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your palms facing down with your pinkies slightly higher than your thumbs as you raise and lower the weights to keep the focus on your delts.
Preacher_Curl: You will need a preacher bench and an EZ-curl bar. Grip the bar with a close grip on the inner curves—ideally have someone hand it to you or unrack it from the bench rests.

Rest your upper arms and chest securely against the bench pad, holding the bar at shoulder height. Your palms should face forward and slightly inward due to the shape of the bar. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar until your arms are fully extended and your biceps are fully stretched.
Exhale and curl the bar up using your biceps to shoulder height and full contraction. Squeeze your biceps hard and hold for a second.
Preacher_Hammer_Dumbbell_Curl: Rest your upper arms on a preacher bench, holding the dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended and your biceps are fully stretched.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells up using your biceps to shoulder height and full contraction.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a second.
Reverse_Barbell_Curl: Stand straight, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width, elbows tucked close to your torso. This is the starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar up as you exhale, squeezing your biceps until fully contracted at shoulder level. Only move your forearms. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Reverse_Barbell_Preacher_Curls: Grip an EZ bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width.
Rest your upper arms on the preacher bench with your arms extended. This is the starting position.
Exhale and curl the bar up toward your shoulders until your biceps are fully contracted. Squeeze hard at the top for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar until your arms are fully extended and your biceps are stretched.
Reverse_Cable_Curl: Stand upright and grip the straight bar attached to a low pulley with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width, elbows close to your torso. This is the starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar up as you exhale, squeezing your biceps until fully contracted at shoulder level. Only move your forearms. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Reverse_Crunch: Lie flat on the floor with your legs extended and arms along your sides, palms flat on the floor. Keep your arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Raise your legs so your thighs are perpendicular to the floor, with your feet together and parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
Inhale and pull your legs toward your torso, curling your pelvis up off the floor until your knees touch your chest.
Hold for a second, then exhale and lower your legs back to the starting position.
Reverse_Flyes: Lie chest-down on an incline bench holding dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Extend your arms in front of you perpendicular to the bench. Keep your legs stationary, planted on the balls of your feet. This is the starting position.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, exhale and raise the dumbbells out to the sides in an arc until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to make the exercise more effective.
Reverse_Flyes_With_External_Rotation: Lie chest-down on an incline bench set to 30 degrees, holding dumbbells with your palms facing down.

Extend your arms in front of you perpendicular to the bench with your elbows slightly bent. Keep your legs stationary, resting on the balls of your feet with your heels off the floor. This is the starting position.
Maintaining the bend in your elbows, exhale and raise the dumbbells in an arc to head level, rotating your wrists outward 90 degrees from palms-down to a neutral grip.
Feel the contraction, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to make the exercise more effective.
Reverse_Grip_Triceps_Pushdown: Attach a straight or EZ bar to the high pulley.

Face the machine, grab the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width, and pull it down using your lats until your arms are fully extended. Keep your elbows at your sides and feet shoulder-width apart. This is the starting position.
Inhale and slowly let the bar rise to chest level. Only move your forearms, keeping your elbows and upper arms pinned to your sides throughout.
Exhale and push the bar back down to the starting position, squeezing your triceps hard.
Reverse_Hyperextension: Load the weight and hook your feet between the rollers. Lie face down on the top pad so your hips hang off the back edge, and grasp the handles.
Hinge at your hips, pulling your legs forward.
