Extend your hips, driving your legs backward.
Hinge at your hips again, pulling the pendulum forward as far as possible.
Caution: Avoid hyperextending your hips—stop just short of the full range of motion.
Reverse_Machine_Flyes: Move the handles all the way back, select your weight, and adjust the seat height so the handles are at shoulder level. Grasp them with palms facing inward. This is the starting position.
Pull your arms out to the sides and back in a semicircular motion, squeezing your rear delts.
Keep your arms slightly bent throughout, moving only at the shoulder joints.
Pause at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Rocking_Standing_Calf_Raise: For safety, perform this exercise in a squat rack. Set and load the barbell to match your height, step under the bar, and rest it across the back of your shoulders just below the neck.
Hold the bar with both hands, unrack it by pushing with your legs and straightening your torso. Step back, placing your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned slightly outward.
Keep your head up at all times—looking down will throw off your balance. Keep your back straight and knees slightly bent, never locked. This is the starting position.
Exhale and raise up onto your toes as high as possible by flexing your calves, keeping your knees stationary. Pause for a second, then inhale and slowly lower your heels to feel a stretch.
Next, exhale and pull your toes up, contracting your shins. Hold for a second, then inhale and lower them back down.
Rope_Crunch: Kneel down 1 to 2 feet (30–60 cm) in front of the cable pulley with a rope attachment.
Select your weight and grasp the rope with both hands above your head. Keep your torso upright.
Flex your spine and pull the rope down, bringing your ribcage toward your legs.
Pause at the bottom and slowly return to the starting position.
Variation: Add a twist or side bend to target your obliques.
Rope_Straight-Arm_Pulldown: Attach a rope to the high pulley and select your weight. Stand about 2 feet (60 cm) away with a staggered stance and grasp the rope with both hands.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and your arms extended up and forward. This is the starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the rope down toward your thighs by rotating at your shoulders.
Hold at the bottom, squeezing your lats. Return to the starting position without letting the weight stack touch down.
Seated_Barbell_Twist: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with the barbell across your thighs and feet shoulder-width apart.

Grip the barbell with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and press it overhead until your arms are locked out. Lower the bar behind your head onto the base of your neck. This is your starting position.
Keeping your feet and head still, exhale and rotate your torso to the side, engaging your obliques, then inhale as you return to center. Alternate sides.
Caution: rotate only as far as your waist comfortably allows—twisting too far can lead to injury. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Seated_Bent-Over_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Tricep: Sit on the edge of a flat bench holding a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palm facing in).
Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward at the waist with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Raise your upper arm alongside your torso until it is parallel to the floor, with your forearm pointing down at a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and extend your arm using your triceps until it is fully straightened and parallel to the floor. Move only your forearm.
Hold at the top for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbell. Complete the set, then switch arms.
Seated_Bent-Over_Rear_Delt_Raise: Place dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench. Sit on the edge of the bench with your feet together and the dumbbells behind your calves.
Hinge forward at the waist with a flat back and grab the dumbbells, palms facing each other. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso hinged and stationary and your elbows slightly bent, exhale and raise the dumbbells straight out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Hold at the top for a second, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Tip: avoid swinging your torso or pulling your arms backward—raise them straight out to the sides.
Seated_Bent-Over_Two-Arm_Dumbbell_Tricep: Sit on the edge of a flat bench holding dumbbells in both hands with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward at the waist with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Raise your upper arms alongside your torso until they are parallel to the floor, forearms pointing down at a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and extend your arms using your triceps until they are fully straightened and parallel to the floor. Move only your forearms.
Hold at the top for a second, then inhale as you slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Seated_Calf_Raise: Sit on the machine and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform with your heels hanging off. Point your toes forward, inward, or outward depending on your preference.
Position the lower part of your thighs under the pad, adjusting its height, and place your hands on top to keep it from sliding forward.
Slightly lift the lever by pushing up through the balls of your feet and disengage the safety bar. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your heels until your calves are fully stretched.
Exhale and rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing your calves. Hold at the top for a second.
Seated_Close-Grip_Concentration_Barbell_: Sit on a flat bench with a straight or EZ barbell resting on the floor between your legs. Keep your feet apart, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor.

Grasp the bar with an underhand grip narrower than shoulder-width and press the back of your upper arms against your inner thighs, about 9 cm from your knees. Keep your arms extended with the bar off the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and curl the bar by contracting your biceps; move only your forearms. Lift the bar to shoulder level and hold for a second, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Tip: avoid swinging or using momentum throughout the exercise.
Seated_Dumbbell_Curl: Sit on a flat bench holding dumbbells at arm's length with your elbows tucked close to your torso.
Turn your palms inward toward your body. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and curl the weights; as the dumbbells pass your thighs, begin rotating your wrists so your palms face up. Move only your forearms.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, fully contract your biceps, and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells, rotating your wrists back to a neutral grip.
Seated_Dumbbell_Inner_Biceps_Curl: Sit on the edge of a flat bench holding dumbbells at your sides with your elbows tucked close to your torso.
Turn your palms inward into a neutral grip. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, curl the weights outward and upward while turning your palms up, keeping your forearms aligned with the outer part of your delts. Move only your forearms.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder level, fully contract your biceps, and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells, rotating your hands back to a neutral grip.
Seated_Dumbbell_Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl: Place two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench. Sit on the edge of the bench with your feet about shoulder-width apart, flat on the floor.
Pick up the dumbbells and rest your forearms on your thighs palms down, letting your wrists hang over your knees.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position. Once finished, lower the dumbbells to the floor.
Tip: keep your forearms completely still—move only your wrists.
Seated_Dumbbell_Palms-Up_Wrist_Curl: Place two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench. Sit on the edge of the bench with your feet about shoulder-width apart, flat on the floor.
Pick up the dumbbells and rest your forearms on your thighs palms up, letting your wrists hang over your knees.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position. Once finished, lower the dumbbells to the floor.
Tip: keep your forearms completely still—move only your wrists.
Seated_Leg_Tucks: Sit across a bench, extend your legs forward just below parallel to the floor, and hold onto the edges of the bench. Lean your torso back to about 45°. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull your knees toward your chest while simultaneously bringing your torso forward.
After a one-second pause, inhale and return to the starting position.
Seated_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Palms-Down_Wrist: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Place your feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lean forward and rest your right forearm on your right thigh palm facing down, with the back of your wrist resting over your knee. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell as far as possible while maintaining a secure grip.
Exhale and curl the dumbbell as high as possible, contracting your forearm. Hold for a second before lowering it again. Move only your wrist.
After completing the set, switch arms and repeat.
Standing_Dumbbell_Straight-Arm_Front_Del: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs with your palms facing your thighs.
Keep your arms straight with your elbows slightly bent and locked in place. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise the dumbbells in an arc overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Inhale and slowly lower them along the same path back to the starting position.
Standing_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extension: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Grip a dumbbell with both hands and slowly raise it overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Rest the dumbbell in the palms of your hands with your thumbs wrapped around it, palms facing up. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor with your elbows tucked in. Inhale and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps.
Exhale and use your triceps to raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your upper arms stationary; only your forearms should move.
Standing_Front_Barbell_Raise_Over_Head: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width, elbows slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise the barbell directly overhead, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Once you feel the tension, inhale and lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Standing_Inner-Biceps_Curl: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with your elbows close to your torso.
Turn your palms inward into a neutral grip. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbells outward, engaging your biceps and rotating your wrists so your palms face up at the top. Only your forearms should move.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder level, keeping your forearms aligned with the outer part of your delts. Hold for a second, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells, rotating your wrists back into a neutral grip.
Standing_Leg_Curl: Adjust the machine lever to your height. Lean your torso forward at about a 30–45° angle to better engage your hamstrings.
Position the lever pad behind your right leg just below your calf, resting the front of your leg against the machine pad.
Without straightening your torso, fully extend your leg and grasp the side handles. Keep your toes pointed straight ahead. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl your right leg as far as possible without lifting your thigh off the pad. Hold for a second, then inhale and return your leg to the starting position.
After finishing the set, repeat with your left leg.
Standing_Low-Pulley_Deltoid_Raise: Stand with your right side to a low pulley. Reach across your body with your left hand to grasp the handle with an overhand grip in front of you. Hold the machine with your right hand for support.
Keep your back straight and your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your left arm out to the side across your body until it reaches shoulder height.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
After finishing the set, switch sides.
Standing_Low-Pulley_One-Arm_Triceps_Exte: Grip the low pulley handle with your left hand and face away from the machine, keeping your arm extended by your side.
Use both hands to bring the handle overhead, palm facing forward. Keep your upper arm vertical and support your left elbow with your right hand. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm close to your head, inhale and lower the handle in an arc behind your head until your forearm touches your bicep. Only your forearm should move.
Exhale and use your triceps to return to the starting position.
After finishing the set, switch sides.
Standing_One-Arm_Cable_Curl: Grip the low pulley handle and step far enough away from the machine so your arm holds the weight under tension.
Keep your upper arm stationary and perpendicular to the floor, elbow tucked in, and palm facing forward. Place your free hand on your hip for balance.
Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and slowly curl your arm until your forearm touches your bicep. Only your forearm should move.
Pause to squeeze your bicep, then inhale and lower the handle back to the starting position.
After finishing the set, switch sides.
Standing_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Curl_Over_Incl: Stand behind an incline bench like a spotter. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip and rest your arm against the backrest.
Grip the corner or edge of the bench with your free hand. Press your chest against the top of the backrest, with your feet wide and firmly on the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm still, exhale and curl the weight by engaging your bicep until the dumbbell reaches shoulder level. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
After finishing the set, switch sides.
Standing_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extens: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and extend the arm holding the dumbbell overhead. Your pinky points toward the ceiling with your palm facing forward. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arm close to your head and perpendicular to the floor with your elbow tucked in. Inhale and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your forearm touches your bicep.
Exhale and use your triceps to raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
After finishing the set, switch sides.
Tip: Keep your upper arm stationary; only your forearm should move.
Standing_Overhead_Barbell_Triceps_Extens: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Hold a barbell or EZ bar with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
Raise the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor with your elbows tucked in. Inhale and lower the barbell in an arc behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps.
Exhale and use your triceps to raise the barbell back to the starting position.
Tip: Keep your upper arms stationary; only your forearms should move.
Standing_Palms-Up_Barbell_Behind_The_Bac: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and look straight ahead. Hold a barbell behind your glutes with arms fully extended, hands shoulder-width apart and palms facing backward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists in an upward arc. Only your wrists should move.
Hold for a second, then inhale and lower the barbell back to the starting position.
When finished, lower the barbell onto the rack or to the floor by bending your knees.
Tip: It is easiest to take the barbell from a rack or have a partner hand it to you.
Standing_Rope_Crunch: Attach a rope to the high pulley and select your weight.
Face away from the cable machine, grasp the rope with both hands over your shoulders, and hold it against your upper chest. This is your starting position.
Flex your spine and crunch downward as far as you can.
Hold the peak contraction, then return to the starting position.
Standing_Towel_Triceps_Extension: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold one end of a towel with both hands.
Extend your arms overhead with your elbows tucked in, upper arms perpendicular to the floor, and palms facing each other. This is your starting position.
Have a partner hold the other end of the towel to provide resistance.
Keeping your upper arms close to your head, inhale and lower your hands in an arc behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Move only your forearms.
Exhale and use your triceps to raise the towel back to the starting position.
Straight_Raises_on_Incline_Bench: Place a barbell on the floor behind the head of an incline bench.
Lie face down on the bench. Grab the barbell from the floor with an overhand grip on straight arms and let it hang straight down. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the barbell forward in front of your head.
Tate_Press: Lie flat on a bench with dumbbells resting on your thighs, palms facing each other.
Use your thighs to help raise the dumbbells one at a time over your chest. Keep your hands wider than shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip and elbows flared out. This is your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms still, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells in an inward and downward arc until they touch your upper chest. Keep full control of the dumbbells and do not rest them on your chest.
Exhale and use your triceps to press the dumbbells back up along the same arc, keeping them close together. Fully extend your arms, pause for a second, then lower them slowly again.
Tip: lowering the weight should take at least twice as long as pressing it up.
Thigh_Abductor: Sit in the thigh abductor machine and select a comfortable weight. Position your legs properly and grasp the side handles. Keep your upper body still. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly push your legs outward against the pads.
Hold the contraction for a second, then inhale and return your legs to the starting position.
Caution: keep your upper body still to avoid injury.
Thigh_Adductor: Sit in the thigh adductor machine and select a comfortable weight. Place your legs on the footrests and grasp the side handles. Keep your upper body still. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly bring your legs together, pressing against the pads.
Hold the contraction for a second, then inhale and return your legs to the starting position.
Caution: keep your upper body still and avoid jerky movements to prevent injury.
Tricep_Dumbbell_Kickback: Hold a pair of dumbbells with your palms facing your torso. Slightly bend your knees and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.
Keep your upper arms tucked close to your torso and parallel to the floor, forearms pointing down with elbows bent at 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and fully extend your arms using your triceps. Move only your forearms.
After a brief pause at the top, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Triceps_Pushdown_-_Rope_Attachment: Attach a rope to the high pulley and grasp it with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).

Stand upright with a slight forward lean. Keep your upper arms tucked against your torso and perpendicular to the floor, with your forearms pointing up toward the pulley. This is your starting position.
Exhale and push the rope down using your triceps, spreading the ends apart at the sides of your thighs until your arms are fully extended. Keep your upper arms still; move only your forearms.
Pause for a second, then inhale and slowly return the rope to the starting position.
Triceps_Pushdown_-_V-Bar_Attachment: Attach a V-bar to the high pulley and grasp it with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.

Stand upright with a slight forward lean. Keep your upper arms close to your torso and perpendicular to the floor, with your forearms pointing up and thumbs higher than your pinkies. This is your starting position.
Exhale and push the bar down using your triceps until it touches your thighs and your arms are fully extended. Keep your upper arms still; move only your forearms.
Pause for a second, then inhale and slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Tuck_Crunch: Lie on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed flat against the ground and your arms at your sides, palms facing down.
Cross your ankles and slowly raise your legs until your thighs are perpendicular to the floor, knees slightly bent. Your shins and feet should be parallel to the floor.
Lift your hands off the floor and cross your arms over your chest. This is your starting position.
Keeping your lower back pressed to the floor, exhale and slowly curl your torso up.
Inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position.
Two-Arm_Dumbbell_Preacher_Curl: Hold a pair of dumbbells and rest your upper arms on a preacher bench or incline bench, holding the weights at shoulder level. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells until your arms are extended and your biceps are fully stretched.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells up to shoulder level using your biceps.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a second.
Wide-Grip_Standing_Barbell_Curl: Stand upright and grip the barbell with a wide grip on the outer parts of the bar, palms facing forward and elbows tucked close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and curl the bar upward by contracting your biceps. Move only your forearms.
Raise the barbell to shoulder level, hold for a second, and squeeze your biceps hard.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Wrist_Rotations_with_Straight_Bar: Grip a barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Alternately extend your wrists, as if rolling up a newspaper. Continue until the end of the set.
Then reverse the direction: alternately flex your wrists, rotating the bar in the opposite direction until the end of the set.
Zottman_Curl: Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides, elbows tucked close to your torso, and palms facing each other. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, exhale and curl the weights while rotating your wrists palms-up; only your forearms should move. Curl the dumbbells up to shoulder level.
Hold for a second as you squeeze your biceps, then at the top, rotate your wrists palms-down with your thumbs slightly higher than your pinkies.
Slowly lower the dumbbells using this overhand grip.
As the dumbbells approach your thighs, rotate your wrists back to a neutral grip (palms facing your body).
Zottman_Preacher_Curl: Grab dumbbells and rest your upper arms on a preacher bench or incline bench. Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with elbows bent and palms facing down. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells palms-down until your arms are extended and your biceps are fully stretched. At the bottom, rotate your wrists palms-up.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells up to shoulder level using your biceps. For a full contraction, keep your pinkies slightly higher than your thumbs.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a second, then rotate your wrists back to a palms-down grip.
Alternating_Renegade_Row: Place two kettlebells on the floor about shoulder-width apart. Get into a push-up position holding the handles of the kettlebells, keeping your body in a straight line. Spread your feet wide for better stability.
Push one kettlebell into the floor as you row the other to your side, bending your elbow and retracting your shoulder blade on the working side.
Lower the kettlebell back to the floor and repeat with the other arm.
Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees: Load an Olympic barbell with 2.5–5 kg plates on each side and kneel on the floor.
Place the barbell on the floor in front of you, supporting yourself on your hands and knees as in a kneeling push-up position. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly roll the barbell forward, stretching your body out into a straight line. Go as low as possible without letting your body touch the floor.
Hold for a second, then exhale and pull yourself back to the starting position.
Tip: Move slowly and keep your core braced throughout the movement.
Barbell_Squat_To_A_Bench: For safety, perform this exercise inside a squat rack. Place a flat bench or box behind you; it teaches you to sit your hips back and squat to the proper depth.
Set the barbell in the rack to your height, load the weight, step under the bar, and rest it across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck.

Grip the bar, unrack it by driving through your legs and straightening your torso. Step back from the rack with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out. Keep your back straight and head up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself by bending your knees and driving your hips back until you lightly touch the bench. Exhale and drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
Bent_Press: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder by extending your hips and legs, rotating your wrist as you bring it up. This is your starting position.
Bend sideways away from the kettlebell until your free hand touches the floor. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell.
Simultaneously press the kettlebell straight up by extending your arm, keeping it perpendicular to the floor.
Stand back upright with the kettlebell overhead, then lower it back to your shoulder.
Box_Squat_with_Chains: Set up inside a squat rack with a box of the appropriate height behind you. Typically, choose a height that allows you to squat to parallel, but it can be higher or lower.
Drape a lead chain over the ends of the barbell and attach the heavy chain to it using a carabiner. Adjust the length so that a few links rest on the floor at the top.
Rest the bar on the back of your shoulders, pull your shoulder blades together, and drive your elbows forward. Unrack the bar with an arched lower back and step back. Keep your head facing forward.
Keeping your back and core tight, push your hips back and knees out, then sit back onto the box; your shins should ideally be vertical. Pause briefly and release your hip flexors. Do not bounce.
Keeping your weight on your heels and knees forced out, powerfully explode off the box, leading the movement with your head. Keep your entire body braced.
Double_Kettlebell_Snatch: Place two kettlebells just behind your feet. Bend your knees, hinge your hips back, and grip both kettlebells.
Powerfully swing the kettlebells back between your legs, then reverse the direction.
Drive through your hips and lock out the kettlebells overhead in one continuous motion.
Front_Barbell_Squat: For safety, perform this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the barbell to your height and load the weight. Bring your arms under the bar with your elbows high and upper arms slightly above parallel to the floor.
Rest the barbell on your front delts and secure it with a crossed-arm grip. Unrack the bar by driving through your legs and straightening your torso.
Step back from the rack with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly out. Keep your back straight and head up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower down by bending your knees until the angle between your thighs and calves is slightly less than 90°. Exhale and push back up through the middle of your feet.
Front_Barbell_Squat_To_A_Bench: For safety, perform this exercise inside a squat rack. Place a flat bench behind you, set the barbell to your height, and load the weight.
Bring your arms under the bar with your elbows high. Rest the bar on your front delts, secure it with a crossed-arm grip, and unrack it by driving through your legs and straightening your torso.
Step back from the rack with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly out. Keep your back straight and head up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself by bending your knees until your glutes touch the bench. Exhale and drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
Handstand_Push-Ups: Stand facing away from a wall, bend forward, and place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
Kick your legs up into a handstand against the wall. Keep your arms and legs straight and your body as aligned as possible. Face your head toward the wall without looking down.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself until your head almost touches the floor.
Exhale and slowly press yourself back up, extending your elbows almost completely.
Caution: Lower yourself slowly to avoid injuring your head. Have a spotter assist you the first time.
Hanging_Pike: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, keeping your legs together. You can use wrist straps for a secure grip.
Bend your knees to 90 degrees and raise your thighs until they are parallel to the floor, with your shins perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your legs up until your shins almost touch the bar. Try to straighten your legs as much as possible at the top.
Lower your legs back to the starting position as slowly as possible.
Tip: Avoid swinging and using momentum at all times.
Kettlebell_Pistol_Squat: Hold a kettlebell by the horns with both hands. Lift one foot off the floor.
Squat down on your standing leg by bending your knee and sending your hips back, keeping the kettlebell in front of you.
Hold for a second at the bottom, then push through your heel to stand up, keeping your chest up and head forward.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Snatch: Place a kettlebell between your feet. Bend your knees and hinge at the hips. This is your starting position.
Look straight ahead and swing the kettlebell back between your legs.

Immediately reverse the motion by powerfully extending your hips and knees, driving the kettlebell upward. As it passes your shoulder, punch your hand up and rotate your wrist to lock the kettlebell out overhead.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Split_Snatch: Grip the kettlebell handle with one hand.
Squat down, then reverse direction by extending your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the kettlebell overhead.
As you reach full extension, drop into a split lunge with one foot forward and one back, catching the kettlebell overhead in one smooth movement.
Stand up with the kettlebell overhead and bring your feet together. Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position.
One-Arm_Overhead_Kettlebell_Squats: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder with one hand by extending your hips and legs and rotating your wrist, then press it overhead, locking out your elbow. This is your starting position.
Look forward, keep the kettlebell locked out overhead, and squat down by bending your knees and hips, keeping your chest and head up.
Pause for a second at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
One-Arm_Side_Deadlift: Stand sideways next to the middle of the barbell. Bend your knees and lower yourself down to reach the bar.
Grip the bar like a suitcase handle with your palm facing in. For heavy weight, you may want to use wrist straps. This is your starting position.
Exhale and drive through your legs to stand up with the barbell, keeping your arm fully extended.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell, making sure to bend your knees to avoid injury.
Switch hands once you complete the set.
One_Leg_Barbell_Squat: Stand 60 to 90 cm in front of a flat bench with your back to it, feet shoulder-width apart, and a barbell on the floor in front of you.

Bend your knees, grip the barbell with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width, and clean it to your chest. Then press it overhead and rest it across the back of your shoulders at the base of your neck.
Place the top of one foot behind you on the bench, keeping the other foot forward. Keep your back straight, chest up, and head held high.

Inhale and lower down until your front thigh is parallel to the floor, with your knee over your toes and your chest over the middle of your thigh. Exhale and drive through your quad to return to the starting position.
Switch legs once you complete the set.
Open_Palm_Kettlebell_Clean: Place a kettlebell between your feet. Drive through your hips and legs to lift the kettlebell toward your shoulders.
As it rises, release the handle and let the kettlebell flip so that its body rests into your open palms.
Push the kettlebell forward and catch the handle with both hands. Lower it back to the starting position.
Plyo_Kettlebell_Pushups: Place a kettlebell on the floor. Get into a push-up position with one hand on the floor and the other on the kettlebell, arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Lower your chest as far as you can while keeping your back straight.
Explosively push up and shift your body across the kettlebell to switch hands. Lower down immediately and continue moving side to side.
Press_Sit-Up: Lie back on an ab bench with a barbell across your chest. Secure your legs firmly under the rollers. This is your starting position.
Inhale and brace your core and glutes. Exhale and curl your torso up like a regular sit-up while simultaneously pressing the barbell overhead.
Inhale and lower your torso back to the starting position, bringing the barbell back to your chest.
Tip: Press the barbell with your arms, but keep the focus on engaging your abs.
Speed_Squats: For safety, use a power rack. Set the barbell to your height, load the weight, step under the bar, and rest it across the back of your shoulders just below your neck.

Grip the bar, unrack it by pushing through your legs and straightening your torso. Step back from the rack with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward. Keep your back straight and head up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower down by bending your knees until the angle between your thighs and shins is slightly less than 90 degrees.
Exhale and drive up as quickly as possible, pushing primarily through your heels, without using momentum or sacrificing form.
Squat_Jerk: Stand with the barbell resting on the front of your shoulders, feet hip-width apart. Dip by slightly bending your knees without shifting your hips back, then immediately reverse the motion with power.
Drive through your heels to accelerate the barbell upward, moving your head out of the way as the bar leaves your shoulders.
As your feet leave the floor, quickly snap them slightly wider than hip-width, turning your toes out if needed. Catch the barbell overhead with locked arms in a full squat.
Keeping the bar balanced over your heels, with your head and chest up, drive through your heels to stand fully upright. Carefully lower the barbell to the floor.
Weighted_Sissy_Squat: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, rising onto your toes. Hold onto a rack upright with one hand and press a weight plate against your chest with the other. This is your starting position.
Holding onto the rack, inhale and bend your knees to slowly lower your torso toward the floor, driving your hips and knees forward until your knees reach nearly a 90-degree angle.
Hold the stretch for a second.
Exhale and drive through your thighs to return to the starting position.
Zercher_Squats: For safety, perform this exercise in a power rack. Set the barbell on the pins just above your waist but below chest level, then load the weight.
Clasp your hands together, hook your elbows under the bar, and unrack it so the bar rests in the crooks of your elbows across your arms.
Step back from the rack with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes turned slightly out. Keep your back straight and your head up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower down by bending your knees until the angle between your thighs and calves is slightly under 90 degrees. Exhale and drive back up, pushing primarily through the balls of your feet.
Ab_Roller: Hold the ab roller with both hands and kneel on the floor.
Place the roller on the floor in front of you, supporting yourself on your hands and knees like in a kneeling push-up. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body into a straight line. Lower yourself as far as you can without letting your body touch the floor.
Pause, then exhale and pull yourself back to the starting position.
Tip: Move slowly and keep your abs engaged the entire time.
Balance_Board: Place the balance board on the floor in front of you.
Step onto the board and try to find your balance.
Maintain your balance for as long as needed.
Band_Assisted_Pull-Up: Loop a resistance band around the middle of the pull-up bar. Bands with different resistance levels will provide varying amounts of assistance.
Pull the band down and place one bent knee into the loop, making sure it will not slip out. Grip the bar with a medium or wide grip. This is your starting position.
Pull yourself up by engaging your lats and bending your elbows, driving your elbows down toward your sides. Pull your chest up until your chin clears the bar, without swinging or jerking.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower back to the starting position.
Battling_Ropes: You will need a heavy battle rope anchored at its midpoint 15–20 feet (4.5–6 m) away. Hold one end of the rope in each hand with your arms down at your sides. This is your starting position.
Raise one arm up to shoulder height as quickly as you can.
As you whip that arm back down, raise the other arm.
Continue alternating arms, whipping the ropes up and down as fast as possible.
Bodyweight_Mid_Row: Grip the bar with an overhand grip, medium or wider than shoulder-width. From a dead hang, pull your knees to your chest, lean back, and place your legs over the bar. This is your starting position.
Starting with straight arms, bend your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades together, pulling your body up until your legs touch the bar.
Pause briefly, then lower yourself back to the starting position.
Decline_Push-Up: Lie face down on the floor, place your hands about 3 feet (90 cm) apart, and press up to support your body with straight arms. Place your feet on a box or bench. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Exhale and press back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower yourself again.
Dips_-_Chest_Version: You will need parallel dip bars. Push up onto the bars with your arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself, leaning your torso forward about 30 degrees and allowing your elbows to flare out slightly, until you feel a light stretch in your chest.
Once you feel the stretch, exhale and use your chest to press back up to the starting position.
Tip: Squeeze your chest at the top for a second.
Exercise_Ball_Pull-In: Place an exercise ball nearby and get into a push-up position in front of it with your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Rest your shins on top of the ball with your legs straight and your upper body supported on straight arms. This is your starting position.
Keeping your back straight and your upper body still, exhale and pull your knees toward your chest, rolling the ball under your ankles. Squeeze your abs and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly straighten your legs, rolling the ball back to the starting position.
Gironda_Sternum_Chins: Grip the pull-up bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Hang with straight arms, push your chest forward, and lean back, maintaining this arch throughout the entire movement. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up, arching your back and keeping your head tilted away from the bar. At the top, your hips and legs will be angled at about 45 degrees to the floor.
Pull until your collarbones clear the bar and it touches the lower part of your chest. Hold for a second; your head should be parallel to the floor at this point.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Inverted_Row: Set a barbell in a rack at about waist height. You can also use a Smith machine.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width and hang underneath it: keep your body straight, heels on the floor, and arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to pull your chest up to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top, then lower yourself back to the starting position.
Inverted_Row_with_Straps: Attach a rope or suspension straps to a rack or another sturdy anchor. Grab the handles and hang facing up with your body straight, heels on the floor, and arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top, then lower back to the starting position.
Kipping_Muscle_Up: Grip the rings with a false grip, resting the base of your palms on top of the rings.
Initiate the movement by swinging your legs slightly backward.
Powerfully swing your legs forward and up, drive your chin and chest back, and pull up with both arms.
At the top, pull the rings toward your armpits, lean your shoulders forward, and drive your elbows straight back. Then, maintaining balance, press up until your arms are fully extended.
Caution: lower yourself to the floor carefully.
London_Bridges: Attach a climbing rope to a high beam. Place a Smith machine bar directly underneath, securely locked onto the safety stops, or use a sturdy plyo box.
Stand on the bar while holding the rope for balance. This is your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, lean back and lower yourself by walking your hands down the rope until your body is parallel to the floor.
Keeping your body straight, walk your hands back up the rope to return to the starting position.
Muscle_Up: Grip the rings with a false grip, resting the base of your palms on top of the rings.
Pull yourself up, bending your elbows and keeping them close to your sides.
At the top, pull the rings toward your armpits, lean your shoulders forward, and drive your elbows straight back to transition into a dip.
Maintaining balance, press up to fully extend your arms.
Caution: lower yourself to the floor carefully.
One-Arm_Medicine_Ball_Slam: Stand in an athletic staggered stance. Hold a medicine ball in one hand on the side of your rear leg. This is your starting position.
Wind up and raise the ball overhead, extending your hips, knees, and ankles for the throw.
At full extension, forcefully drive through your shoulders, core, and hips to slam the ball into the floor directly in front of you.
Catch the ball on the rebound and continue.
Otis-Up: Anchor your feet and lie on the floor with your knees bent. Hold a weight at your chest with both hands. This is your starting position.
Flex through your hips and spine to raise your torso off the floor.
As you sit up, press the weight overhead so it finishes directly above you at the top.
Lower your torso back down while bringing the weight back to your chest, without resting your back completely on the floor.
Parallel_Bar_Dip: Stand between parallel bars, take hold of them, and jump up into a support position on straight arms. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself until the angle at your elbows is less than 90°. Avoid swinging and keep good posture.
Extend your elbows to press back up to the starting position.
Physioball_Hip_Bridge: Rest your upper back on an exercise ball with your hips unsupported. Place your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart or wider. This is your starting position.
Extend your hips by driving through your glutes and hamstrings to lift into a bridge.
Pause at the top, then lower back to the starting position.
Plate_Twist: Sit on the floor or a mat with your legs extended and your torso upright. Hold a weight plate by its edges with both hands in front of your stomach, elbows slightly bent.
Slowly cross your legs at the ankles and raise them off the floor with knees slightly bent. Lean your torso back slightly for balance. This is your starting position.
Exhale and twist the plate to the left to lightly tap the floor.
Inhale to return to the starting position, then repeat on the right side.
Caution: move slowly and with control, as jerky motions can injure your back.
Push-Ups_With_Feet_On_An_Exercise_Ball: Lie face down on the floor, place your hands about 36 inches (90 cm) apart, and push up to support your upper body.
Place your toes on top of an exercise ball so your body is elevated.
Inhale and lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Exhale, press back up to the starting position using your chest muscles, and squeeze your pecs. Hold for a second.
Ring_Dips: Grip the rings and jump lightly into a support position on straight arms. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself until the angle at your elbows is less than 90°. Avoid swinging and keep good posture.
Extend your elbows to press back up to the starting position.
Rocky_Pull-Ups_Pulldowns: Grip the bar with a wide overhand grip. Hanging from straight arms, lean your torso back about 30°, arch your lower back, and drive your chest forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up until the bar touches your upper chest, pulling your shoulders down and back. Keep the work in your arms and back; your forearms should only hold the bar.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top, hold for a second, and inhale as you slowly lower until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
Next, pull up with a straight torso so the bar touches the back of your neck instead of your chest. Tilt your head slightly forward to make the movement smoother.
Rope_Climb: Grasp the rope with both hands overhead, jump up, and pull down.
Wrap the rope around one leg and clamp it between your feet. Reach up as high as possible with your hands, gripping the rope firmly.
Release the rope with your feet and pull yourself up with your arms, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Clamp the rope with your feet again and stand up to reach higher. Continue climbing until you reach the top.
To descend, loosen the clamp with your feet and slide down, alternating your handholds.
Side_To_Side_Chins: Grasp the pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip. Hanging with straight arms, lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back, and push your chest forward. This is the starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up toward the left side until the bar nearly touches your upper chest, pulling your shoulders down and back. Hold for a second, squeezing your back muscles.
Inhale and return to the starting position.
Repeat the pull-up toward the right side and lower yourself down on an inhale. Alternate sides.
Tip: Keep your torso from swinging; only your arms move, and your forearms should just hold the bar.
Single-Leg_High_Box_Squat: Place a box inside a power rack and secure a resistance band or rope above it.
Stand in front of the box and step onto it with one leg until it is fully extended, keeping the other leg unsupported. Hold the band for balance.
Continue stepping up onto and down from the box with the same leg, then switch legs.
Sled_Overhead_Backward_Walk: Attach two handles to the sled with a rope or chain. Load the sled with light weight.
Face the sled and walk backward until the line is taut. Raise your arms straight overhead with your elbows locked. This is the starting position.
Walk backward while keeping your arms overhead. Avoid jerking.
Sled_Row: Attach two handles to the sled with a rope or chain and load it with an appropriate weight. Face the sled and step back until the line is taut.
Grasp a handle in each hand, bend your knees slightly, keep your head and chest up, and extend your arms.
Bend your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades together to row the sled toward you.
Take a step or two back to make the line taut again, then repeat.
Suspended_Push-Up: Securely anchor the suspension straps to the top of a rack or another overhead mount.
Lean toward the straps, take a handle in each hand, and get into a push-up position with straight arms, staying as close to parallel to the floor as possible while maintaining good posture.
Keeping your core tight and your body in a straight line, slowly lower yourself by bending your elbows.
Lower down until the angle at your elbows is less than 90 degrees, pause, and press back up to the starting position.
Suspended_Row: Set the suspension straps to about chest height. Grasp a handle in each hand and lean back. Keep your body straight, head and chest up, and arms extended. This is the starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull yourself up toward the handles.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then return to the starting position.
Suspended_Split_Squat: Set the suspension strap handles about 45–75 cm off the floor.
Stand facing away from the anchor point and place your rear foot in the strap behind you. Look straight ahead with your chest up and your front knee slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Lower toward the floor by bending your knee and hips. Keep your weight on your front heel and maintain good posture throughout the exercise.
At the bottom, reverse the movement and extend your hip and knee to return to the starting position.
Svend_Press: Stand up straight. Squeeze two light weight plates together between your palms and hold them at your chest, flexing your pecs. Point your fingers forward. This is the starting position.
Keeping the plates pressed together, extend your arms straight out in front of you with control.
Hold for a moment at full extension, then slowly return to the starting position.
Trap_Bar_Deadlift: Place a loaded trap bar on the floor with an appropriate weight. Step into the center and grasp both handles.
Lower your hips, look straight ahead, and keep your chest up.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand up. Never round your back.
Lower the weight back to the floor with control.
Weighted_Ball_Hyperextension: Lie face down on an exercise ball with your torso parallel to the floor. Dig the balls of your feet into the floor for balance. Hold a weight plate under your chin or behind your neck. This is the starting position.
Exhale and slowly raise your torso by extending your lower back.
Hold for a second, squeezing your lower back, then inhale and lower your torso to the starting position.
Weighted_Bench_Dip: Place one bench behind you and another in front of you, both perpendicular to your body. Grip the edge of the rear bench close to your hips with hands shoulder-width apart and arms straight.

Place your straight legs on the front bench so they are parallel to the floor, keeping your torso perpendicular to the floor. Have a partner place a dumbbell on your lap. This is the starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself by bending your elbows until the angle at your elbows is slightly under 90 degrees. Keep your elbows tucked close to your body with your forearms pointing down.
Exhale and push through your triceps to return to the starting position.
Caution: Perform this exercise with a partner; placing the weight onto your lap by yourself is difficult and can cause injury.
Weighted_Pull_Ups: Attach a weight to a dip belt and fasten it securely around your waist. Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, fully extending your arms.
Lean your torso back about 30 degrees, creating a slight arch in your lower back, and push your chest out. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up until your head is above your hands. At the top, squeeze your shoulder blades back and down.
After a brief pause, inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position, fully extending your arms and stretching your lats.
Weighted_Squat: Place two flat benches shoulder-width apart and stand on them. Put on a dip belt with a comfortable weight, pointing your toes slightly outward.
Stand tall so the weight hangs freely between your legs, keeping your arms at your sides. This is your starting position.
Inhale and bend your knees with a straight back and head up until your thighs go slightly below parallel with the floor (just under a 90-degree angle).
Exhale and push primarily through the balls of your feet against the benches to straighten your legs and return to the starting position.
Ball_Leg_Curl: Lie on your back on the floor and place your feet on an exercise ball so your ankles rest on top of it with your legs straight. This is your starting position.
Raise your hips off the floor, supporting your weight on your shoulder blades and feet.
Bend your knees and roll the ball as close to your glutes as possible, squeezing your hamstrings.
After a brief pause, slowly return to the starting position.
Donkey_Calf_Raises: Position yourself in a donkey calf raise machine, resting your lower back and hips under the padded lever at your tailbone. Grip the side handles for support.

Place the balls of your feet on the foot platform with your heels hanging off. Point your toes forward, inward, or outward depending on your goal. Keep your knees straight but not locked. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves. Keep your knees still and straight throughout the movement. Hold for a second at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower your heels until you feel a deep stretch in your calves, returning to the starting position.
Downward_Facing_Balance: Lie face down with your stomach resting on an exercise ball.
Balancing on the ball, walk your hands forward along the floor and lift your legs, keeping your elbows and knees straight.
Exercise_Ball_Crunch: Lie on an exercise ball so your lower back rests snugly against its curve. Bend your knees, plant your feet flat on the floor, and let your upper torso hang off the ball.
Keep your arms along your sides or cross them over your chest to avoid straining your neck.
Lower your torso back into a stretch without moving your neck. This is your starting position.
Exhale, keep your hips steady, contract your abs, and curl your shoulders and torso upward. Keep your lower back in contact with the ball the entire time. Hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise: Have a partner hold your feet firmly down, or anchor them under a sturdy, immovable object.
Kneel tall with your hips extended and torso upright while your partner secures your feet. This is your starting position.
Lower yourself forward by extending your knees, keeping your hips straight and body in a line.

As you near the floor, place your hands in front of you and lightly push off to help return to the starting position. This movement is very challenging and often requires a light push-off with your hands.
Front_Plate_Raise: Stand tall and hold a weight plate by the sides at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions, palms facing each other. Keep your arms straight with a slight bend in the elbows, letting the plate hang in front of your thighs. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly raise the plate until it is slightly above shoulder height, holding for a second at the top. Keep your arms locked in position throughout the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the plate back to the starting position.
Tip: do not swing the weight or bend your elbows; keep your torso completely still.
Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench and secure your ankles firmly under the foot pads.

Adjust the upper pad so the top of your thighs rests on it, leaving your hips free to bend forward. Straighten your body and cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly bend forward at the waist with a flat back until you feel a good stretch in your hamstrings and can keep your spine neutral.
Slowly raise your torso back to the starting position.
Tip: do not round your back, hyperextend past a straight line, or swing your torso. To increase resistance, hold a weight plate against your chest under your crossed arms.
Knee_Hip_Raise_On_Parallel_Bars: Step onto a captain's chair station, placing your forearms on the pads along your sides and gripping the handles with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright with your lower back pressed firmly against the back pad and your straight legs hanging down. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your straight legs until they are roughly parallel to the floor, holding for a second at the top. Avoid swinging or relying on momentum.
Inhale and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Lying_Face_Down_Plate_Neck_Resistance: Lie face down on a flat bench with your body straight, shoulders just past the edge so your upper chest, neck, and face hang off. Hold a weight plate against the back of your head. This is your starting position.
While keeping the plate secure against the back of your head, inhale and slowly lower your head downward as if nodding yes.
Exhale and raise your head back up in a smooth semi-circular motion to the starting position, holding for a second at the top.
Lying_Face_Up_Plate_Neck_Resistance: Lie face up on a flat bench with your body straight, shoulders just past the edge so your traps, neck, and head hang off. Hold a weight plate securely against your forehead. This is your starting position.
While holding the plate firmly against your forehead, inhale and slowly lower your head backward in a semi-circular motion.
Exhale and raise your head back up in a smooth semi-circular motion to the starting position, holding for a second at the top.
Plate_Pinch: Take two wide-rim plates and place them together with the smooth sides facing out.
Grip the outer side of one plate with your fingers and the other with your thumb to hold them together. This is your starting position.
Pinch the plates firmly and hold for as long as possible.
Platform_Hamstring_Slides: Use a wooden or similar smooth floor. Lie on your back with your legs straight, placing a towel or a light plate under one heel. This is your starting position.
Bend your knee while keeping the other leg straight.
Pull your heel toward you by sliding it along the floor.
Once your knee is fully bent, reverse the motion and return to the starting position.
Prone_Manual_Hamstring: You will need a partner. Lie face down with your legs straight, and have your partner place their hand on your heel.

Bend your knee to raise your lower leg. Your partner provides resistance—light at first, increasing the pressure toward the end of the movement. Communicate with your partner to adjust the resistance.
Pause at the top, then return your leg to the starting position while your partner resists in the opposite direction.
Reverse_Plate_Curls: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a plate with an overhand grip at arms' length near your groin, placing your fingers on the ribbed side and your thumbs on the smooth side. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly curl the plate up, keeping your elbows close to your torso and your shoulders still, until your forearms touch your biceps. The plate should be directly in front of your torso.
Pause for a second, then inhale and lower the plate back to the starting position.
Tip: It is best to hold the plate at the 11 and 1 o'clock positions.
Scapular_Pull-Up: Grip the bar with an overhand grip and hang from it.
Without bending your arms, pull yourself up a few inches by depressing your shoulder girdle—like a reverse shrug.
Hold at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back to the starting position.
Seated_Band_Hamstring_Curl: Anchor a resistance band low near the floor and place a bench about 2 feet away.
Sit on the bench and loop the band around your ankles with your legs straight. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees to pull your feet toward the bench. You may need to lean back slightly so your feet do not touch the floor.
Pause at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Seated_Head_Harness_Neck_Resistance: Place a neck harness with your selected weight on the floor near the end of a flat bench. Sit on the edge with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing outward.

Hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor and securely fit the harness onto your head with both hands while the weight stays on the floor. Then, supporting the weight with your hands, bring your torso back to a near-upright position.
Keep your head and torso tilted slightly forward. Rest your hands on your knees. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your head until your chin touches the top of your chest.
Exhale and return your head to the starting position.
Sled_Overhead_Triceps_Extension: Attach two handles to the sled with a chain or rope and load the sled with an appropriate weight.

Face away from the sled and step forward until there is tension. Raise your arms overhead with your hands together, palms facing each other, and elbows bent and pointing up. This is your starting position.
Extend your elbows to straighten your arms. Keep your upper arms stationary to isolate the triceps.
After reaching full extension, step forward to restore tension. You can use a staggered stance for better stability.
Sled_Reverse_Flye: Attach two handles to the sled with a rope or chain and load it with a light weight.
Face the sled and step back until there is slight tension. Hold the handles with straight arms at waist level, knees slightly bent, and chest and head up. This is your starting position.
Without bending your elbows, pull the handles up and out to the sides in a reverse flye motion with external rotation. Keep your palms facing forward.
Return to the starting position and take a couple of steps back to regain tension.
Standing_Olympic_Plate_Hand_Squeeze: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a plate by the rim in each hand with your arms at your sides and a neutral grip. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the plates until your fingers are almost fully open but still holding the weight.
Exhale, squeeze your hands, and pull the plates back to the starting position.
Suspended_Fallout: Adjust the straps so the handles hang below waist level.
Stand, grasp the handles, and lean forward into the straps in an inclined push-up position. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, lean further forward to bring your body closer to the floor while raising your arms overhead by moving at the shoulders.
Keep your spine neutral and your body in a straight line—only your shoulder joints should move.
Pause at the point of maximum tension, then return to the starting position.
Suspended_Reverse_Crunch: Set up the suspension straps so the handles hang about 12 inches off the floor. Get into a push-up position facing away from the anchor point.
Place your feet into the foot cradles. Keep your body in a straight line without letting your hips sag. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and hips to pull your knees toward your chest, tucking your pelvis and rounding your spine.
Reach the top position under control, then return to the starting position.
Weighted_Ball_Side_Bend: Lie on an exercise ball on your left side with your waist, hip, and shoulder resting against the ball. Keep your feet on the floor with your legs crossed.

Hold a weight plate against the right side of your head with your right hand, smooth side facing in. Bend your left arm at a right angle and rest your palm on your obliques. This is your starting position.
Exhale and lift your torso sideways by bending at the waist.
Hold for a second, then inhale and slowly lower back to the starting position.
Weighted_Crunches: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the floor or resting on a bench, knees bent at 90 degrees.
Hold a weight against your chest or on straight arms above your torso. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly lift your shoulders about 4 inches (10 cm) off the floor, keeping your lower back pressed down.
Squeeze your abs at the top and pause briefly.
Inhale and slowly lower back to the starting position.
Weighted_Sit-Ups_-_With_Bands: Attach resistance bands to the base of a decline bench and place the handles inside the bench so you can reach both while lying down.

Secure your legs and grab the handles with an overhand grip. Bring them up to your collarbones and rotate your wrists to a neutral grip, keeping your arms stationary from here on. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl your torso up until it is perpendicular to the floor. Hold for a second, then inhale and lower back to the starting position.
Wrist_Roller: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the wrist roller with an overhand grip.

Slowly raise your straight arms out in front of you parallel to the floor. The cord should be completely unrolled. Keep your entire body still except for your forearms. This is your starting position.
Roll your wrists upward one at a time, winding the cord around the roller and lifting the weight toward it.
Once the weight reaches the roller, slowly lower it back down by rolling your wrists downward until you return to the starting position.
Mixed_Grip_Chin: Grip the pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width (about an inch wider), with one palm facing away and the other facing you. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up. The underhand arm works your back muscles with the elbow tucked close, while the overhand arm engages your lats with the elbow flared to the side.
Pause for a second at the top, then inhale and slowly lower yourself down.
On the next set, switch grips so each hand takes the opposite position.
One_Arm_Chin-Up: Drape a towel over the pull-up bar. Grip the bar with an underhand grip with one hand and hold the towel with the other.
Lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back, and push your chest forward. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull yourself up until the bar touches your upper chest, drawing your shoulders down and back. Squeeze your back muscles at the top; your forearms should only be maintaining your grip.
After a second, inhale and slowly lower yourself until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched.
Band_Good_Morning: Stand on one end of a 41-inch (104 cm) resistance band with your feet slightly apart. Hinge at the hips and loop the other end behind your neck. This is your starting position.
Keeping your legs straight, extend your hips until you are nearly standing upright.
Lower back down to the starting position without rounding your back.
Band_Good_Morning_Pull_Through: Loop a resistance band around a rack. Step forward slightly and drape the other end over your neck, holding onto it with your hands.
Hinge forward at the hips, pushing your pelvis back as far as possible. Keep your back flat, hinge to about 90 degrees, and keep your knees only slightly bent.
Drive your hips forward to return to the starting position.
Barbell_Glute_Bridge: Sit on the floor with a loaded barbell over your legs. A thick bar or bar pad will significantly reduce discomfort. Roll the barbell over your hips and lie flat on the floor.
Drive through your heels to extend your hips straight up with the barbell. Keep your weight supported by your upper back and heels.
Extend as high as possible, then lower back down to the starting position.
Bench_Jump: Place a plyo box or bench 1 to 2 feet (30–60 cm) in front of you. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Drop into a shallow quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Explode upward by extending your hips, knees, and ankles, jumping as high as possible while swinging your arms forward and up.
Jump over the bench and land softly on bent knees, absorbing the impact with your legs.
Turn around and jump back over the bench.
Bench_Press_-_Powerlifting: Lie on the bench with your head positioned slightly behind the bar if possible. Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back.

Using the bar for support, lift your shoulders and retract your shoulder blades. Drive through your legs to press your traps firmly into the bench, keeping this tight position throughout the entire lift.
Use any grip width as long as your hands cover the ring markings on the bar. Unrack the bar without letting your shoulders roll forward, and squeeze the bar as if trying to rip it apart.
Lower the bar to your lower chest or upper abs. Keep the bar, wrists, and elbows aligned at all times.
Pause briefly as the bar touches your torso, then press it up as powerfully as possible. Keep your elbows tucked until your arms are fully extended.
Board_Press: Lie on the bench with your head positioned slightly behind the bar if possible. Place 1 to 5 boards (2x6 inches) on your chest, held in place by a partner, resistance bands, or tucked under your shirt.

Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar for support, lift your shoulders, retract your shoulder blades, and drive your traps into the bench with your legs. Keep this position throughout the lift.
Use your regular grip or a shoulder-width grip for more triceps emphasis. Unrack the bar without letting your shoulders roll forward, and squeeze the bar as if trying to rip it apart.
Lower the bar to the boards and press it up as powerfully as possible. Keep the bar, wrists, and elbows in line, with your elbows tucked until your arms are fully extended.
Box_Squat: Set up a box inside a power rack behind you—usually at a height that allows you to squat to parallel, but you can set it higher or lower.

Rest the barbell across your upper back, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and pull your elbows forward as if bending the bar. Unrack the bar with your lower back tight and arched, then step back.
A wide stance targets your back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings more, while a narrow stance emphasizes your quads. Keep your eyes forward.
Keeping your back, shoulders, and core braced, push your knees outward and sit your hips back until you sit on the box, ideally with your shins vertical. Pause and relax your hip flexors.
Drive through your heels, keep your knees pushed out, and stand up powerfully off the box, leading with your head and keeping your entire body tight. Never bounce off the box.
Clean: Position the barbell over your midfoot against your shins, using an overhand or hook grip slightly wider than your legs. Drop your hips, keep your weight on your heels, back flat, chest up, and shoulders slightly ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: Drive through your heels and extend your knees, keeping your back angle constant and arms straight. Lift the bar smoothly until it clears your knees.

Second pull (the main explosion): As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jump-like movement without pulling with your arms. At the finish, your body should be fully extended and leaning slightly back.

Third pull: Shrug forcefully, pull your elbows up and out, and quickly pull yourself under the bar, rotating your elbows around it. Catch the bar across the front of your shoulders near your throat with relaxed wrists.
Descend into a full front squat and immediately stand up by driving through your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows high.
Clean_Deadlift: Stand at the bar with it touching your shins, feet under your hips, and toes angled slightly out. Grip the bar with an overhand or hook grip at shoulder width.
Squat down to the bar: keep your back completely flat, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and torso as upright as possible.
Drive through the front of your heels while maintaining your torso angle. Push your knees out so they do not block the path of the bar.
Once the bar clears your knees, drive your hips forward toward the bar to fully lock out your hips and knees.
Clean_Pull: Position the barbell against your shins, using an overhand or hook grip slightly wider than your legs. Drop your hips, keep your weight on your heels, back straight, chest up, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: Drive through your heels and extend your knees, maintaining your torso angle with straight arms and elbows pointed out. Lift the bar with control until it clears your knees.

Second pull (the main explosion): As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jump-like motion without pulling with your arms. At the finish, your body should be fully extended and leaning slightly back.
Extend sharply and powerfully without dragging out the extension longer than necessary.
Clean_Shrug: Grip the barbell with an overhand or hook grip at shoulder width, holding the bar at mid-thigh level. Keep your back straight with a slight forward lean.
Shrug your shoulders forcefully straight up toward your ears. You can typically use heavier weight than your clean, but not so heavy that the movement slows down.
Clean_from_Blocks: Set the barbell on blocks at the desired height, taking an overhand or hook grip slightly wider than your legs. Lower your hips, keep your weight on your heels, back straight, chest up, and shoulders slightly ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
Drive through your heels and extend your knees, keeping your back angle constant, arms straight, and elbows turned out.
Once extended, shrug powerfully, pull your elbows up and out, and drop underneath the bar, whipping your elbows forward under the bar.
Catch the barbell in a front squat across the front of your shoulders near your throat with relaxed wrists, sinking into the bottom position.
Immediately drive through your heels to stand up with an upright torso and high elbows. Return the bar to the blocks for the next rep.
Deficit_Deadlift: Stand on a 2.5–7.5 cm platform or weight plates with the barbell over the middle of your feet, hip-width apart.
Hinge at your hips and grip the bar at shoulder width with your shoulder blades spread apart. Use a double overhand grip, or switch to a mixed grip for heavy sets.
Take a deep breath, drop your hips, and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look forward, keep your chest high, and arch your lower back. Drive through your heels to start the lift.
Once the bar passes your knees, pull it back aggressively by squeezing your shoulder blades together and driving your hips forward to lock out.
Lower the barbell under control by hinging at your hips and returning it to the floor.
Double_Leg_Butt_Kick: Stand tall with your knees slightly bent.
Quickly dip down by bending your hips and knees, then immediately explode into the air as high as you can.
In midair, bend your knees and pull your heels up, trying to touch your glutes.
Land softly on slightly bent knees, using your legs to absorb the impact.
Dumbbell_Floor_Press: Lie on your back on the floor holding dumbbells, with your knees comfortably bent. Press the dumbbells straight up above your chest.
Lower the dumbbells until your upper arms touch the floor. Keep your elbows tucked to target your triceps, or flare them out wider to focus on your chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then press the dumbbells back up, bringing them together at the top.
Dumbbell_Seated_Box_Jump: Place a box about 60 cm in front of a bench. Hold a dumbbell with both hands against your chest and sit on the bench facing the box. This is your starting position.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor, lean forward, and explosively extend your hips and knees to jump up and forward.
Land softly on top of the box on both feet, absorbing the impact by bending your hips and knees.
Step down safely from the box and return to the starting position.
Fast_Skipping: Stand in a relaxed stance with one foot slightly in front of the other. This is your starting position.
Perform skips using a step-hop pattern: right-right-step, left-left-step, alternating sides.
For fast skipping, stay low to the ground, keep your air time minimal, and move as quickly as possible.
Floor_Press: Set the rack pins at an appropriate height. Lie on the floor inside the rack with your head near the uprights. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and unrack the barbell.
Lower the bar toward your lower chest or upper abdomen, gripping the bar tightly as if pulling it apart, with your elbows tucked. Pause briefly when your upper arms touch the floor without bouncing.
Press the bar up explosively, keeping the barbell, wrists, and elbows aligned in a vertical path.
Floor_Press_with_Chains: Set the power rack pins to the appropriate height. Hang the chains on the ends of the barbell so they don't touch the weight plates.
Lie on the floor with your head toward the edge of the rack. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and unrack the bar.

Lower the bar toward your lower chest or upper abdomen, squeezing the bar as if pulling it apart and keeping your elbows tucked. Pause when your upper arms touch the floor, without bouncing or slamming the weight.
Press the bar up as fast as possible, keeping the bar, wrists, and elbows in line.
Frankenstein_Squat: This exercise teaches proper bar and body positioning for the clean and front squat.

Rest the barbell across the front of your shoulders, release your grip, and extend your arms straight forward. Push your shoulders forward to create a shelf, with the bar touching your throat. Move only your shoulder blades without rounding your back.
Squat down by bending your hips and knees, sitting down between your legs. Keep your torso upright, arms up, shoulders forward, and the bar still. Lower until your hamstrings touch your calves.
Stand back up by driving through the front of your heels and extending your knees and hips.
Glute_Ham_Raise: Adjust the machine to fit your body. Lie face down with your feet secured on the platform between the rollers, knees positioned just behind the pad.
Start from the bottom position. Keeping an arch in your back, bend your knees while pressing your toes into the platform. Keep your torso straight and pull yourself up to a vertical position.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Good_Morning: Set the barbell on the rack at shoulder height. Rest it across your rear delts as in a power squat, rather than on top of your shoulders. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades squeezed together, and knees slightly bent.
