Step back from the rack. Hinging at your hips and pushing them back, bend forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep an arch in your lower back and your neck aligned with your spine.
Extend your hips by driving through your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position.
Good_Morning_off_Pins: Set the barbell on the safety pins at about belly height. Bend under the bar and place it across your rear delts as in a power squat; your torso should be nearly parallel to the floor.
Keep your back tight and arched, shoulder blades squeezed together, knees slightly bent, and neck in line with your spine.
Extend your hips using your glutes and hamstrings to stand all the way up with the barbell.
Slowly lower the barbell back onto the pins to return to the starting position.
Groiners: Get into a push-up position on the floor. This is your starting position.
Jump both feet forward next to your hands, keeping your head up.
Jump back to the starting position and repeat immediately for 10–20 reps.
Hang_Clean: Grip the barbell with an overhand or hook grip at shoulder width, letting the bar hang at mid-thigh level. Keep your back straight and slightly leaned forward.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar upward, shrugging your shoulders toward your ears at the same time.
Immediately stand up by driving through your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows high, until fully extended.
Hang_Clean_-_Below_the_Knees: Grip the barbell with an overhand or hook grip at shoulder width, letting the bar hang just below your knees. Keep your back straight and slightly leaned forward.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar upward, shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. Once fully extended, bend your arms, pulling your elbows up and out.
Quickly drop under the bar, rotating your elbows under and around the bar. Catch it in a front squat on your shoulders near your throat with relaxed wrists, and descend to the bottom position.
Immediately stand up by driving through your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows high, until fully extended.
Hanging_Bar_Good_Morning: Suspend the barbell from chains or straps on the rack at about belly height.
Duck under the bar and place it across your rear delts as in a power squat, not on your traps. At the proper height, your torso will be nearly parallel to the floor.
Keep your back tight and arched, shoulder blades squeezed together, knees slightly bent, and neck aligned with your spine.
Extend your hips using your glutes and hamstrings to stand all the way up with the barbell.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position until the chains support the weight again.
Heaving_Snatch_Balance: This exercise helps you master the snatch. Hold a light barbell across your rear delts with your feet slightly wider than hip-width, toes turned out as in a squat stance.
Dip slightly at the knees and drive up explosively to momentarily unload the bar. Drop under it, pressing the bar overhead and sinking into a full squat.
Stand back up while keeping the bar stabilized overhead.
Hip_Lift_with_Band: Secure a suitable resistance band on both sides of a power rack and lie down in the middle. If there are no band pegs, anchor the band with heavy dumbbells or similar sturdy objects to prevent shifting.
Position yourself so the band runs directly across your hips. Bend your knees with your feet flat on the floor. Rest your arms on the floor or hold the band in place.
Keeping your shoulders on the floor, drive through your heels and raise your hips as high as possible, stretching the band.
Pause at the top, then lower yourself back to the starting position.
Inchworm: Stand with your feet together. Keeping your legs straight, hinge forward and place your palms on the floor directly in front of you. This is your starting position.
Slowly walk your hands forward, alternating left and right, hinging only at the hips while keeping your legs straight.
Continue until your body forms a straight line parallel to the floor in a push-up position.
Without moving your hands, take short steps of a few inches toward them until your feet reach your hands. Keep your legs straight throughout.
Isometric_Chest_Squeezes: Sitting or standing, bend your arms to 90 degrees and bring your palms together in front of your chest. Keep your hands open with your fingers pointing forward.
Press your palms firmly against each other, engaging your chest. Start with light pressure and gradually increase it, breathing evenly.
Hold for the target number of seconds, then slowly release the tension.
Jerk_Balance: This exercise teaches you to drop deeper into the split jerk and corrects shifting backward. Hold the barbell on your shoulders in the jerk rack position: shoulders forward, torso upright, and feet in a shallow split stance.
Start like a standard jerk: dip at the knees with an upright torso and drive up powerfully, lifting the weight using momentum rather than your arms.
Keep your back foot planted: push off it as you drop forward into a full split and drive the bar overhead. Stand up while maintaining the weight overhead.
Jerk_Dip_Squat: This exercise reinforces the dip in the jerk. Hold the barbell on your shoulders in the jerk rack position: shoulders pushed forward into a shelf, with the bar lightly touching your throat.
Place your feet under your hips with your toes turned out comfortably. Keeping your torso upright, dip by bending your knees forward without pushing your hips back. Keep the dip shallow.
Drive powerfully through your feet to return to the starting position.
Knee_Circles: Stand tall with your feet together and hands on your hips.
Rotate your knees in smooth circles, breathing evenly.
Knee_Tuck_Jump: Stand comfortably with your knees slightly bent. Hold your hands in front of your chest, palms facing down, and fingertips touching. This is your starting position.
Quickly perform a quarter squat and immediately jump up explosively, tucking your knees toward your chest and trying to touch your palms.
Jump as high as possible. As you land, extend your legs slightly and absorb the impact by bending your knees again.
Kneeling_Squat: Set the bar in a power rack at the appropriate height. Kneel behind the bar, placing an exercise mat under your knees if needed.
Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders with your shoulder blades retracted and the bar firmly against your back. Unrack the bar.
Looking straight ahead, lower your hips backward until your glutes touch your calves.
Drive your hips forward to return your torso to an upright position.
Lateral_Bound: Stand in a quarter squat sideways to the direction of movement. This is your starting position.
Make a countermovement by shifting your lead leg inward and loading your outside leg.
Immediately push off and extend your body, jumping sideways as far as you can.
Upon landing, immediately push off in the opposite direction to return to the starting spot. Continue bounding back and forth.
Muscle_Snatch: Hold the barbell with a wide grip at mid-thigh level. Place your feet under your hips, turning your toes slightly out as needed.
Lower your hips with your chest lifted, eyes forward, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
Start the pull by driving through the front of your heels. In the second pull, extend your hips, knees, and ankles as quickly as possible, keeping the barbell close to your body.
Continue driving the bar overhead into a lockout without re-bending your knees or dipping under the bar.
Olympic_Squat: Rest the barbell on top of your traps. Keep your chest lifted, eyes forward, feet hip-width apart, and toes turned out slightly as needed.
Lower down by bending your knees with minimal backward hip shift. Track your knees forward over your toes and keep your torso as upright as possible.
Squat all the way down, keeping your weight over the front of your heels. Once your hamstrings touch your calves, drive up powerfully.
Pin_Presses: The pin press eliminates the eccentric phase to build starting strength while letting you work through a specific range of motion.
Place a flat bench inside a power rack and set the safety pins to your target height: anywhere from near full lockout to an inch off your chest. Rest the barbell on the pins.

Lie on the bench so the bar lines up over your standard touchpoint. Plant your feet, arch your upper back, squeeze your shoulder blades, and drive through your legs to anchor your traps into the bench.
Use your standard grip, or shoulder-width to target the triceps. Keep the bar, wrists, and elbows aligned, gripping the bar tightly as if trying to snap it apart.
Press the bar up as explosively as possible, keeping your elbows tucked until full lockout. Return the bar to the pins and pause before the next rep.
Plyo_Push-up: Get into a plank position on your palms and toes: arms straight, hands roughly shoulder-width apart, and body forming a straight line. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor.
At the bottom, push off explosively by extending your arms so your hands leave the floor.
Land softly back in the starting position and repeat.
Variation: to make it harder, clap your hands while in midair.
Power_Clean_from_Blocks: Place the barbell on blocks at the desired height, gripping it slightly wider than your legs. Lower your hips with your weight on your heels, back flat, eyes forward, chest lifted, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: drive through your heels to extend your knees, maintaining your torso angle and keeping your arms straight. As the bar reaches mid-thigh, begin extending your hips.

Jump-shrug explosively by extending your hips, knees, and ankles without pulling with your arms. At the end of the second pull, your body should be fully extended and leaning slightly back with arms straight.
Third pull: shrug aggressively, pull your elbows up and out, and dip under the bar just enough to catch it on your front shoulders near your throat.
Stand up immediately by driving through your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows high. Return the bar to the blocks.
Lower_Back_Curl: Lie on your stomach with your arms extended out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Use your lower back muscles to extend your spine, lifting your chest off the floor. Do not push off with your arms, and keep your head raised. Complete 10–20 reps.
Rear_Leg_Raises: Get on all fours on a mat. Look forward with your knees bent at 90° between your hamstrings and calves. This is your starting position.
Raise one leg up and back, extending your knee and hip. Complete 5–10 reps, then switch sides.
Recumbent_Bike: Sit on the recumbent bike and adjust the seat for your height.
Select manual mode or a program from the menu; you may need to start pedaling to power it on. You can usually enter your age and weight to track calories.
You can adjust the resistance throughout your workout. Use the handlebars to monitor your heart rate and maintain the right intensity.
Rowing_Stationary: Sit on the machine with your heels resting comfortably against the base of the footplates and the straps secured. Choose a program if needed. Sit tall and hinge forward at your hips.
The first phase is the catch: knees bent and tucked toward your chest, torso leaning slightly forward while keeping proper posture.

Push off the footplates by extending your legs, then pull the handle toward your upper abdomen while drawing your shoulders back. Drive primarily through your legs and hips to avoid straining your back.
The recovery phase: straighten your arms, bend your knees, and hinge your torso forward again to return to the catch position.
Running_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and select manual mode or a program from the menu. You can usually enter your age and weight to track calories. Adjust the incline to change the intensity.
The treadmill is convenient, great for your heart, and typically lower-impact than running outside.
Run with good posture. Hold onto the handrails only when necessary, such as when stepping off or checking your heart rate.
Scissor_Kick: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat. Fully extend your arms out to the sides with your palms facing down, keeping them still throughout the exercise.
Slightly bend your knees and lift your legs so your heels are about 15 cm off the floor. This is your starting position.
Raise your left leg to about 45° while lowering your right leg until your heel is 5–8 cm off the floor.
Switch legs by raising your right leg and lowering your left. Remember to breathe continuously.
Side_Leg_Raises: Stand next to a chair so you can hold onto it for support. Balance on one leg. This is your starting position.
Keeping your leg straight, swing it out to the side as high as you comfortably can, then swing it down across the front of your standing leg.
Perform 5–10 swings, gradually increasing your range of motion.
Stairmaster: Step onto the stepper and select manual mode or a program from the menu. You can usually enter your age and weight to track calories.
Pace your steps rhythmically up and down, pushing the pedals without letting them bottom out. Hold onto the handrails for balance and to monitor your heart rate.
The stepper is convenient, great for your heart, and typically lower-impact than running outdoors, but it is much more demanding than other cardio machines.
Standing_Hip_Circles: Stand on one leg, holding onto a sturdy vertical support.
Raise your free knee to 90°. This is your starting position.
Open your hip out as wide as you can, tracing a large circle with your knee.
Perform the movement slowly for the target number of reps, then repeat on the other side.
Step_Mill: Step onto the revolving stair climber and select manual mode or a program from the menu. You can usually enter your age and weight to track calories.
Climb the steps carefully to avoid tripping. Hold onto the handrails for balance.
The stair climber is convenient, great for your heart, and typically lower-impact than outdoor running, but it is significantly more challenging than other cardio machines.
Stomach_Vacuum: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands on your hips. This is your starting position.
Take a slow, deep breath in, then exhale completely, pulling your stomach in as far as possible, and hold. Imagine your belly button touching your spine.
Hold for about 20 seconds while trying to breathe normally. Then inhale and release your stomach back to the starting position.
Tip: once you master the technique, increase the hold beyond 20 seconds, working your way up to 40–60 seconds.
Toe_Touchers: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your arms along your sides, palms facing down.
Bring your legs together and slowly raise them until they are almost perpendicular to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your knees. Your feet should be parallel to the floor.
Extend your arms straight up at a 45° angle to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your lower back pressed to the floor, exhale and slowly lift your upper torso, reaching your hands toward your toes.
Inhale as you slowly lower your torso and arms back to the starting position. Keep your arms straight and pointing toward your toes throughout the rep.
Power_Snatch_from_Blocks: Place the barbell on blocks. Take a wide grip with your feet hip-width apart and toes pointed slightly out. Lower your hips, keep your chest up, look straight ahead, position your shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and point your elbows out. This is your starting position.
Drive through the front of your heels to lift the bar off the blocks. Then, extend your hips, knees, and ankles as explosively as possible, keeping the bar close to your body.
At the peak of full extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.
Shift your feet slightly wider than hip-width and aggressively pull yourself under the bar, driving it overhead. Catch it on locked-out arms in a power position, above a full squat.
Keeping the bar over the front of your heels and your head and chest up, drive through your heels to stand fully upright. Carefully lower the bar back onto the blocks.
Push_Press_-_Behind_the_Neck: Stand with the barbell resting across the back of your shoulders and your feet hip-width apart. Begin the dip by bending your knees without shifting your hips back. Dip down just slightly, then reverse direction as explosively as possible.
Drive through your heels to accelerate the bar vertically. Use that upward momentum to press the weight overhead until your arms are fully locked out.
Lower the bar back to the starting position, absorbing the impact with your legs.
Rack_Delivery: This exercise teaches you how to receive the bar on your shoulders. Hold the bar in a scarecrow position: upper arms parallel to the floor, forearms hanging straight down. Use a hook grip, wrapping your fingers over your thumbs.

Rotate your elbows around the bar to rack it across your shoulders, loosening your grip as your elbows drive forward. Form a shelf with your front deltoids, allowing the bar to lightly touch your throat.
Keep the bar close to your body at all times; with heavier weights, any gap will cause it to crash onto you. Once the movement feels smooth, you can increase speed and weight.
Rack_Pull_with_Bands: Set the barbell on the power rack safety pins just below the knees, just above them, or at mid-thigh level.
Anchor resistance bands to the base of the rack or heavy dumbbells, and attach the other ends to the barbell. Loop the bands if needed to create adequate tension.
Step up to the bar in a deadlift stance: feet hip-width apart, grip shoulder-width apart, back arched, and hips pushed back. For heavy weights, use a mixed grip, hook grip, or lifting straps.
Looking straight ahead, extend your hips and knees while pulling the bar up and back to full lockout, pulling your shoulders back at the top. Lower the bar back onto the pins and repeat.
Rack_Pulls: Set the barbell on the power rack safety pins just below the knees, just above them, or at mid-thigh level.
Step up to the bar in a deadlift stance: feet hip-width apart, grip shoulder-width apart, back arched, and hips pushed back. For heavy weights, use a mixed grip, hook grip, or lifting straps.
Looking straight ahead, extend your hips and knees while pulling the bar up and back to full lockout, pulling your shoulders back at the top.
Lower the bar back onto the pins and repeat.
Reverse_Band_Bench_Press: Place a bench inside the power rack and set the barbell at the desired height. Attach resistance bands to band pegs or the top of the rack directly above the bar, and loop the other ends around the barbell.

Lie on the bench, tuck your feet underneath you, and arch your back. Holding the bar, lift your shoulders, retract your shoulder blades, and drive with your legs to pin your traps into the bench. Place your hands so your palms cover the ring marks on the bar.

Unrack the bar without letting your shoulders roll forward, gripping the bar tightly as if trying to pull it apart. Lower the bar to your lower chest or upper abs, keeping the bar, wrists, and elbows stacked.
Touch your torso, pause briefly, and press the bar up as explosively as possible. Keep your elbows tucked until your arms are fully extended.
Reverse_Band_Box_Squat: Step into a power rack and place a box of the desired height behind you. Attach resistance bands to band pegs or the top of the rack directly above the bar, and loop the other ends around the barbell.
Rest the barbell across your rear delts, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and rotate your elbows forward as if bending the bar. Unrack the bar with a tight lower back arch and step back.
A wide stance places more emphasis on your back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, while a narrow stance targets the quads. Look straight ahead.

Keeping your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees out and sit back until you are seated on the box with vertical shins. Pause briefly by relaxing your hip flexors, without bouncing off the box.
Keep your weight on your heels and knees pushed out, then drive explosively off the box leading with your head and maintaining full-body tension. Carefully re-rack the bar.
Rocket_Jump: Stand relaxed with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Lower into a half squat and explosively jump straight up as high as possible.
Fully extend your body, reaching your hands up as high as you can. Land softly, absorbing the impact with your legs.
Romanian_Deadlift_from_Deficit: Stand upright holding the barbell in front of you with arms fully extended. Stand on a raised platform or weight plate to increase the range of motion.

Slightly bend your knees and hinge at the hips, pushing them as far back as possible and lowering your torso as far as your flexibility allows. Keep your back flat at all times and the bar close to your legs.
You should feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings. Return to the starting position.
Scissors_Jump: Start in a lunge: your front knee is bent directly over midfoot, and your back knee is hovering just above the floor.
Extend both legs and swing your arms to jump as high as you can.
Switch your legs in midair, bringing the front leg back and the rear leg forward.
Land softly back into a lunge, absorbing the impact with your legs, and repeat.
Seated_Good_Mornings: Place a box inside the power rack and set the safety pins to the desired height. Rest the barbell across your rear delts rather than your traps. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward as if bending the bar.
Unrack the bar with a tight arch in your lower back, looking straight ahead. Keeping your back, shoulders, and core tight, sit back onto the box. This is your starting position.
Keeping the bar tight against your back, hinge forward at the hips as low as you can. The safety pins set around parallel will serve as a safety stop and cue your depth.
Pause just above the pins, then return to the upright seated position.
Single_Leg_Butt_Kick: Stand on one leg with the other leg lifted and knee bent. This is your starting position.
Dip slightly and jump straight up, extending the hip, knee, and ankle of your standing leg.
Immediately bend the knee of your jumping leg, aiming to kick your heel toward your glute.
Bring the leg back down slightly bent under your hips to absorb the landing. Keep the other leg in roughly the same position throughout.
Sumo_Deadlift: Step up to the barbell on the floor so the bar is over the middle of your feet. Set your feet very wide, almost touching the collars. Hinge at your hips and grip the bar.
Keep your arms directly under your shoulders inside your legs, using an overhand, mixed, or hook grip. Relax your shoulders to lengthen your arms.

Inhale, lower your hips, look forward, and keep your chest lifted. Drive through the floor by pushing your feet outward, keeping your weight on the back half of your feet, and extend your hips and knees.
Once the bar passes your knees, lean back slightly and drive your hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell back to the floor by hinging at your hips and controlling the weight.
Sumo_Deadlift_with_Bands: Loop short resistance bands over the barbell and step into them so they sit under the back half of your feet, right where you push into the floor.

Position the bar over midfoot with your feet very wide, nearly at the collars. Hinge at your hips and grip the bar inside your legs with your arms under your shoulders, using an overhand, mixed, or hook grip.
Inhale, drop your hips, look ahead, and keep your chest up. Drive through the floor by spreading your feet, keeping your weight on the back half of your feet, and extend your hips and knees.
Once the bar passes your knees, lean back slightly and drive your hips forward to the bar, bringing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell to the floor by hinging at your hips with full control of the weight.
Sumo_Deadlift_with_Chains: Attach chains to the ends of the barbell or drape them over the center of the bar to increase resistance. Keep the ends of the chains away from the plates so they do not catch on the descent.

Position the bar over the middle of your feet with a very wide stance, almost touching the collars. Hinge at your hips, relax your shoulders, and grip the bar inside your legs under your shoulders using an overhand, mixed, or hook grip.
Inhale, lower your hips, look forward, and keep your chest up. Drive through the floor by spreading your feet, keeping your weight on the back half of your feet, and extend your hips and knees.
As the bar clears your knees, lean back slightly and drive your hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell to the floor by hinging at your hips under control.
Vertical_Swing: Hold a dumbbell with both hands, letting your arms hang between your legs. Keep your back straight and your head up.
Swing the dumbbell back between your legs by hinging at your hips and bending your knees slightly.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, jumping up and driving the dumbbell overhead.
Cushion the landing with your legs as you bring the dumbbell back toward your torso before the next rep.
Wide_Stance_Stiff_Legs: Take a wide stance by the barbell on the floor, hinge at your hips, and grab the bar. Push your hips back as far as possible with your legs nearly straight, keeping your back flat and your head and chest up. This is your starting position.
Drive your hips forward with your arms straight until you stand up fully.
Slowly return to the starting position. For the following reps, you do not need to let the barbell touch the floor.
90_90_Hamstring: Lie on your back with one leg extended flat on the floor.
Bend your other hip and knee to a 90-degree angle, supporting the leg with your hands if needed. This is your starting position.
Extend your leg straight up, pause for a moment, and return to the starting position.
All_Fours_Quad_Stretch: Get on all fours, lift one foot off the floor, and grab it with your hand.
Holding your foot or ankle with your knee fully bent, stretch your quad and hip flexors.
Work on extending your hip by pushing it toward the floor. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Bicycling_Stationary: Sit on the stationary bike and adjust the seat height to fit your body.
Select a mode from the menu—you may need to start pedaling to turn it on. Choose manual mode or a preset program.
You can usually enter your age and weight to estimate calories burned. Adjust the resistance throughout your workout.
Use the handgrip sensors to monitor your heart rate and stay at your target intensity.
Elliptical_Trainer: Step onto the elliptical trainer and select manual mode or a preset program from the menu.
You can usually enter your age and weight to estimate calories burned. Adjust the incline to change your workout intensity.
The handlebar sensors monitor your heart rate to help you maintain the right intensity.
Front_Leg_Raises: Stand next to a chair or another sturdy support and hold on with one hand.
Swing your straight leg forward, then down and back as far as your flexibility allows. Do 5–10 reps, then switch legs.
Hip_Circles_prone: Get on all fours. Keeping good posture, lift one bent knee off the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your knee bent, rotate your hip in an arc, aiming to trace a large circle with your knee.
Perform the prescribed number of reps slowly, then switch to the other side.
Jogging_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and choose manual mode or a program from the menu. You can usually enter your age and weight to track calories. Adjust the incline to change intensity.
The treadmill is convenient, great for cardiovascular health, and generally has less impact than outdoor jogging.
Jog with good posture. Hold onto the handrails only when necessary, such as when stepping off or checking your heart rate.
Snatch: Place your feet shoulder-width apart with the barbell over the balls of your feet.
Bend your knees, keep your back flat, and grasp the barbell with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width. Lower your hips as if sitting into a chair. This is your starting position.
Push through your feet into the floor and lift the barbell close to your legs. At mid-thigh, explosively push off the floor and extend fully.
As the barbell rises, shrug your shoulders back, flare your elbows out to the sides, and keep them above the bar as long as possible.
Quickly and aggressively drop under the barbell, catch it on locked-out arms overhead in a squat, and stand up. Finish with your feet in line and arms fully extended.
Snatch_Balance: Stand with your feet in a pulling stance, the barbell across the back of your shoulders, and grip it with a wide snatch grip.
Dip sharply and drive through your knees to pop the barbell up, then aggressively drop under it while shifting your feet into your receiving stance.
Catch the barbell on locked-out arms overhead near the bottom of your squat. Keep your torso upright and let your hips sink between your legs.
Descend into a full squat and stand up. Carefully lower the barbell.
Snatch_Deadlift: This exercise strengthens the first pull of the snatch. With the barbell on the platform, use a wide snatch grip, set your feet hip-width apart, and turn your toes slightly out.
Squat down to the bar, keeping your back completely flat and your gaze forward.
Drive through your heels to begin the lift, raising your hips. Keep your back angle unchanged until the bar passes your knees.
Then drive your hips forward to the bar as you stand upright. Lower the barbell back to the platform in reverse motion.
Snatch_Shrug: Hold the barbell with a wide grip—using a hook grip or overhand grip—with the bar at mid-thigh level. Keep your back flat and slightly leaned forward.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears. You can typically use more weight than your snatch, but not so heavy that it slows down the movement.
Speed_Box_Squat: Attach resistance bands to the barbell, securing them firmly near the floor. You can loop them for added tension.
Set up a box at an appropriate height. Choose a challenging weight that does not compromise your speed—typically 50–70% of your one-rep max.
Rest the bar across your upper back with your shoulder blades pulled together, your back arched, and your entire body tight. This is your starting position.
Unrack the barbell and step in front of the box. Sit back with control onto the box without plopping down.
Pause briefly, then explosively stand up from the box by extending your hips and knees.
Split_Clean: Start with the barbell on the floor against your shins, using an overhand grip just outside your legs. Lower your hips, keep your weight on your heels, back flat, chest up, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: drive through your heels and extend your knees, keeping your back angle constant and arms straight, lifting the bar under control past your knees.

Second pull: at mid-thigh, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jump-like motion without pulling with your arms. Then shrug your shoulders hard and bend your elbows high and out to the sides.
Drop under the bar, rotating your elbows forward, and catch it in a split stance—one foot forward, one back—across your front shoulders near your collarbones with relaxed wrists.
Sink to the bottom of the split and immediately stand up by driving through your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows high, then step your feet back together.
Split_Jerk: Stand with the barbell resting across your front shoulders and feet hip-width apart, then start the dip by bending your knees straight down without shifting your hips back.
Dip just slightly and explosively reverse direction, driving through your heels. As the bar leaves your shoulders, move your head back out of its path.
As soon as your feet leave the floor, quickly split your stance—one foot forward, one back, with knees slightly bent. Drive the bar up while dropping your body underneath it.
Catch the barbell on locked-out arms overhead. Step your feet back together to stand fully upright.
Split_Jump: Step into a lunge with your front knee bent over mid-foot and your back knee hovering just above the floor.
Drive through both legs and swing your arms to jump as high as possible.
Bring your legs together in midair, then return them to the split position as you land.
Absorb the impact by sinking smoothly back into the starting lunge.
Squat_with_Bands: Loop resistance bands over the barbell sleeves and secure the opposite ends to pegs, the rack, or heavy dumbbells to create the desired tension.
Rest the bar across your rear shoulders, pinch your shoulder blades together, and rotate your elbows forward as if bending the bar. Unrack the bar with an arched lower back and step back.
Take a wide stance to shift more work to your back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings. Keep your gaze forward.

Keeping your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees out and sit your hips back as far as possible, ideally keeping your shins vertical. The lower the bar sits, the more your torso will lean forward.
Descend until your hip crease is level with the top of your knees. Keeping your weight on your heels and pushing your knees out, drive up explosively, leading with your head and maintaining tension.
Squat_with_Chains: Drape the leader chains over the barbell sleeves and attach the heavy chains using carabiners. Adjust the length so a few links remain on the floor at the top of the lift.
Rest the bar across your rear shoulders, pinch your shoulder blades together, and rotate your elbows forward as if bending the bar. Unrack the bar with an arched lower back and step back.
Take a wide stance to shift more work to your back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings. Keep your gaze forward.

Keeping your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees out and sit your hips back as far as possible, ideally keeping your shins vertical. The lower the bar sits, the more your torso will lean forward.
Descend until your hip crease is level with the top of your knees. Keeping your weight on your heels and pushing your knees out, drive up explosively, leading with your head and maintaining tension.
Standing_Long_Jump: Best performed on sand or another soft surface where you can measure distance. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart in a quarter squat.
With a vigorous arm swing and dip, jump forward as far as possible.
Land softly, reaching your feet as far forward as possible.
Measure the distance from the starting line to your landing point and record your results.
Star_Jump: Stand in a relaxed stance with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.
Lower into a half squat and jump explosively as high as you can, fully extending your body and spreading your arms and legs out to the sides.
As you land, bring your arms and legs back in and absorb the impact with your knees.
Power_Snatch: Place the barbell on the floor close to your shins and take a wide grip. Position your feet hip-width apart with your toes turned out. Lower your hips, keep your chest up, look forward, and keep your shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: drive through the front of your heels and lift the bar off the floor. Maintain your back angle until the bar passes your knees.
Second pull: explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles while keeping the bar close to your body. At the peak, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.
Shift your feet slightly wider and drop underneath the bar, driving it overhead. Catch it in a partial squat and lock it out on straight arms.
Stand up fully while keeping the barbell locked out overhead.
Reverse_Band_Deadlift: Set up a barbell in a power rack. Secure resistance bands to the top of the rack on hooks or the frame, and loop the other ends around the bar.

Stand with the bar over your midfoot and feet hip-width apart. Hinge forward and grip the bar shoulder-width apart, keeping your shoulder blades spread. Use a double overhand grip, or switch to a mixed grip on heavier sets.
Take a deep breath, lower your hips, and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look forward with your chest open and back arched. Drive through your heels to lift the bar.
As the bar passes your knees, pull it back forcefully, bringing your shoulder blades together and driving your hips forward.
Lower the bar back to the floor by hinging at your hips and guiding it down.
Reverse_Band_Power_Squat: Set the safety pins and barbell at the appropriate height in a power rack. Once the bar is loaded, attach bands to the top of the rack on hooks or the frame, and loop the other ends around the bar.

Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward. Unrack the bar, create a strong arch in your lower back, step back, and take a wide stance.

Look forward. Keeping your back, shoulders, and core braced, push your knees out and sit your hips back as far as possible. Keep your shins perpendicular to the floor; lean your torso forward more if using a low bar position.
Squat down below parallel until the crease of your hips is below the tops of your knees.
Keeping your weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees outward, drive up forcefully with your head leading the movement and your entire body braced to return to the starting position.
Reverse_Band_Sumo_Deadlift: Place a loaded barbell on the floor inside a power rack. Secure bands to the top of the rack on hooks or the frame, and attach the other ends to the bar.

Stand with the bar over your midfoot and set your feet very wide, close to the collars. Hinge down and grip the bar directly under your shoulders, inside your legs. Use a double overhand, mixed, or hook grip.
Relax your shoulders as if lengthening your arms. Inhale, drop your hips, look forward, and keep your chest lifted.

Drive into the floor as if spreading it apart with your feet, keeping your weight on your heels, and extend your hips and knees. Once the bar passes your knees, lean back slightly and drive your hips forward, bringing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the bar back to the floor with control by hinging at your hips.
Snatch_from_Blocks: Rest the barbell on blocks at the desired height and take a wide grip. Place your feet hip-width apart with your toes pointed out. Lower your hips, chest up, eyes forward, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and elbows turned out. This is your starting position.
First pull: drive through the front of your heels and lift the bar off the blocks.
Second pull: explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles while keeping the bar close to your body. At the peak, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.
Shift your feet slightly wider than your hips and aggressively drop underneath the bar, driving it overhead. Catch it in a deep squat with your arms fully locked out.
Keeping the bar over the front of your heels and your chest and head up, drive through your heels to stand up. Carefully return the bar to the blocks.
Split_Snatch: Place the barbell on the floor close to your shins and take a wide grip. Position your feet hip-width apart with your toes turned out. Lower your hips, keep your chest up, look forward, and keep your shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
First pull: drive through the front of your heels and lift the bar off the floor. Maintain your back angle until the bar passes your knees.
Second pull: explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles while keeping the bar close to your body. At the peak, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.
Aggressively drop underneath the bar, splitting your legs dynamically into a lunge with one foot forward and the other back. Catch the bar as low as possible on fully locked-out arms.
Keeping the bar over the front of your heels and your head and chest up, drive through your heels to stand up and bring your feet together. Carefully lower the bar to the floor.
Lying_Crossover: Lie on your back with your legs extended.

Cross one bent leg over your body, aiming to touch your knee to the floor. Have your partner kneel beside you, pinning your opposite shoulder down with one hand and holding your knee with the other. This is your starting position.
Try to lift your bent knee off the floor while your partner holds it firmly in place.
After 10–20 seconds, relax your leg while your partner gently presses your knee closer to the floor. Repeat on the other side.
Lying_Glute: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.
Raise one bent leg and rotate it so your foot rests over your opposite thigh and your shin lies across your body. Have your partner hold your knee and ankle. This is your starting position.
Try to push your leg toward your partner while they keep it from moving.
After 10–20 seconds, relax completely while your partner gently presses your ankle and knee toward your chest.
Caution: let your partner know when the stretch is enough to prevent injury or overstretching.
Lying_Prone_Quadriceps: Lie on your stomach with your partner kneeling beside you. Bend one knee and lift the leg, aiming to bring your foot toward your glutes. Have your partner hold your knee and ankle. This is your starting position.
Try to straighten your knee while your partner resists and keeps your leg in place.
After 10–20 seconds, relax while your partner gently presses your foot closer to your glutes to deepen the stretch in your quadriceps and hip flexors.
Overhead_Triceps: Sit up straight on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm overhead and bend your elbow, trying to touch your upper back with your hand. Have your partner hold your elbow and wrist. This is your starting position.
Try to straighten your arm upward while your partner resists to keep it still.
After 10–20 seconds, relax your arm while your partner applies gentle pressure to your wrist to deepen the triceps stretch. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Seated_Biceps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your partner standing behind you. Reach your straight arms back with palms facing each other. Have your partner hold your wrists. This is your starting position.
Try to bend your elbows while your partner resists and keeps your arms in place.
After 10–20 seconds, relax your arms while your partner gently pulls your wrists upward to stretch your biceps.
Caution: let your partner know when the stretch is enough to prevent injury or overstretching.
Seated_Front_Deltoid: Sit up straight on the floor with your knees bent and your partner standing behind you. Extend your straight arms out to the sides with palms facing down, bringing them as far back as comfortable; have your partner hold your wrists. This is your starting position.
Without bending your elbows, try to bring your arms forward while your partner gently holds them in place for 10–20 seconds.
Then relax while your partner gently deepens the stretch through your shoulders and chest. Hold for 10–20 seconds.
Walking_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and select manual mode or a program from the menu. You can usually enter your age and weight to track calories. Adjust the incline to change the intensity.
Walk at a moderate to brisk pace rather than a leisurely stroll. While walking burns fewer calories than higher-intensity exercise, it is still very beneficial.
Maintain good posture throughout. Hold onto the handrails only when necessary, such as when stepping off the treadmill or checking your heart rate.
Wrist_Circles: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Raise your straight arms out to the sides at shoulder height, parallel to the floor, palms facing down so your body forms a “T”. This is your starting position.
Keeping the rest of your body still, rotate both wrists forward in a circular motion as if drawing circles. Breathe naturally.
Bench_Press_with_Chains: Adjust the leader chain to the desired length and hang the chains onto the ends of the barbell.

Lie on the bench, positioning your head slightly past the bar if possible. Pull your feet back and arch your back. Grasp the bar to lift your shoulders slightly, pull them back, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.

Drive through your feet to press your traps firmly into the bench and maintain this tension throughout the entire movement. Use your preferred grip width, keeping the ring mark on the bar under your palm.

Unrack the barbell without letting your shoulder blades spread apart. Squeeze the bar as if trying to pull it apart, and lower it to your lower chest or upper abdomen. Keep the bar, wrists, and elbows aligned.
Pause briefly once the bar touches your body, then press it up explosively. Keep your elbows tucked until your arms are fully extended.
Box_Squat_with_Bands: Place a box inside the power rack behind you, typically at a height that allows you to squat to parallel. Attach resistance bands to the ends of the barbell and secure them to band pegs, the rack, or heavy dumbbells to set the desired tension.

Step under the bar and rest it across your upper back and rear shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward. Unrack the bar, maintain an arch in your lower back, and take a step back. Look straight ahead.
A wide stance places more emphasis on your back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, while a narrower stance targets your quads.

Keeping your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees outward and hinge your hips back to sit onto the box. Keep your shins perpendicular to the floor. Pause briefly while relaxing your hip flexors, avoiding any bounce.
Keep your weight on your heels, drive your feet and knees outward, and powerfully stand up from the box, leading with your head and keeping your whole body engaged. Carefully re-rack the barbell.
Clean_and_Jerk: Set a barbell on the floor against your shins, gripping it slightly wider than your legs with an overhand or hook grip. Lower your hips, keep your weight on your heels, back flat, chest up, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.

Drive through your heels to lift the bar above your knees, keeping your back angle constant and arms straight. As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jump-like motion.

At peak extension, shrug your shoulders and pull your elbows up and out, then drop under the bar, whipping your elbows forward. Catch the bar on your shoulders in a front squat and descend into the bottom position.

Stand up immediately by driving through your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows high. To prepare for the jerk, position your feet under your hips, perform a shallow dip without shifting your hips back, and aggressively reverse direction.

Drive through your heels and launch the bar overhead, clearing your head out of the way. Quickly split your feet and catch the barbell on locked-out arms overhead. Step your feet together to stand tall.
Deadlift_with_Bands: Loop short resistance bands over the barbell and stand on them. If using long bands, anchor them to a secure base, such as heavy dumbbells or a rack.
With your feet set and hands on the bar, take a deep breath, lower your hips, and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar.

Look straight ahead with your chest open and back arched. Drive through your heels to lift the bar. Once it passes your knees, pull back powerfully, squeezing your shoulder blades and driving your hips forward.
Lower the barbell back to the floor by hinging at your hips and guiding the weight down.
Deadlift_with_Chains: Attach chains to the ends of the barbell, or simply drape their centers over the bar so the weight increases more noticeably as you lift.

Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width apart. Hinge down and grip the bar shoulder-width apart with your shoulder blades spread. Use an overhand grip, switching to a mixed grip for heavy sets.
Take a deep breath, lower your hips, and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look forward with your chest open and lower back arched.
Drive through your heels to lift the barbell. Once the bar passes your knees, pull back forcefully, squeezing your shoulder blades and driving your hips forward.
Lower the bar back to the floor by hinging at your hips and guiding it down.
Hang_Snatch: Grip the barbell with a wide overhand or hook grip. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes turned slightly out, knees soft, torso hinged forward, and back flat, holding the bar at hip level. This is your starting position.
Powerfully extend your legs and hips. At the peak of the extension, shrug your shoulders and allow your elbows to bend outward to the sides.
As you shift your feet into your receiving stance, drop aggressively under the bar, bringing it overhead. Catch the barbell in a deep squat with your arms fully locked out.
Stand up fully while holding the barbell overhead, then lower it to the floor with control.
Hang_Snatch_-_Below_Knees: Grip the barbell with a wide overhand or hook grip. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes turned slightly out, knees soft, torso hinged forward, and back flat, holding the bar just below your knees. This is your starting position.
Powerfully extend your legs and hips. At the peak of the extension, shrug your shoulders and allow your elbows to bend outward to the sides.
As you shift your feet into your receiving stance, drop aggressively under the bar, bringing it overhead. Catch the barbell in a deep squat with your arms fully locked out.
Stand up fully while holding the barbell overhead, then lower it to the floor with control.
Kneeling_Jump_Squat: Kneel on the floor with a barbell resting across your upper back and rear shoulders, or use just your body weight. Using a power rack makes it easier to unrack and rack the bar.
Hinge your hips back until your glutes touch your feet. Keep your chest up and head high.
Explosively drive your hips forward and jump up so you land flat on both feet in a squat.
Complete the squat by driving through your heels and extending your knees to stand up fully.
Overhead_Squat: Stand in front of a barbell on the floor with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and take an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width. Clean or lift the barbell to your chest.
Press the barbell overhead and slightly back on fully locked-out arms. Keep your head up, back flat, and shoulder blades pulled together. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly bend your knees until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat and arms locked out overhead throughout.
Exhale and drive through your legs to return to the starting position.
Power_Jerk: Stand with the barbell resting across your front deltoids, feet hip-width apart. Perform a shallow dip by bending your knees without pushing your hips back, then reverse direction as forcefully as possible.
Drive through your heels to generate maximum speed and power, tilting your head back slightly as the bar leaves your shoulders.
As soon as your feet leave the floor, quickly snap them slightly wider with your knees soft. Catch the barbell on fully locked-out arms overhead.
Seated_Glute: Sit with your knees bent and place one ankle on the opposite knee. Have your partner stand behind you. Lean forward as your partner places their hands on your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Try to lean back for 10–20 seconds while your partner keeps your torso from moving.
Then relax as your partner gently presses your torso forward for 10–20 seconds to deepen the stretch.
Alternate_Leg_Diagonal_Bound: Stand comfortably with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Push off your front foot, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible before landing. Try to cover maximum lateral distance with each bound.
You can use a line on the floor to gauge your lateral distance.
Repeat by pushing off the other leg.
Atlas_Stone_Trainer: This apparatus, made from barbell collars or thick pipe, builds strength for Atlas stones when actual stones are not available.
Load the apparatus with the desired weight. Straddle it with your feet wide, hinge at the hips, and wrap your arms around it.
Lift the weight above your knees by extending your hips. Once it passes your knees, you can lap it by sitting back and pulling it tight against your chest.
Finish the movement by extending your hips and knees to lift the weight as high as possible. Return the weight to your lap or to the floor for the next rep.
Axle_Deadlift: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, placing your feet hip-width apart. Bend over and grip the bar at shoulder width with your shoulder blades spread. An over-under grip is typically used.
Take a deep breath, drop your hips, and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look forward with your chest open and back arched. Drive through your heels to lift the bar.
Once the bar passes your knees, pull it back aggressively, pinching your shoulder blades together and driving your hips forward.
Lower the barbell to the floor by hinging at the hips and guiding it down.
Backward_Drag: Load the sled with the desired weight and attach a rope or straps to hold onto.
Walk backward for the target distance. Lean back and drive through your legs with short, quick steps, moving as fast as possible.
Backward_Medicine_Ball_Throw: This is best done with a partner. If training solo, you can throw and retrieve the ball, or throw it against a wall.
Stand a few meters in front of your partner, facing the same direction. Hold the ball between your legs.
Squat down, then explosively reverse direction, fully extend your body, and throw the ball backward overhead to your partner.
Have your partner roll the ball back to you.
Bear_Crawl_Sled_Drags: Put on a harness or belt and attach the chain behind you so that your back faces the sled. Place your hands on the floor with your back flat and knees bent. This is your starting position.
Drive forward alternately with your left and right legs, using your hands for balance and extra pulling power. Keep your back flat throughout the entire distance.
Bench_Sprint: Stand on the floor and place one foot on a bench or box with your heel near the edge.
Push off through the foot on the bench by extending your hip and knee.
Land with the opposite foot on the bench and return the first foot to the starting position.
Continue alternating legs until the set is complete.
Box_Jump_Multiple_Response: Stand relaxed facing the box or platform, about an arm’s length away. Keep your arms at your sides and knees slightly bent.
Swing your arms to jump up and forward, landing with both feet simultaneously on the box.
Immediately jump or step down back to the starting spot and repeat.
Box_Skip: Set up several boxes in a row, spaced about 2.4 m apart.
Stand facing the first box with one foot slightly behind the other.
Push off with your rear leg, driving your hips up as high as possible.
Immediately upon landing on the box, drive your other leg forward and up to bound off, maximizing height and distance. Land between the boxes on the same foot that landed on the first box.
Step up to the next box and repeat.
Car_Deadlift: The apparatus typically has neutral-grip handles, though some use a straight bar, which you deadlift like a conventional bar. It is loaded with a car, tires, or kegs.
Center yourself between the handles if your squat is stronger, or stand 2 inches back if your deadlift is stronger. Keep your feet hip-width apart.
Bend down and grasp the handles. Take a deep breath, drop your hips, and bend your knees. Look forward with your chest open and back arched.
Drive through your heels to lift the weight, pulling your shoulder blades together and driving your hips forward.
Lower the weight to the floor by hinging at the hips and guiding it down.
Catch_and_Overhead_Throw: Stand facing a wall or your partner.
Bring the ball behind your head with both hands, stretching back as far as comfortable, and throw it forcefully forward.
Follow through with the throw and prepare to catch the rebound. If throwing against a wall, stand close enough to catch the ball and aim slightly higher than you would to a partner.
Linear_Depth_Jump: Place two plyo boxes or benches about 1 meter apart. Stand on one box, facing the other.
Step down softly onto the floor between the boxes, bending your knees and hips to absorb the impact.
Immediately and explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to jump up onto the second box.
Land softly, cushioning the landing with your legs.
Log_Lift: Stand in front of the log and grip the handles. From a bent-over position, pull the log as high as possible toward your chest, then extend your hips and knees to finish the clean.
Tilt your head back and look up, creating a shelf for the log across your chest. Dip slightly by bending your knees, then reverse the motion to drive the log upward.
Extend your arms, pressing the log overhead. There are no strict rules on technique—use whatever is most effective for you. Push your head forward through the window on each rep.
Repeat for the target number of reps. Lower the log back to the floor with control.
Medicine_Ball_Chest_Pass: Find a partner; if working solo, you can use a solid wall instead.
Face your partner, holding the ball with both hands close to your torso.
Draw the ball to your chest and throw it forcefully, extending your arms. For sports performance training, you can step into the throw.
Your partner catches the ball and passes it back. Catch it with both hands at chest height.
Medicine_Ball_Full_Twist: You will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back-to-back with your partner about 60–90 cm apart. This is your starting position.
Hold the ball in front of your torso. Open your hips and turn your shoulders simultaneously with your partner.
To perform a full twist, rotate in the same direction as your partner, such as counter-clockwise.
Pass the ball to your partner, then reverse the motion and twist in the opposite direction together.
Medicine_Ball_Scoop_Throw: Start in a quarter-squat holding a medicine ball with both hands, arms hanging down so the ball is near your feet.
Drive your hips forward, extend your legs, and jump explosively upward.
Simultaneously swing the ball up and over your head with straight arms, releasing it at the peak of your jump. The goal is to throw the ball as far behind you as possible.
Mountain_Climbers: Get into a push-up position, balancing on your hands and toes. Bend one knee and hip to draw your leg forward so your knee is roughly beneath your hips. This is your starting position.
Explosively switch legs: extend the bent leg back onto your toes while driving the opposite knee and hip forward. Alternate back and forth for 20–30 seconds.
Moving_Claw_Series: This exercise develops sprinting technique. While running, flex your knee and aim to bring your heel to your glutes as your hip extends.
As your leg swings forward again, re-engage your quads and actively claw the ground on the next stride.
Pump your arms actively in a quick, rhythmic one-two tempo as you run.
One_Knee_To_Chest: Keep one leg straight and pull the opposite knee toward your chest, clasping your hands behind the knee to protect the kneecap.
Gently draw your knee closer toward your nose.
Switch sides. You will feel a stretch in the glute and lower back of the bent leg and in the hip flexor of the straight leg.
Overhead_Slam: Hold a medicine ball with both hands with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Bring the ball overhead to wind up, extending your body fully.
Quickly reverse direction and slam the ball into the floor directly in front of you with maximum force.
Catch the ball on the rebound with both hands and repeat.
Overhead_Stretch: Stand tall, interlace your fingers, and turn your palms toward the ceiling. Press your arms straight up while keeping your shoulders relaxed down.
To stretch your entire torso, tuck your tailbone down and brace your core. Feel the stretch across both the front and back of your torso.
Pelvic_Tilt_Into_Bridge: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the floor, heels directly under your knees.
Tilt only your tailbone up toward the ceiling to stretch your lower back, keeping the rest of your spine down for now. Draw your belly in.
To press up into a bridge, peel the rest of your spine off the floor, leaving only your neck and shoulders resting on the mat.
Power_Stairs: In this event, heavy implements are walked up a flight of stairs. You can use a tire or a sturdy box for training.
Grip the implement with both hands. Take a wide stance, keeping your chest up and head forward. Drive through your heels and extend your knees and hips to lift the weight off the ground.
Lean back slightly to swing the weight onto the step—typically 40–45 cm high. You can use your legs to help bump it up.
Complete 3–5 reps, then move on to a heavier weight, working as quickly as possible.
Chain_Press: Attach the chains to cable handles. Lie back on a flat bench as if setting up for a dumbbell bench press: use an overhand grip with your arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to lower the chains, letting them partially rest on the floor.
Once your elbows reach a 90-degree angle, press back up until your arms are fully extended.
Chest_Push_from_3_point_stance: Get into a three-point stance: squat down with a flat back and place one hand on the floor. Position the ball directly in front of you.
As you take your first step, pull the ball to your chest and grip it with both hands to set up for the throw.
On your second step, explosively push the ball forward as hard as possible.
Chest_Push_multiple_response: Kneel facing a wall or a partner. Hold the ball firmly against your chest with both hands.
Explosively thrust your hips forward and push the ball away as hard as you can.
Follow through by falling forward onto your hands to catch yourself.
Immediately push back up to the upright kneeling position.
Chest_Push_single_response: Kneel on the floor, holding the ball firmly against your chest with both hands.
Explosively thrust your hips forward and push the ball as far forward as possible.
Follow through by falling forward onto your hands to catch yourself.
Chest_Push_with_Run_Release: Assume an athletic stance: bend your knees, push your hips back, and keep your back straight. Hold the ball near your feet. This is your starting position.
As you take your first step, bring the ball up to your chest.
On your second step, explosively push the ball forward and immediately sprint 9 m. If you are fast enough, try to catch your own throw!
Conans_Wheel: Load the apparatus and secure the arm in a Zercher grip: rest the bar in the crooks of your elbows and clasp one wrist with the other hand. Avoid bearing the load with your forearms.
Lift the weight off the ground and take short, quick steps in a circle, keeping your torso upright and your core braced. Look forward and slightly up, and maintain steady breathing.
Continue walking until you complete one or more full revolutions.
Depth_Jump_Leap: You will need two boxes or benches: one 30–40 cm high and another 55–65 cm high.
Stand on the first box with your arms at your sides, feet together, and toes near the edge. Place the second box about 60–90 cm in front of you.
Step off the box, land softly on the ground, and immediately rebound off both feet.
Explode upward and forward onto the taller box, swinging your arms and fully extending your body. Land softly with knees slightly bent to absorb the impact.
Drop_Push: Place two low boxes or platforms 60–90 cm apart.
Assume a push-up position between them with your hands resting on the boxes.
Keeping your body aligned, push off and drop your hands down to the floor at shoulder width, absorbing the impact with your arms.
Farmers_Walk: Use farmer's walk handles, or use heavy dumbbells or short barbells if specialized equipment is unavailable. Stand between the weights.
Grip the handles firmly and lift the weights by driving through your heels. Keep your back flat and your head up.
Walk forward using short, quick steps while maintaining steady breathing. Cover the target distance, typically 15–30 m, as quickly as you can.
Forward_Drag_with_Press: Attach a chain or rope with two handles to a sled. Face away from the sled, holding a handle in each hand.
Take a step forward, leaning into the movement and driving through your legs and hips. Pause after each step and press your hands forward until your elbows are fully locked out.
Continue stepping forward until you return to the starting position, ready for the next press.
Frog_Hops: Stand with your hands behind your head and lower into a squat, keeping your torso upright and your head up. This is your starting position.
Hop forward about one meter, staying low rather than jumping high. Land softly to absorb the impact and immediately leap into the next jump. Complete 5–10 reps.
Front_Box_Jump: Place a box of suitable height 30–60 cm in front of you. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Dip into a shallow squat to prepare for the jump, swinging your arms back.
Explosively jump as high as you can by extending your hips, knees, and ankles while swinging your arms forward and up.
Land softly on the box with your knees bent to absorb the impact. Jump down or, ideally, step down one foot at a time.
Front_Cone_Hops_or_hurdle_hops: Set up a row of cones or low hurdles about a meter apart.
Stand in front of the first cone with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Jump over the first cone with both feet, swinging both arms for momentum.
Absorb the landing by bending your knees, and immediately jump over the next cone.
Continue until you have jumped over all the cones.
Groin_and_Back_Stretch: Sit on the floor, bend your knees, and bring the soles of your feet together.
Interlace your fingers behind your head. This is your starting position.
Round your back and bend forward, bringing your elbows toward your inner thighs. After a brief pause, return to the starting position with your head up and back straight. Complete 10–20 reps.
Heavy_Bag_Thrust: Stand tall next to a heavy bag in a wide staggered stance. Place your hand on the bag at about chest height. This is your starting position.
Rotate at the waist and push the bag away from you as hard and fast as possible.
As the bag swings back, catch it by reversing the movement.
Hurdle_Hops: Set up a row of hurdles about a meter apart.
Stand in front of the first hurdle with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Jump over the first hurdle with both feet, swinging both arms for momentum.
Absorb the landing by bending your knees, and immediately jump over the next hurdle. Continue until you have jumped over all the hurdles.
Incline_Push-Up_Depth_Jump: You will need a box about 12 inches (30 cm) high and two thick mats or step platforms.
Set the platforms slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and place your feet on the box in a push-up position, with your hands just inside the platforms. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to lower down, then explosively push off the floor. In midair, place your hands onto the platforms, absorbing the landing by bending your elbows.
Repeat the movement to return to the starting position.
Intermediate_Hip_Flexor_and_Quad_Stretch: Lie on your stomach with a rope, strap, or band looped around one foot.
Bend your knee and extend the hip of the leg being stretched by pulling the strap with both hands. Your knee and thigh will lift off the floor, stretching your hip flexors and quads.
Hold for 10–20 seconds, then repeat on the other leg.
Iron_Crosses_stretch: Lie on your stomach with your arms out to the sides and palms flat on the floor. This is your starting position.
Bend one knee and reach that leg behind your back across to the opposite side, trying to touch the floor near your opposite hand.
Quickly return to the starting position and repeat with the other leg. Alternate for 10–20 reps.
Keg_Load: Set up the required number of kegs at a distance from the platform, usually 9–15 m.
Grip the near handle of the first keg, tilt it onto its side, and grab the opposite bottom rim. Lift the keg up to your chest.
The higher you carry the keg, the faster you can move; resting it on your shoulder is usually not allowed. Keep a firm grip and walk to the platform as quickly as possible.
Load the keg onto the platform by extending your hips, knees, and ankles to lift it as high as possible. Return for the next keg and repeat until the exercise is complete.
Lateral_Box_Jump: Stand comfortably next to a low plyo box. This is your starting position.
Quickly dip into a quarter squat to trigger the stretch reflex, then immediately explode up and sideways.
Drive your knees high enough for your feet to clear the box. Land softly in the center of the box, absorbing the impact with your legs.
Carefully step down to the other side of the box and continue jumping back and forth for several reps.
Lateral_Cone_Hops: Set up a row of cones about a meter apart.
Stand at the start of the row, facing sideways to the direction of travel. This is your starting position.
Dip down slightly to trigger the stretch reflex, then immediately jump up and sideways over the cone.
Absorb the landing with your legs and immediately jump over the next cone until you clear the entire row.
Linear_3-Part_Start_Technique: This exercise teaches you how to accelerate into a sprint as quickly as possible from a standstill. It helps to start at a line: stand on it with both feet.
Place the toes of your left foot next to your right ankle, and set your right foot about 10–15 cm behind your left.

Place your right hand on the line and bring your nose close to your left knee. Crouch with a forward lean so your head is lower than your hips and your weight is on your left leg. This is your starting position.
Extend your left arm back parallel to the floor, and when you are ready, sprint forward explosively.
Linear_Acceleration_Wall_Drill: Lean against a wall at about a 45-degree angle. Keep your feet together and glutes engaged.
Quickly drive your right knee up, hold briefly, and forcefully strike your foot straight down into the floor.
Switch legs: drive your left knee up and strike your foot straight down the same way.
Repeat once more with your right leg, and as soon as it hits the floor, alternate legs as quickly as possible.
Prowler_Sprint: Place the sled on a suitable surface and load it so it is challenging to push, but not so heavy that you slow down significantly.
You can use either the high or low handles. Grip the handles with straight arms, leaning your body weight into the sled.
Maintaining good posture, drive into the ground with short, alternating steps. Sprint the short distance as fast as you can.
Quick_Leap: You will need a plyo box. Stand facing it about 1 to 2 feet (30–60 cm) from the edge.
Drive through your hips and jump onto the box with both feet. Land softly on bent knees with your feet flat on the surface.
Immediately upon landing, fully extend your body and swing your arms overhead as you explosively jump off the box. Absorb the landing with your legs.
Return_Push_from_Stance: You will need a partner. Begin in an athletic two- or three-point stance.
On cue, break out into position to receive a pass from your partner.
Catch the ball with both hands and immediately pass it back to your partner.
Variation: Perform this using different running routes.
Rickshaw_Carry: Place the rickshaw frame at the starting point and load it with the desired weight. Stand in the center of the frame, grip the handles, and drive through your heels to lift it. Keep your chest and head up with a straight back.
Immediately begin walking with quick, controlled steps. Keep your chest up, look straight ahead, and breathe steadily.
Once you reach the finish line, lower the frame back down to the ground.
Rickshaw_Deadlift: Load the rickshaw frame with the desired weight. Stand centered between the handles with your feet hip-width apart. Hinge down and grip the handles, letting your shoulder blades spread.
Take a deep breath, lower your hips, and bend your knees. Look forward with your chest open and back flat.
Drive through your heels to lift the weight, pulling your shoulder blades back and driving your hips forward.
Lower the weight back to the floor by hinging at your hips and guiding it down.
Sandbag_Load: Place the sandbags or other implements at a distance from the platform, typically about 15 m away.
Lift the sandbag: bags are awkward, and the technique varies with each bag. Wrap your arms as far around it as possible, then extend your hips and knees to pull it up high.
Shouldering the bag is usually not allowed. Walk as quickly as you can to the platform and load the bag by extending your hips, knees, and ankles. Make sure it does not fall off.
Return for the next bag and repeat until the exercise is complete.
Side_Hop-Sprint: Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle.
Hop laterally over the obstacle and, driving off the ground immediately upon landing, hop back.
Complete the prescribed number of hops as quickly as possible. Immediately transition into a short sprint after the final hop.
Side_Standing_Long_Jump: Stand in an athletic stance with your feet hip-width apart. Keep your head and chest up with your knees and hips slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Leaning to the right, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to jump. Leading with your arms, jump as far to the right as you can.
Land facing the same direction with your feet hip-width apart, absorbing the impact through your legs.
Side_to_Side_Box_Shuffle: Stand beside a plyo box with your left foot placed in the center of the top.
Hop laterally over the box to the other side, landing with your right foot on the box and your left foot on the floor. Swing your arms to help generate momentum.
Continue hopping back and forth across the box.
Single-Leg_Hop_Progression: Set up a row of cones in front of you. Stand relaxed on one leg with the opposite knee lifted. This is your starting position.
Hop forward over the first cone, taking off and landing on the same leg.
Hop from cone to cone, using a quick dip before each takeoff.
At the end, turn around and repeat the progression on the other leg.
Single-Leg_Lateral_Hop: Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle on one leg, with your knee slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Dip down quickly and hop sideways over the cone.
Land on the same leg and immediately hop back to the starting position.
Single-Leg_Stride_Jump: Stand beside a plyo box with your inside foot placed near the edge on top.
Swing your arms upward and drive off the foot on the box to jump as high as you can. Drive your opposite knee up as you jump.
Land back in the starting position, absorbing the impact with the leg on the box.
Single_Leg_Push-off: Stand on the floor with one foot placed on the box so your heel is near the edge.
Push off with the foot on the box, jumping as high as possible through hip and knee extension.
Land with the same foot on the box, bringing the other foot back to the starting position.
Sled_Drag_-_Harness: Load the sled with the desired weight and attach the tow strap. You can pull by holding handles, wearing a harness, or attaching the strap to a belt.
Moving forward or backward, lean in the direction of travel and drive forward by extending your hips and knees.
Sled_Push: Load the sled with the desired weight.
Assume an athletic stance and lean into the sled, gripping the handles with straight arms.
Push the sled as fast as possible, emphasizing hip and knee extension to strengthen your posterior chain.
Sledgehammer_Swings: You will need a tire and a sledgehammer. Stand about 60 cm in front of the tire with a staggered stance. Grip the sledgehammer.
For a right-handed swing: place your left hand at the bottom of the handle and your right hand closer to the head.
As you raise the sledgehammer, slide your right hand toward the head, and as you strike down, slide it toward your left hand. Strike the tire with full force and control the bounce.
Standing_Two-Arm_Overhead_Throw: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball in both hands. Bring the ball deeply behind your head, slightly bending your knees and leaning back.
Explosively throw the ball forward, hinging at your hips and engaging your entire body.
Throw to a partner or against a wall, and catch the ball on the rebound.
Stride_Jump_Crossover: Stand beside the box, placing your inside foot on the box near the edge.
Swing your arms up and push off the box, jumping as high as possible. Drive the opposite knee upward.
Land on the other side of the box in a mirrored position: the foot that was on the box is now on the floor, and the other foot is on the box.
Repeat by jumping back to the other side.
Supine_Chest_Throw: This exercise is great for practicing a chest pass without a partner or a solid wall. Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Place the ball on your chest, holding it from underneath with both hands.
Explosively extend your arms and throw the ball straight up as high as possible.
Catch the ball with both hands as it comes back down.
Supine_One-Arm_Overhead_Throw: Lie on your back with your knees bent. Hold the ball in one hand, extending your arm fully behind your head. This is your starting position.
Initiate the movement from your shoulder and throw the ball straight ahead as far as possible as you sit up.
Throw to a partner or against a wall.
Supine_Two-Arm_Overhead_Throw: Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Hold the ball with both hands, extending your arms fully behind your head. This is your starting position.
Initiate the movement from your shoulders and throw the ball straight ahead as far as possible as you sit up.
Throw to a partner or against a wall.
Tire_Flip: Grip the bottom of the tire by the tread and step your feet back slightly. Rest your chest against the tire.
To lift the tire, extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving it forward and upward.
As the tire reaches a 45-degree angle, step forward and drive your knee into it. Shift your hands to the top of the tire and push forcefully forward to complete the flip.
Yoke_Walk: This is typically performed with a yoke bar, or sometimes with a refrigerator or another heavy object.
Position the yoke across the back of your shoulders. Look straight ahead with an arched back and lift the yoke by driving through your heels.
Walk as fast as possible using short, quick steps. You can hold onto the side posts to keep the yoke steady.
Cover the prescribed distance as quickly as possible, usually 23–30 m.
Adductor: Lie face down with one leg resting on a foam roller.
Rotate your leg so the roller rests against your inner thigh. Shift as much body weight onto the roller as you can tolerate.
While trying to relax your inner thigh muscles, roll from your hip to your knee, pausing on tender spots for 10–30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.
Adductor_Groin: Lie on your back with your legs extended toward the ceiling.
