Have a partner hold your feet or ankles. Spread your legs as wide as possible. This is your starting position.
Try to pull your legs together for 10 seconds or longer while your partner resists the movement.
Then relax your leg muscles as your partner gently pushes your feet apart to a comfortable stretch. Let them know when it is enough to avoid overstretching and injury.
Ankle_Circles: Hold onto a sturdy support, such as a power rack.
Lift your right foot about 2 inches (5 cm) off the floor and make circles with your big toe, as if drawing a large circle.
Once you finish with your right foot, repeat with your left.
Tip: one full circle counts as one rep. Breathe naturally.
Ankle_On_The_Knee: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place the ankle of one leg onto the opposite knee.
Grasp the thigh or knee of the bottom leg and pull both legs toward your chest. Relax your neck and shoulders. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Anterior_Tibialis-SMR: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Use a hand-held massage roller or rolling pin to apply pressure to the muscles along the outside of your shin.
Roll from just below the knee down to the ankle, holding on tender spots for 10–30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.
Arm_Circles: Stand tall and extend your arms out to the sides parallel to the floor, at a 90-degree angle to your torso. This is your starting position.
Slowly trace circles with your outstretched arms, about 1 foot (30 cm) in diameter. Breathe naturally.
Continue the circular motion for about 10 seconds, then switch directions.
Bicycling: Adjust the seat height to fit your height.
Brachialis-SMR: Lie on your side with your upper arm resting on a foam roller. Keep your arm roughly in line with your body, with the outer side of your bicep pressed against the roller.
Lift your hips off the floor, supporting yourself with your arm and feet. Hold for 10–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Calf_Stretch_Elbows_Against_Wall: Stand facing a wall, about 2 feet (60 cm) away from it.
Lean toward the wall, resting your weight on your forearms.
Try to keep your heels flat on the floor. Hold for 10–20 seconds. Step further back to increase the stretch, or move closer to make it easier.
Calf_Stretch_Hands_Against_Wall: Stand facing a wall about 3 feet (1 meter) away. Step one foot forward.
Lean forward and place your palms against the wall, keeping your back heel, hips, and head in a straight line.
Try to keep your back heel flat on the floor. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Calves-SMR: Sit on the floor and place a foam roller under your lower leg. Cross your other leg on top or place your foot on the floor to support some of your weight. This is your starting position.
Place your hands on the floor beside or slightly behind you and lift your hips, shifting most of your weight onto your calf muscle.
Roll from below the knee down to the ankle, holding on tender spots for 10–30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.
Carioca_Quick_Step: Stand with your feet a few inches apart, left arm raised, in a relaxed athletic stance.
Quickly step your right foot behind your left and drive your knee upward.
As you drive your right knee up, pump your arms dynamically; keep your knee moving strictly up and down. Keep your feet pointing forward and look ahead while moving laterally.
Chain_Handle_Extension: You will need two cable handles, a flat bench, and chains. Attach the middle of the chains to the handles and lie on the bench with your elbows pointing up.
Extend your arms at the elbows without moving your upper arms, using an overhand grip.
Pause at full extension, then return to the starting position.
Chair_Leg_Extended_Stretch: Sit up straight on a chair and hold onto the edges of the seat.
Lift one leg, straightening your knee while pulling your toes toward you.
Slowly move that leg out to the side as far as comfortable, then return it to the center and lower it.
Chair_Lower_Back_Stretch: Sit up straight on a chair.
Lean to the side, reaching your arm overhead. You can hold onto the chair with your free hand.
Hold for 10 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Chair_Upper_Body_Stretch: Sit on the edge of the chair and hold onto the backrest.
Straighten your arms, keep your back straight, and lean your upper body forward until you feel a stretch. Hold for 20–30 seconds.
Chest_And_Front_Of_Shoulder_Stretch: Stand with your feet together, holding a gymnastics stick or a broom handle.
Grip the stick slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing down, and hold it in front of you.
Gently raise the stick overhead and bring it behind your back.
Chest_Stretch_on_Stability_Ball: Get on all fours next to a stability ball.
Place your elbow on the ball with your arm out to the side. This is your starting position.
Lower your torso toward the floor, keeping your elbow on the ball. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds and repeat on the other arm.
Childs_Pose: Get on all fours and walk your hands forward.
Lower your hips toward your heels. As you push your hips back, slide your hands forward along the floor to stretch your entire spine.
Once sitting on your heels, rest your arms alongside your feet and relax. Breathe into your back and rest your forehead on the floor.
Caution: avoid this stretch if you have knee issues.
Chin_To_Chest_Stretch: Interlace your fingers behind your head with your thumbs pointing down and elbows pointing straight forward.
Slowly pull your chin toward your chest. Hold for 20–30 seconds.
Crossover_Reverse_Lunge: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Perform a reverse lunge by stepping one leg back, bending your hips and front knee. At the same time, rotate your torso toward your front leg.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, alternating legs.
Crucifix: The goal is to statically hold weights out to the sides for time. You can train with dumbbells, but special implements (like axes or hammers) work best because the feel is different.
Stand tall and raise your arms with the weights straight out to the sides, parallel to the floor. In competitions, judges or sensors track when your arms drop below parallel.
Hold for as long as you can. Typically, pick a weight that allows you to hold the position for 30–60 seconds.
Dancers_Stretch: Cross your right leg over your left with the right knee bent. Keep your left leg straight on the floor.
Place your left hand on your right leg and your right palm on the floor.
Twist your upper body to the right and hold for 10–20 seconds. Switch sides.
Dynamic_Back_Stretch: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Swing your straight arms forward and up 5–10 times, increasing the range of motion with each rep until your arms reach overhead.
Dynamic_Chest_Stretch: Stand with your arms extended straight in front of you, palms together. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, quickly swing them back as far as possible, then bring them back together in an exaggerated clapping motion.
Repeat 5–10 times, gradually picking up the pace.
Elbow_Circles: Sit or stand with your feet slightly apart.
Place your palms on your shoulders, keeping your elbows at shoulder level and pointed out to the sides.
Slowly draw circles with your elbows. Exhale at the start of each circle and inhale at the end.
Elbows_Back: Place both palms on your lower back with your fingers pointing down and elbows out to the sides.
Gently draw your elbows back, trying to bring them together.
Foot-SMR: This exercise stretches the plantar fascia. Sit down and take off your shoes.
Place the arch of your foot across a foot roller or a similar object, such as a piece of plastic pipe. This is your starting position.
Apply firm pressure and roll the arch of your foot over the roller. Hold on tender spots for 10–30 seconds, then switch feet.
Hamstring-SMR: Sit down and place a foam roller under your hamstrings. Place your hands on the floor beside or behind you for support. This is your starting position.
Pressing into your hands, lift your hips off the floor and shift your weight onto the roller with one leg. Relax the hamstring of that leg.
Roll from your glutes to just above your knee, pausing on tender spots for 10–30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.
Hamstring_Stretch: Lie on your back, extend one leg up at a 90-degree angle at the hip, and keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a strap, band, or rope around the ball of your foot. This is your starting position.
Pull the strap to feel a stretch in your calf and hamstring. Hold for 10–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Hug_A_Ball: Straddle an exercise ball with your legs and lower your hips toward the floor.
Wrap your arms around the ball for support. Place your feet flat on the floor with your knees stacked above your ankles.
Hold the ball firmly so it does not roll away and you do not fall backward onto your glutes.
Hug_Knees_To_Chest: Lie on your back and bring both knees toward your chest.
Wrap your hands around your legs just behind your knees rather than over them to avoid excessive pressure on the knee joints.
Slowly draw your knees toward your shoulders. This also stretches your glutes.
IT_Band_and_Glute_Stretch: Lie on your back, loop a strap, rope, or band around one foot, and bring that straight leg across your body toward the opposite side. This is your starting position.
Keeping your foot off the floor, pull the strap to angle your toes upward with tension. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Iliotibial_Tract-SMR: Lie on your side with the bottom leg on a foam roller between your hip and knee. You can cross your top leg over in front for support.
Place as much weight on the bottom leg as you can tolerate; it does not need to touch the floor. Relax the muscles of the leg being worked.
Roll your leg along the roller from your hip to your knee, pausing on tender spots for 10–30 seconds. Repeat on the other side.
Intermediate_Groin_Stretch: Lie on your back with your legs straight. Loop a strap, rope, or band around one foot and move that leg out to the side as far as comfortable. This is your starting position.
Gently pull the strap to create a stretch in your groin and hamstring. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Knee_Across_The_Body: Lie on your back with your right leg straight. Bend your left leg and bring it across your body, gently pressing the knee toward the floor with your right hand.
If your flexibility is limited, your knee does not need to touch the floor.
Rest your left arm comfortably out to the side and turn your head to the left.
Imagine a weight attached to your tailbone: let your tailbone sink toward the floor while reaching your chest in the opposite direction to stretch your lower back. Switch sides.
Kneeling_Arm_Drill: This exercise improves running arm mechanics. Kneel on your right knee with your left foot forward. Press your front heel into the floor, engaging your glutes and hamstrings.
Start with long swinging arm motions, like a pendulum. Then reduce the bend in your elbows and pump your arms as if jogging lightly, progressing to a run and then a sprint.
As your hands pass your hips, drive them forward forcefully as you would in a sprint, moving your arms as fast as possible.
Kneeling_Forearm_Stretch: Kneel on a mat with your palms flat on the floor, fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Slowly lean back while keeping your palms flat on the floor until you feel a stretch in your wrists and forearms. Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Kneeling_Hip_Flexor: Kneel on a mat. Step your right leg forward with your foot flat on the floor, and extend your left leg back with the top of your foot on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Latissimus_Dorsi-SMR: Lie on the floor and place a foam roller under your side, just below your armpit. This is your starting position.
Reach the arm on the stretched side back and out to the side, shifting your weight onto your lats without letting your upper body touch the floor.
Hold for 10-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Leg-Up_Hamstring_Stretch: Lie on your back, bend one knee, and place your foot flat on the floor to stabilize your spine.
Raise your other leg up. If your muscles are tight, it's completely normal if you can't fully straighten it.
Extend your knee so the sole of your foot points toward the ceiling (or as close as you comfortably can).
Slowly straighten your legs as much as possible, then gently pull the raised leg toward your nose. Switch sides.
Looking_At_Ceiling: Kneel down and reach back to grasp both heels with your hands.
Push your hips up and forward while tilting your head back and looking toward the ceiling to arch your back.
Lower_Back-SMR: Sit down and place a foam roller under your lower back. Cross your arms over your chest and round your shoulders forward. This is your starting position.
Lift your hips off the floor and lean back, shifting your weight onto your lower back.
Tilt slightly to one side so your weight rests on the muscles beside your spine rather than directly on the spine itself.
Roll along your lower back, pausing on tender spots for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other side.
Middle_Back_Stretch: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands on your hips.
Twist at your waist until you feel a stretch. Hold for 10-15 seconds, then twist to the other side.
Neck-SMR: Place a handheld massage roller or a rolling pin against the back of your neck.
Do not press directly on your spine: angle the roller slightly so it presses into the muscles along the side of your neck. This is your starting position.
Starting from the upper neck, slowly roll down along the neck muscles, pausing on tender spots for 10-30 seconds.
On-Your-Back_Quad_Stretch: Lie on a flat bench or step platform with one arm and leg hanging off the edge.
Bend your knee and grasp the top of your foot. Make sure not to arch your lower back.
Draw your belly button toward your spine to maintain a neutral position. Press your foot down into your hand. To stretch the hip as well, lift the hip on that side toward the ceiling.
On_Your_Side_Quad_Stretch: Lie on your right side with your right knee bent at 90 degrees on the floor in front of you to stabilize your torso.
Bend your left knee back and grasp your left foot with your left hand.
To stretch your hip flexors, push the left side of your pelvis forward while pressing your left foot back into your hand. Switch sides.
One_Arm_Against_Wall: Stand and place a bent arm against a wall or doorframe.
Slowly lean in toward your arm until you feel a stretch in your lats.
One_Half_Locust: Lie face down on your stomach.
Slide your left hand under your left hip bone to cushion your pelvis and pubic bone.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right foot with your right hand.
Lift your foot upward while lifting your shoulders off the floor. This stretches your right hip flexor, chest, and shoulders. Switch sides.
Variation: If your back feels fine, try doing this with both arms and legs at the same time.
Seated_Calf_Stretch: Sit up tall on a mat.
Bend one knee and place your foot flat on the floor to stabilize your torso.
Extend the other leg straight and flex your foot, pulling your toes toward you.
Use a resistance band, towel, or your hand (if you can reach) to pull your toes toward you. Hold for 10-20 seconds, then switch sides.
Seated_Floor_Hamstring_Stretch: Sit on a mat with your right leg extended forward and your left leg bent, resting the sole of your foot against your inner right thigh.
Hinge forward at your hips and reach toward your ankle until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Seated_Hamstring_and_Calf_Stretch: Loop a strap, rope, or resistance band around one foot. Sit upright with both legs extended straight. This is your starting position.
Hinge slightly forward and pull on the strap to draw your toes toward you. Hold for 10-20 seconds, then repeat with the other leg.
Seated_Overhead_Stretch: Sit up tall on a mat.
Bring the soles of your feet together, placing them 6-8 inches (15-20 cm) in front of your pelvis.
Place one hand on the floor next to you and bring the other hand behind your head.
Lift your elbow toward the ceiling as you lean your torso to the opposite side. Hold for 10-20 seconds, then switch sides.
Shoulder_Circles: Relax your shoulders and let your arms hang freely at your sides (or rest them on your knees if seated).
Gently roll your shoulders forward, up, back, and down.
Reverse the direction. You can roll your shoulders alternately or both at the same time.
Shoulder_Raise: Relax your arms and let them hang by your sides.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, then lower them back down.
Shoulder_Stretch: Bring your left arm across your chest.
Side-Lying_Floor_Stretch: Lie on your left side with your left knee bent in front of you to stabilize your torso (engage your core to help hold the position).
Straighten your right leg and place your right foot on the floor behind your left foot.
Reach your right arm overhead and gently pull on your right wrist, stretching along the entire right side of your body. Switch sides.
Side_Lying_Groin_Stretch: Lie on your right side and bend your right knee in front of you to stabilize your torso.
Rest your head on your right arm or shoulder. Lift your left leg and hold it behind the knee (easier) or by the foot (more challenging).
Pull your left knee toward your left shoulder while pressing your foot or knee toward the floor. To intensify the stretch, straighten your left leg. Switch sides.
Side_Neck_Stretch: Relax your shoulders and gently tilt your head toward your shoulder.
Deepen the stretch by gently applying light pressure to the side of your head with your hand.
Side_Wrist_Pull: This stretch is best performed standing. Bring your left arm across the midline of your body and grasp your left wrist with your right hand at hip height. Keep your left arm bent.
Slowly straighten your arm, pulling and lifting it up to shoulder height.
You should feel the stretch in your back rather than your shoulders; avoid pulling too hard on the shoulder joint. Switch sides.
Single-Cone_Sprint_Drill: This exercise develops fast footwork. You will need one cone. Stand next to it with one arm back and the other forward.
Pump your feet as fast as possible while driving your arms. Circle around the cone with high knees and quick, sharp foot movements.
Rest after completing three laps around the cone.
The_Straddle: Sit up straight and spread your straight legs out in front of you in a wide V-shape.
Place your hands on the floor and lean forward as far as you comfortably can. Hold for 10–20 seconds.
Torso_Rotation: Stand tall, holding an exercise ball with both hands. Extend your arms so the ball is directly in front of you. This is your starting position.
Rotate your torso to one side, following the ball with your eyes. Then smoothly rotate all the way to the opposite side.
Trail_Running_Walking: Trail running or walking instantly gets your blood pumping and raises your heart rate. Make sure to wear supportive footwear.
Uphill sections work your calves and glutes, while descents place more impact on your knees, joints, and ankles.
Take shorter steps on the way down, keep your knees slightly bent to absorb impact, and slow your pace to stay balanced.
A 68 kg person burns over 200 kcal in 30 min of uphill walking (compared to 175 kcal on flat ground), and well over 500 kcal when running on trails.
Tricep_Side_Stretch: Bring your right arm across your body above your left shoulder, using your left hand to support your right elbow.
Gently pull until you feel a stretch in your triceps. Then switch arms and repeat.
Triceps_Stretch: Reach one arm behind your head, hold your elbow with the opposite hand, and gently pull.
Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Upper_Back-Leg_Grab: Sit on the floor, lean forward, and wrap both arms underneath your thighs.
Keep your knees together and legs extended forward, lowering your chest toward your knees.
To also stretch your mid-back, pull your back away from your knees while keeping your arms clasped around your legs.
Upper_Back_Stretch: Interlace your fingers with your thumbs pointing down.
Reach your arms forward, rounding your shoulders and upper back.
Upward_Stretch: Reach both arms directly overhead with your palms pressed together.
Slowly stretch your hands upward and slightly back, keeping your back straight.
Windmills: Lie on your back with your arms out to the sides and legs straight. This is your starting position.
Raise one leg and quickly sweep it across your body, aiming to touch the floor near your opposite hand.
Return to the starting position and repeat with the other leg. Alternate legs for 10–20 reps.
Worlds_Greatest_Stretch: This is a three-part stretch. Step forward into a lunge with your front foot flat on the floor and your back foot on its toes. Bend your knees to lower down until your back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and hold for 10–20 seconds.
Place the hand on the side of your front leg onto the floor, bringing your elbow next to your foot. Place your other hand flat on the floor parallel to your front leg for balance.
After 10–20 seconds, place both hands on the floor on either side of your front foot. Lift your front toes off the floor and straighten that leg; you may adjust your back foot if needed.
Hold for 10–20 seconds, then repeat the entire sequence on the other side.
Atlas_Stones: Stand with the stone centered between your feet. Hinge at your hips and wrap your arms around the stone, getting your fingers underneath it (flat spots on some stones make this easier).
Hug the stone tight against your body, drive through your heels into the floor, and pull it off the ground.
Once the stone clears your knees, sit back into a deep squat and roll it onto your thighs.
Staying low, hoist the stone high onto your chest and re-wrap your arms over the top. Stand up tall by powerfully extending your hips.
Step close to the platform and lean back, extending your hips to lift the stone as high as possible and place it on top.
Circus_Bell: A circus dumbbell is an oversized dumbbell with a thick handle. Place it between your feet and grip the handle with both hands.
Clean the bell to your shoulder by powerfully extending your hips and knees, then release your assisting hand.
Tuck one end of the dumbbell behind your shoulder to maintain stability and balance.
To press overhead, dip slightly by bending your knees, then drive the dumbbell explosively upward, leaning slightly away from it.
Carefully lower the dumbbell back to the floor with full control. It is best to do this on thick rubber gym flooring to protect the surface.
Behind_Head_Chest_Stretch: Sit upright on the floor with your partner positioned behind you.
Place your hands behind your head and pull your elbows back as far as comfortable. Have your partner hold your elbows. This is your starting position.
Gently try to bring your elbows forward without taking your hands off your head for 10 seconds or longer, while your partner resists the movement.
Then relax your muscles as your partner gently pulls your elbows back to a comfortable stretch. Tell them when to stop to avoid overstretching and injury.
Lying_Bent_Leg_Groin: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of your feet pressed together. Have your partner hold your knees. This is your starting position.
Try to bring your knees together while your partner resists the movement.
After 10–20 seconds, relax your muscles as your partner gently presses your knees toward the floor. Tell them when to stop to prevent injury or overstretching.
Lying_Hamstring: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your partner kneeling beside you. Raise one leg toward the ceiling; have your partner hold your ankle and support it with their shoulder if needed. This is your starting position.
While your partner holds your leg in place, try to bend your knee by contracting your hamstrings for 10–20 seconds.
Then relax your leg as your partner gently pushes it toward your head. Tell them when to stop to prevent injury or overstretching.
Overhead_Lat: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm overhead and bend your elbow, reaching your palm toward your upper back.
Have your partner hold your triceps and wrist. This is your starting position.
Try to pull your upper arm down toward your side while your partner resists the movement.
After 10–20 seconds, relax your arm as your partner gently presses on your triceps to deepen the lat stretch. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Seated_Hamstring: Sit with your legs straight and your partner standing behind you. Lean forward from your hips, and have your partner place their palms on your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Try to push your torso back up for 10–20 seconds while your partner resists the movement.
Then relax your muscles as your partner gently pushes your torso forward for 10–20 seconds to deepen the stretch.
Sit_Squats: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. This is your starting position.
Begin the movement by bending your knees and hips, sending your hips back.
Lower yourself partially, staying above parallel, and quickly return to the starting position. Complete 5–10 reps.
Skating: Roller skating is a fun activity that builds cardiovascular, respiratory, and muscular endurance. It requires decent balance and coordination.
Master the basics, including turning and stopping. Wear protective gear to prevent injuries.
Skate at a comfortable pace for 30 min without stopping. For a cardio boost, use intervals: skate fast for two minutes out of every five, then recover for three.
A person weighing 68 kg typically burns about 175 kcal in 30 min of skating at a comfortable pace—similar to brisk walking.
Spinal_Stretch: Sit on a chair with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows out to the sides, chin tucked down.
Rotate your upper body as far as possible to one side about 3 times. Then lean forward and, twisting your torso, reach your elbow toward the floor inside your knee.
Return to the upright position and repeat on the other side.
Standing_Biceps_Stretch: Clasp your hands behind your back, palms together, straighten your arms, and turn your palms downward.
Raise your arms upward until you feel a stretch in your biceps, and hold.
Standing_Elevated_Quad_Stretch: Stand with your back to a bench or step platform at a distance of 60–90 cm.
Reach one leg back and place your foot on the elevated surface, resting on the top of the foot or the ball—whichever is more comfortable.
Keep your standing knee slightly bent. Switch sides.
Standing_Gastrocnemius_Calf_Stretch: Place your right heel on a step platform with your knee straight, hinge forward, and hold your toes with your right hand. Keep your left knee slightly bent and back straight.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and rest your left hand on your left thigh.
Pull your right toes toward your knee until you feel a stretch in your calf.
Standing_Hamstring_and_Calf_Stretch: Loop a strap, band, or rope around one foot. While standing, step that foot forward.
Bend your back leg while keeping the front leg straight. Lift the toes of your front foot off the floor and hinge forward.
Pull on the strap against the top of your foot to deepen the stretch in your calf. Hold for 10–20 seconds and repeat on the other leg.
Standing_Hip_Flexors: Stand tall with your spine upright and your left foot slightly in front of your right.
Bend both knees and lift your back heel off the floor, pushing the right side of your pelvis forward.
You won't get a deep stretch here, as it's hard to relax the hip flexor while standing on that leg. Switch sides.
Standing_Lateral_Stretch: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Place your right hand on your right hip to support your spine.
Raise your left arm straight up and place your left hand behind your head. Keeping it there, bend your torso to the right.
Distribute your weight evenly between both legs without shifting into your left hip. Switch sides.
Standing_Pelvic_Tilt: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly so they stay soft and springy.
You can tilt your pelvis back and forth a few times before holding it with your tailbone tucked forward.
Standing_Soleus_And_Achilles_Stretch: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, one foot slightly ahead of the other.
Bend both knees while keeping your back heel on the floor. Switch sides.
Standing_Toe_Touches: Stand with clear space in front of and behind you.
Hinge at the waist with your legs straight until you can relax and let your upper body hang loosely downward.
Let your arms hang freely. Hold for 10–20 seconds.
One_Handed_Hang: Grip a pull-up bar with one hand using an overhand grip. Keep your feet on the floor or on a platform.
Shift most of your weight onto that arm without lifting your feet off the support. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch arms.
Peroneals-SMR: Lie on your side, propping yourself up on your forearm with a foam roller placed under the outer side of your lower leg. Stack your top leg or cross it in front. This is your starting position.
Lift your hips off the floor and roll along the outer calf from your knee to your ankle, pausing on tender spots for 10–30 seconds.
Peroneals_Stretch: Sit down and loop a strap, rope, or resistance band around one foot. This is your starting position.
Straighten your leg with your heel off the floor, and pull the strap so the inner edge of your foot turns toward you. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Piriformis-SMR: Sit with your glutes on a foam roller. Bend your knees and cross one ankle over the opposite knee. This is your starting position.
Shift your weight toward the side of the crossed leg and roll across the glute until you feel tension in its upper part.
To deepen the stretch, gently pull the bent knee toward your chest with one hand. Hold for 10–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Posterior_Tibialis_Stretch: Sit down and loop a strap, rope, or resistance band around one foot. This is your starting position.
Straighten your leg with your heel off the floor, and pull the strap so the outer edge of your foot turns toward you. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Pyramid: Roll forward over an exercise ball so your hips rest on top of the ball, becoming the highest point of your body.
Place your hands and feet on the floor. Keep your arms and legs straight or slightly bent, depending on ball size, flexibility, and limb length.
This exercise also develops core and shoulder stability.
Quad_Stretch: Lie on your side. Loop a strap, rope, or resistance band around the foot of your top leg.
Bend your knee and bring your thigh back, aiming to bring your heel toward your glutes while holding the strap. This is your starting position.
Holding the strap over your shoulder or overhead, gently pull it to deepen the quad stretch. Hold for 10–20 seconds, then switch sides.
Quadriceps-SMR: Lie face down, propping yourself up on your hands or forearms. Place a foam roller under the quad of one leg with your foot off the floor.
Relax your leg as much as possible. This is your starting position.
Placing as much weight onto this leg as you can tolerate, roll from your knee to your hip, pausing on tender spots for 10–30 seconds. Switch sides.
Rhomboids-SMR: Lie on your back with a foam roller under your upper back. Cross your arms over your chest, drawing your shoulders forward. This is your starting position.
Lift your hips off the floor, shifting your weight onto the roller.
Shifting your weight from side to side, roll along your mid and upper back. Pause on tender spots for 10–30 seconds.
Rope_Jumping: Hold the ends of the jump rope in each hand with the rope resting on the floor behind you.
Swing the rope up and over your head. As it reaches the floor, jump over it.
Find a comfortable rhythm you can maintain. Vary your speed and technique to keep things challenging.
Jumping rope improves coordination and burns plenty of energy: a 68 kg person burns about 350 kcal in 30 min (and over 450 kcal running).
Round_The_World_Shoulder_Stretch: Stand up straight with your feet together, holding a dowel or a broomstick.
Hold the stick behind your hips with a wider-than-shoulder-width grip, palms facing down and thumbs pointing out.
Slowly raise your arms up behind your head. If it feels too difficult to go further, do not force it.
Runners_Stretch: The easiest way to enter this stretch is from standing: step one foot back and slowly lower your torso toward the floor.
Keep your front heel on the floor (if it lifts, step your back foot further away).
Place your hands on the floor on either side of your front foot. For a deeper stretch, lift your hips toward the ceiling, then smoothly lower them back down.
This stretches the hip flexor of your back leg, as well as the hamstring and glute of your front leg.
